provenance: Composes with `test-fixtures-mirror-production-failure-modes` (the sterile-fixture inverse) and `reward-hacking`. See the `faked-uat-theatre` and `mock-uat-seam` artifacts. Imported from v1 `assets/guidelines/implementer-shortcut-patterns.yml`.

title: Pull-based context architecture
description: Brief an agent thinly and let it pull fresh context just-in-time, rather than pushing a fat static brief at session start.
statement: Give an agent a thin bootstrap and let it pull exactly the context its current step needs — minimal initial load, fetched on demand, always read from the live source — rather than pushing a large static brief at session start.
problem: The push model — pre-loading a big static brief covering every situation the agent might hit — pays three costs every turn: a context tax (a large brief consumes the attention budget even when most is irrelevant), staleness (a brief loaded at session start does not reflect later changes; the agent reasons over a snapshot), and one-size-fits-all (every step gets the whole brief; no step gets context tailored to it).
approach: Thin bootstrap — the starting brief carries the agent’s role, current objective, and how to fetch more; pointers, not payloads. Pull on demand — the agent fetches operational context when it needs it, and what it fetches is paths to read, not embedded blobs, always reading current state. Progressive disclosure — each step’s result points at the next thing to fetch. Keep briefs lean: name the surface and link its authoritative source instead of inlining it (self-contained means complete pointers, not complete payloads). When a single context to pull would still exceed the window, escalate to recursive decomposition. The CLI is one such pull surface: it renders its doctrine prose from the Library on demand — the choose-your-own-adventure CLI (ADR-0023/ADR-0053) — instead of carrying a fat static brief, because static instruction is followed less reliably than context pulled at the step that needs it.
tradeoffs: You trade a guaranteed-complete upfront snapshot for freshness and a small initial load; the agent makes extra fetches, but each reads live state instead of a stale cache. In storytree the event store is the single source of truth and the orchestrator briefs each node — this argues for those briefs to be pointers into live state, not fat snapshots.
provenance: A context-engineering principle for how agents are briefed, not a code spec for any subsystem. Composes with `signal-and-noise` (at the briefing layer) and `recursive-decomposition-patterns`. See ADR-0011 (pull-based just-in-time context). Imported from legacy AgenticEngineering `AgenticGuidance`.

title: Recursive decomposition patterns
description: When a context genuinely exceeds the model window, hold it as a queryable environment, filter to the sparse relevant slice, and recurse with bounded depth — do not summarise lossily.
statement: When a context genuinely exceeds the model's window, decompose rather than summarise lossily or hope a bigger window saves you: hold the large context as an environment the agent queries programmatically, filter to the sparse relevant slice, and recurse with bounded depth.
problem: Most tasks do not need all of a large context at once. Loading everything wastes the attention budget and degrades reasoning; summarising upfront loses the details the task needs. The alternative is to treat the context as data the agent searches — loading only the slice each sub-step requires — so it can work over a corpus far larger than its window without lossy compression. Reserve this for contexts that actually exceed the limit; for anything that fits, plain loading is simpler and faster.
approach: Context as environment — store the large input as named, queryable state and issue queries (filter for a pattern, navigate a section, find usages) pulling only what each step needs. Filter over chunk — prefer extracting the semantically relevant slice over blind size-based splitting. Recursive decomposition — break into sub-tasks, process each over its own slice, accumulate, aggregate (filter-then-process, hierarchical extraction, map-reduce). Search/execution firewall — separate context curation from task execution; a curation pass prepares the minimal slice, an execution pass works with only that slice and does no further searching. Discipline: measure before activating; bound and decrement a max depth; name the accumulators; hold the firewall; aggregate before signalling completion.
tradeoffs: You trade setup overhead and orchestration complexity for the ability to reason over an oversized corpus without lossy compression; not worth it when the context fits comfortably. Natural homes in storytree: oversized exploration, large owned-loop-event-stream or evidence analysis, and reasoning over big spec inputs during decomposition.
provenance: Source: Recursive Language Models (Zhang/Kraska/Khattab, MIT CSAIL); a context-engineering principle, not a code spec. Composes with `exploration-principles` and `pull-based-context-architecture`. Imported from legacy AgenticEngineering `AgenticGuidance`.

title: Repo surface allow-list
description: The repo root and docs/ are allow-listed: a new root entry or a new standalone doc is refused unless added to repo-manifest.json — and a new doc must justify why it does not belong in the Library.
statement: New files at the repo root, and new standalone docs under docs/, are refused at the gate unless listed in repo-manifest.json — and a new doc’s entry must state why it does not belong in the Library.
rule: The set of tracked top-level root entries and loose docs/ files must equal the allow-list in repo-manifest.json. Durable project knowledge belongs in the Library — as a typed artifact of one of its schema-validated kinds (see the `library` definition; `KIND_SPECS` in `packages/library/src/knowledge.ts` is the authoritative kind table) — or in an ADR under docs/decisions/, not a loose prose doc; the only standalone narrative doc kept is README.md. ADRs (docs/decisions/) and research notes (docs/research/) are allow-listed at the directory level, so new ADRs need no entry; any other file directly under docs/ needs an explicit, justified manifest entry.
enforcedBy: scripts/check-manifest.mjs (`pnpm check:manifest`), run inside `pnpm gate` and the CI `verify` job before typecheck (ADR-0022). It reads `git ls-files` and exits non-zero on any unlisted root entry or unlisted/unjustified doc, so an offending change cannot pass the green gate that guards merge to `main`.
failureMode: Without it, agents accrete temp/ad-hoc files at the root and one-off prose docs under docs/ that duplicate or bypass the Library — splitting authority over durable knowledge, rotting the tree, and re-creating the doc-sprawl the Library was meant to replace.
provenance: Authoritatively defined by ADR-0025; enforces on the ADR-0022 dev-repo green gate. The repo-hygiene complement to `edit-first-curation` (search/edit before authoring) and `signal-and-noise` (cut low-signal docs). Distinct from the PRODUCT proof gate (`gate` / `never-bypass-the-gate` / `prove-it-gate`): same "a gate refuses, it does not warn" family, but this guards the dev repo’s git surface, not promotion onto the story DAG. Mechanism: `repo-manifest.json` + `scripts/check-manifest.mjs`.

steps:
1. **Explore offline.** `pnpm storytree library` (the dashboard) is the first command when working with the Library; drill in with `pnpm storytree library artifact <id>`, `pnpm storytree library artifact list <category>`, and `pnpm storytree library tree focus <id>`. Reads run against the in-memory seed — no DB needed.
2. **Search before you write** (asset:edit-first-curation). Real search is deferred (ADR-0023 §6) — `artifact list <category>` is the interim discovery path. Find the closest existing artifact and edit it by default; reaching for `artifact new` must be justified by why editing wasn't right. `new` refuses an existing id and points at `edit`.
3. **Bring the DB up:** `pnpm db:up`. The instance sleeps on a fixed nightly window (01:00–07:00 Australia/Sydney, ADR-0114) and otherwise stays up across the day; `db:up` is a no-op if already up.
4. **Write through the CLI with `--pg`:** `pnpm storytree library artifact edit <id> --set <field>=<value> --pg`, or `pnpm storytree library artifact new --file <doc.json> --pg`. Writes are **refused without `--pg`**; every write re-validates at the boundary (`validateLibraryDoc`) and returns a failure as guidance rather than persisting. **Editing an EXISTING DURABLE-TIER artifact? Edit BOTH surfaces**: the live store (for a multi-field edit, push the whole doc — `artifact edit <id> --file <doc.json> --pg` upcast-validates and replaces wholesale) AND the seed `apps/studio/data/knowledge.json` (every offline read comes from it) — or make the live edit and discharge it with `storytree library export-corpus --pg --write`, which writes the seed for you. The durable tier is the `SEED_SCOPE_KINDS` allowlist (ADR-0263): definition, principle, pattern, guardrail, techstack, process, open-question, proposal. **Everything else is out of seed scope and costs nothing** — a `friction`, `arc`, `uat-criterion`, or `plan` edit is live-only by decision (ADR-0263 / ADR-0183 D2), so it needs no seed edit and creates no drift. `sync-corpus` is **migrate-only** — it adds seed-only artifacts to live but never updates one that already exists live — so a one-sided durable-tier edit silently drifts. `check:corpus-content` is what catches that drift, and **its axes all sit at ZERO** — authored value-drift 0, degraded-live 0, authored live-only 0, each redding on its own and never summed (ADR-0252 D3 in ADR-0168 D4's shape; `packages/cli/src/corpus-content-drain.ts` holds the live numbers and is the only place they are stated). There is no headroom left: **the FIRST unreconciled durable-tier artifact THIS BRANCH AUTHORED reds the gate.** Since ADR-0290 it is scoped by authorship rather than charged to whoever gates next — the check reads your seed diff against the merge base and the latest live writer per artifact (live writes now stamp `cli@<branch>`), and prints everything else as `BEHIND MAIN` (remedy: `git merge origin/main`) or `ANOTHER WRITER` (named, with its writer — not yours to reconcile). So reconcile YOUR edit in the same pass — the discharge is one command scoped to one artifact, `export-corpus --id <id> --pg --write`, which the check prints for you verbatim. **But DRY-RUN before you `--write`, and never read a green `check:corpus-content` as evidence that the export is a no-op** — the two do not measure the same population. `diffCorpusContent` iterates the SEED scope and skips any id live carries but the seed does not (`const l = liveById.get(s.id); if (!l) continue;`), so a LIVE-ONLY artifact is invisible to the check on both axes; `computeExportedSeed` loops over ALL live docs and APPENDS every live-only export-scope one. The export therefore writes a strict SUPERSET of what the check names. Measured 2026-07-30: `check:corpus-content` printed `OK — every seed body matches live across 177 export-scope artifacts` and exited 0 while `export-corpus --pg` (no `--write`) in the same shell reported `0 update(s) + 1 addition(s)`. So run `export-corpus --pg` first, read the `added (live-only)` list, and make the per-artifact direction call on every id you did not author — the failure modes below give the two opposite causes and why one of them makes a blind `--write` destructive.
5. **Mind the `--json` trap:** `pnpm` swallows the `--json` flag (it is reserved by pnpm). Pass a doc via `--file`, or use inline `--json` only via `npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts …`.
6. **If a write can't connect,** the DB is likely in its overnight sleep window (or a slow cold-start) — re-run `pnpm db:up` (works any time inside the window) and retry.
7. **Keep sessions off the same artifact.** Different artifacts never contend (per-id rows, transactional upserts); the **same** artifact across two sessions is not coordinated — claims are DBOS-deferred — so don't co-edit one artifact in parallel.
title: Library edit ceremony
trigger: A session needs to change Library state — edit an artifact's fields, author a new artifact, or RETIRE one — rather than merely read it. (Pure reads need no ceremony: they run offline against the in-memory seed. `artifact comment` is not yet a CLI surface; `artifact retire` IS — `storytree library artifact retire <id> --reason "…" [--superseded-by asset:<id>|doc:<path>] --pg`, a delete that folds `retiredReason`/`supersededBy` onto the append-only `deleted` event, and it HARD-REFUSES while any live artifact still cites `asset:<id>`. Retirement is also how an `open-question` is CLOSED: that kind carries no lifecycle field — `lifecycleOf('open-question', doc)` returns `open` unconditionally and the schema is `.strict()`, so there is no status to set and inventing one is refused at validation, per ADR-0267 D5.)
surfaces:
- **Library** — the only surface written. Each CLI write lands in the live Cloud SQL store as one event plus a transactional projection upsert; this store is the **live source of truth** for artifact state. Reads touch it only with `--pg`; offline reads come from the in-memory seed.
- **Repo** — read-only here. `apps/studio/data/knowledge.json` is the migration seed/export, and it is the ONLY committed view: the generated `assets.json` and its `build-corpus.mjs` generator were retired by ADR-0210, so nothing is regenerated after a seed write and there is no post-edit build step. The ceremony writes the seed only for a DURABLE-TIER artifact (the `SEED_SCOPE_KINDS` allowlist, ADR-0263) — via the step-4 dual edit or `export-corpus --pg --write`; an out-of-scope kind (`friction`, `arc`, `uat-criterion`, `plan`) has no seed row to write. A live-only durable-tier edit leaves the seed lagging until one of those reconciles it, and reds `check:corpus-content` immediately.
statement: A session changes Library state only through the CLI against the live Cloud SQL store — explore offline, search before writing, then `pnpm db:up` and write with `--pg` — never by hand-editing the seed or generated files.
provenance:
Derived (per ADR-0034) from ADR-0023 §10–11 and the CLAUDE.md library section; on any disagreement the cited ADRs win. The step-4 dual seed+live edit rule was graduated 2026-07-02 from agent-memory `artifact-authoring-traps` (ADR-0095); the idle-stop and no-DB→seed-export claims were corrected on the same pass against ADR-0114 (fixed nightly sleep window) and ADR-0120 (export-corpus). Corrected 2026-07-29 (ADR-0154 process-tier projection, ADR-0139 pass) against what ADR-0263 landed: the seed scope is now the durable-tier `SEED_SCOPE_KINDS` allowlist, not every non-agent kind, so the dual-edit duty is scoped to that tier and an out-of-scope kind (`friction` / `arc` / `uat-criterion` / `plan`) costs nothing; the `check:corpus-content` ceiling is stated as ZERO on both axes rather than 14, with the numbers left to `corpus-content-drain.ts` (reference-dont-restate); the retired `assets.json` / `build-corpus.mjs` generated view was removed from Surfaces per ADR-0210; and the all-or-nothing `--write` warning was retired as resolved by the narrowed scope. The direction-is-never-auto-inferred failure mode (the seed is sometimes the newer side; `degraded-live: 0` is not evidence live is right; MIXED is a real outcome needing a hand-merge BEFORE the export) was graduated on the same pass from agent-memory `live-to-seed-corpus-export` (ADR-0095 D4/D6), whose event-specific residue stays in git and the ADR.
 Corrected and extended 2026-07-30 (librarian-curator pre-merge pass, ADR-0095 D7): the Trigger claim that `retire` is not yet a CLI surface was STALE and is corrected in place — `artifact retire` ships, and ADR-0267 D5 decided it is how an `open-question` is closed, that kind having no lifecycle field to set. The retire-is-two-surface rule and the resurrection race were graduated on the same pass from agent-memory `closing-an-open-question-is-a-retire-not-a-status` (ADR-0095 D4/D6), whose durable half is the DISCRIMINATOR between a missed migration and a deliberate retire — two cases `check:corpus-sync` renders identically with opposite remedies — plus the event-log evidence that settles direction; the incident residue stays in git and in ADR-0267. Corrected again 2026-07-30 (librarian-curator pre-merge pass, ADR-0139 in-place correction, in an ADR-0168 D4/D5 board-drain session): the step-4 and failure-mode-2 claim that at a drained backlog `export-corpus --pg --write` "carries only the artifact you edited" was measured FALSE and is corrected in place. `diffCorpusContent` iterates the SEED scope and skips any id live carries but the seed does not, while `computeExportedSeed` appends every live-only export-scope doc — so the export writes a strict SUPERSET of what `check:corpus-content` can name, and the difference is a population the check is structurally blind to. Reproduced the same day: a GREEN check ("OK across 177 export-scope artifacts", exit 0) alongside an `export-corpus --pg` dry run reporting `0 update(s) + 1 addition(s)`. That addition was `oq-diff-view-altitude`, retired by owner direction under ADR-0267 D5 and found live for the FOURTH time (`events.library_event` seq 2742) — one blind `--write` from being resurrected into the committed seed, where it would have survived every future migration; this pass re-retired it live. A new failure mode records the blind spot and the two OPPOSITE causes of a live-only id. The identical false claim was corrected on the same pass in `packages/cli/src/corpus-content-drain.ts` and `CLAUDE.md`. The conclusion that header drew from the false premise — "a per-artifact export verb is therefore NOT needed and should not be built on this reasoning" — is WITHDRAWN rather than inverted: whether such a verb should exist is left open, and is not this correction's to settle.Extended 2026-08-01 (librarian-curator pre-merge pass, ADR-0095 D7): the authorship-differential failure mode was GRADUATED from agent-memory `corpus-content-red-may-not-be-yours` (ADR-0095 D4/D6 capture-then-delete — the source memory was deleted on this pass). EDIT-FIRST into this ceremony rather than a new `process` (asset:edit-first-curation): this artifact already owns the seed-versus-live direction call, and the gap was a consequence it stated but never drew. It already recorded that at a zero ceiling the FIRST unreconciled durable-tier artifact reds the gate "for every session and not just the one that made it" — yet it gave the session that FINDS the red no way to tell which of the two it is, while continuing to document `export-corpus --pg --write` as the discharge. On a shared gate those two facts compose into a real hazard: the finding session blind-writes, and every sibling's in-flight drift lands in its commit under its name. The pristine-HEAD differential is the missing instrument, and it is not reconstructible from the corpus — live is not in git, so no ordinary `git diff` can answer the authorship question, and the measurement only means anything against a seed checked out at HEAD. Evidence 2026-08-01: 3 artifacts drifted against the pristine HEAD seed versus 2 after the session's own change, so the red was pre-existing and that change had reduced it; and `audit-the-signed-verdict` entered the drift list between two `check:corpus-content` runs minutes apart under a concurrent session's live edit, which is why the rule is re-measure-then-act rather than act-on-the-list-you-have. The surgical single-field reconcile (locate, assert exactly-once, replace, re-parse) is the same round-trip discipline this artifact already prescribes for a seed retire removal, applied to a value edit. Event-specific residue stays in git. Consumers: any session whose `pnpm gate` reds on `check:corpus-content`, and the librarian-curator making the per-artifact direction call. Corrected 2026-08-02 (ADR-0139 in-place correction) for what ADR-0290 landed: `check:corpus-content` charges each seed↔live drift by AUTHORSHIP rather than to whoever gates next, so the claims that the first unreconciled artifact reds "every session, not just yours" and that a red cannot be told from a sibling's are no longer true and are corrected rather than deleted. The manual pristine-HEAD differential this artifact prescribed on 2026-08-01 is now the check's own work — it is replaced by the instruction to READ THE LABEL (`YOURS` / `BEHIND MAIN` / `ANOTHER WRITER`) and act on it, with the two things the mechanism does NOT do stated explicitly: it settles no direction, and it charges everything when a signal is unreadable. The all-or-nothing warning is narrowed rather than retired, because the bare form still behaves that way: ADR-0290 D6 adds `export-corpus --id <id>`, so the discharge for your own edit is one artifact wide. The evidence for all of it is in ADR-0290 and in `packages/cli/src/corpus-content-attribution.ts`; the per-artifact DIRECTION judgement (ADR-0120) is untouched. Extended 2026-08-03 (librarian-curator pre-merge pass, ADR-0095 D7): the CI-blast-radius clause was GRADUATED from agent-memory `corpus-content-gate`, which was otherwise REJECTED as redundant with this artifact (ADR-0095 D5) and re-parked under ADR-0202. EDIT-FIRST rather than a new `process` (asset:edit-first-curation): the memory restated this ceremony's ADR-0290 label rules (`YOURS` / `BEHIND MAIN` / `ANOTHER WRITER`), the scoped `--id` discharge and the dry-run trap almost clause for clause, and carried exactly one fact this artifact did not — so the gap sat INSIDE it, not beside it. WHAT WAS WRONG: this artifact said the `check:corpus-content` CI skip meant 'the cost is local-only'. True of the CHECK, false of the CONSEQUENCE, and the two were collapsed into one sentence. A blind export's output is the COMMITTED SEED, and the seed is read in CI by a different gate — `check:surface-coverage` runs at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, verified against the workflow file on this pass rather than taken from the memory, and it is seed-reading and DB-free precisely so it CAN run there. EVIDENCE: 2026-08-02, PR #1089 — an unscoped `export-corpus --pg --write` carried a sibling's live prose into the seed; that prose named the verb `storytree proposal`, which existed only on their unpushed branch, and CI went red on a surface the exporting session had never authored. The failure mode is NARROWED, not added to: ADR-0290's `--id` scoping makes it avoidable rather than impossible, so the clause is stated as a reason to scope rather than as a standing hazard, and the recovery (revert that one seed row, disclose in the PR, let their PR close it) is stated because the export is already committed by the time it reds. Nothing else in the artifact moved; the per-artifact DIRECTION judgement (ADR-0120) and the label rules are untouched. The SOURCE MEMORY IS NOT DELETED: its remaining content is a pointer index into this ceremony plus a spent chip id, which is operational navigation rather than an 'able' artifact (ADR-0095 D5/D8), so it stays in the memory trap index under a fresh ADR-0202 lease.
description: How a session writes Library state: explore offline, search first, then CLI writes with `--pg` against the live store — never by hand-editing the seed.
failureModes:
- **Hand-editing `knowledge.json` for a live change** — the edit is invisible to the live store, to parallel sessions, and to the studio; seed and DB silently diverge, and the next migration decides which version survives.
- **Running `load-corpus.ts --force` against a live DB carrying CLI edits** — the seed overwrites the live state and **reverts those edits**; recovery is the DB→seed export (`storytree library export-corpus --pg [--write]`, ADR-0120). The BARE `--write` is still all-or-nothing, and for a `--force` recovery that is exactly what you want. For anything else it is not: **"all" is not "the thing you changed"**, because the export also ADDS every live-only export-scope artifact on top. ADR-0263's narrowed scope shrank the UPDATE half to something a librarian can read per-artifact, and ADR-0290 removed the coupling entirely — `export-corpus --id <id> [--id …] --pg --write` writes only the ids you name, through the same single narrowing point, so a scoped run cannot diverge in policy from an unscoped one. Use the scoped form to discharge your own edit; if you use the bare form, a green check is no evidence the batch is empty, so dry-run first, every time.
- **One-sided edit of an existing durable-tier artifact** — editing only live leaves the seed (and every offline read) stale; editing only the seed is invisible to the live store and the studio. `sync-corpus` will not carry an update across (migrate-only), so the drift persists until someone reconciles by hand — and `check:corpus-content` no longer merely warns about it: with its ceiling at zero the FIRST such edit reds the gate — for the branch that MADE it, which since ADR-0290 is the branch the check charges rather than whoever gates next (ADR-0120's body-diff as bounded under ADR-0252 D3, re-apertured by ADR-0290).
- **Assuming the LIVE side is the canonical one, and letting the export decide direction for you** — it is not, and it cannot. `sync-corpus` is migrate-only, so a SEED edit to an already-live artifact can never propagate; the seed is therefore legitimately sometimes the newer, more correct side, and no mechanism will ever fix live on its own. Nor is `degraded-live: 0` evidence that live is right — that axis only rules out a body below the schema floor, and says nothing about content. Direction is a per-artifact judgement (ADR-0120), and **MIXED is a real outcome**: each side can hold facts the other dropped, so neither is a superset and no field copy works — the live body must be hand-merged BEFORE the export runs, or the export destroys the seed-only facts. Blanket-exporting without that judgement is the failure mode; spawn the `librarian-curator` with the per-artifact seed-vs-live diffs rather than asking it to guess.
- **Trusting a green `check:corpus-content` to mean `export-corpus --write` is safe** — it does not, and the gap is a whole population the check is structurally blind to. `diffCorpusContent` iterates the SEED scope and skips any id the live store carries but the seed does not, so a LIVE-ONLY export-scope artifact is neither value-drift nor degraded-live; it is nothing. `computeExportedSeed` meanwhile loops over ALL live docs and APPENDS every live-only export-scope one to the seed. So the export writes a strict SUPERSET of what the check reports, and the difference is exactly the ids the check never names. This is the export-direction twin of the retire trap below, and it is the more dangerous direction: there, a wrong `sync-corpus` resurrects a retired artifact only in the live store; here, a wrong `--write` resurrects it into the COMMITTED SEED, where it survives every future migration. Measured 2026-07-30: the check printed `OK — every seed body matches live across 177 export-scope artifacts` and exited 0, while `export-corpus --pg` in the same shell reported `0 update(s) + 1 addition(s)` — `oq-diff-view-altitude`, an owner-retired question. So: dry-run, then classify every `added (live-only)` id. There are exactly two causes and they have OPPOSITE remedies — a graduation that reached the seed's live counterpart but never the seed (export it), or an artifact deliberately RETIRED live while a stale branch re-migrated it (do NOT export; drop the live row with `artifact retire … --pg`). Settle it on `events.library_event`, not on the projection.
- **Skipping the search step** — duplicate artifacts split authority and sever the evidence chain (asset:edit-first-curation); consumers no longer know which doc is canonical.
- **Co-editing the same artifact from two sessions** — writes are uncoordinated, so the last upsert silently wins and the other session's edit vanishes without an error.
- **Forgetting `pnpm db:up`** — writes fail to connect after an idle-stop; harmless, but the session stalls until it re-runs `db:up`.
- **Reading a `check:corpus-sync` seed-only artifact as a missed migration** — the check reports a seed artifact absent from live, and the reflex remedy is `sync-corpus --pg` (the ADR-0103 case: graduated into the seed, never migrated). An artifact deliberately RETIRED live looks IDENTICAL on that line and has the OPPOSITE remedy — remove it from the seed — so the reflex resurrects a closed decision. Retiring any `SEED_SCOPE_KINDS` kind is a TWO-SURFACE operation: `artifact retire … --pg` drops the live row and the seed entry must go in the SAME change, because `sync-corpus` is migrate-only and re-adds anything the seed still holds. Settle direction by EVIDENCE before running either: the live history is `events.library_event` (`id`/`kind`/`type`/`doc`/`actor`/`at`), NOT the `events.library_artifact` projection a CLI read shows you — a `deleted` event proves a retire, while an absent id proves only absence and cannot tell the two cases apart. Check whether `origin/main` has already dropped the seed row too; if it has, your branch is merely stale and the fix is the seed removal (or a merge), never a sync. Expect recurrence: a retire stays RACY until the seed removal lands on main, since every sibling branched off an older main still carries the row and re-migrates it. `oq-diff-view-altitude`, closed by owner direction under ADR-0267 D5, has been resurrected FOUR times this way — `seq 2694 deleted`, `2695 created`, `2696 deleted`, `2698 created`, `2702 deleted`, `2742 created` — the fourth found live and re-retired by a librarian pass on 2026-07-30, which is also when it was caught one step from being written into the committed seed by an `export-corpus --write` running against a GREEN `check:corpus-content`. Do the seed removal as a parse → filter → re-stringify at two-space indent with a trailing newline round-trip, which is byte-identical on this file, so the diff is the one artifact rather than a whole-file reformat.

- **Reconciling a `check:corpus-content` red without reading WHO it is charged to** — the check compares the committed seed against the LIVE store, and live is not in git, so `git diff` alone can never tell you whether a difference is yours. Until ADR-0290 it charged the whole shared population to whoever gated next, and the session that found a red was usually not the session that made it; six sessions filed that defect independently, and each proved its innocence by hand. **The check now does that proof**, from two exact signals — your seed diff against `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`, and the latest live writer per artifact (`events.library_event.actor`, stamped `cli@<branch>` since ADR-0290) — and labels every drift `YOURS`, `BEHIND MAIN`, or `ANOTHER WRITER`. So READ THE LABEL, and act on it rather than around it: `YOURS` is the breach and is discharged with the scoped `export-corpus --id <id> --pg --write` the check prints for you; `BEHIND MAIN` means `origin/main`'s seed already carries that live body and the remedy is `git merge origin/main` — exporting there re-authors a hunk already on main; `ANOTHER WRITER` is named with its writer and is not yours to reconcile, so route it back or leave it, and never blind-export it, because that commits their body under your name. Two things the mechanism does NOT do. It does not settle DIRECTION — which side is canonical is still the per-artifact judgement the next entry describes, and it is still yours to make for your own artifact. And it does not survive an unmeasurable signal: if git or the event log cannot be read the check says so and charges everything, so an unexplained red is still a red. Two facts about the substrate remain worth carrying: live moves under you, so a drift list read even minutes earlier is a claim about the past; and every live row written before 2026-08-02 is unattributed, so a pre-existing backlog reports as `ANOTHER WRITER` and drains only through its own authors' gates. The check SKIPs in CI (DB-free), so the ATTRIBUTION work never blocks a PR — but do not read that as the COST being local-only, because what a blind export WRITES is not. The committed seed feeds `check:surface-coverage`, which DOES run in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`; it reads the seed plus the root `package.json` and is DB-free precisely so that it can). Measured 2026-08-02 (#1089): an unscoped export carried a sibling's live prose into the seed, that prose named `storytree proposal` — a verb that existed only on their unpushed branch — and CI went red on a surface the exporting session had never authored. ADR-0290 makes that avoidable rather than impossible: scope the export to your own id and you never carry their prose at all. If you land it anyway, revert that ONE seed row, disclose it in the PR, and let their PR close the gap.
verification: The write-path guards are machine-checked: the CLI **refuses** any write without `--pg`, `artifact new` refuses an existing id, and `validateLibraryDoc` rejects an invalid doc at the boundary — none of these can be skipped by forgetting them. Nothing, however, checks that a session searched before writing, that `knowledge.json` or the generated files weren't hand-edited, or that `load-corpus.ts --force` isn't run over live CLI edits — those steps rest entirely on the session honouring the ceremony.

title: Retire a realized proposal
description: How to retire a Library proposal (or open-question) once a landed ADR/PR realizes it: a dependency-gated retire against the live store PLUS a seed removal — never a status flip, because its lifecycle is permanently `open`.
statement: When a landed ADR/PR realizes a transient signal artifact (proposal / open-question), retire it in BOTH places — `artifact retire --pg` against the live store AND remove it from the seed `knowledge.json` — because its lifecycle is permanently `open` (a status edit is a no-op) and migrate-only `sync-corpus` will otherwise resurrect the seed copy.
trigger: A landed decision — an accepted ADR, a merged PR, a graduation — has REALIZED a Library `proposal` or `open-question`: the thing it asked for now exists, so the signal artifact should leave the active corpus. Observable condition: the ask is settled in the decision log or the code, yet the artifact still shows in `artifact list proposal` / on the studio shelves.
steps:
1. **Confirm the realization.** The proposal's ask is actually landed — cite the accepted ADR / merged PR. A still-open ask is NOT retired; it stays as live signal.
2. **Do NOT reach for a status flip.** `proposal` and `open-question` have no terminal / `consumed` status: `lifecycleOf(kind, doc)` (`packages/library/src/lifecycle.ts`, ADR-0196) returns `open` for both regardless of any field, so `artifact edit <id> --set status=… --pg` is a silent no-op. Retirement is a delete-with-rationale, not a state change.
3. **Clear inbound refs first.** `storytree library artifact retire` HARD-REFUSES while any other artifact still cites this one via an `asset:<id>` edge (`packages/cli/src/retire.ts`) and lists the dependents — re-point or retire them before proceeding.
4. **Retire live:** `pnpm db:up`, then `pnpm storytree library artifact retire <id> --reason "<why — realized by …>" [--superseded-by doc:decisions/<nnnn-slug>.md | asset:<replacement-id>] --pg`. `--reason` is mandatory (the rationale rides the append-only delete event) and `--pg` is required (a retire against the offline seed store is a no-op). `--superseded-by` takes `doc:<path>` (drop the `docs/` prefix) or `asset:<id>`.
5. **Remove it from the seed:** delete the artifact object from `apps/studio/data/knowledge.json`. The seed round-trips byte-identical (two-space indent, trailing newline), so a parse→filter→rewrite yields a minimal diff. Skip this and migrate-only `sync-corpus` (ADR-0103 / ADR-0120) — which re-creates any seed artifact ABSENT from live — RESURRECTS the retired proposal on the next reconcile.
6. **Land the seed removal** through the merge ceremony (asset:merge-ceremony); the live retire already persisted at step 4.
surfaces:
- **Library** — the live Cloud SQL store is written once: `pnpm storytree library artifact retire <id> --reason "…" --pg` folds `retiredReason` / `supersededBy` onto an append-only delete event and drops the projection row. The dependency-wall reads come from the same store.
- **Repo** — `apps/studio/data/knowledge.json` (the migration seed) is hand-edited to remove the artifact object, then landed via `pnpm gate` and the merge ceremony; the generated views derive from the seed, and nothing else is written.
- The live retire and the seed removal are the SAME logical change on two surfaces — `pnpm storytree library sync-corpus --pg` (migrate-only) will NOT reconcile them, so both must be done by hand.
failureModes:
- **Retiring by flipping `status`** — `lifecycleOf(proposal)` / `lifecycleOf(open-question)` always return `open` (ADR-0196), so `artifact edit --set status=retired --pg` changes a field nothing reads and the artifact stays live. Discovered on the ADR-0210 librarian pass: it took reading `lifecycle.ts` + `commands.ts` to see that `retire` (not a status edit) is the drain.
- **Retiring live but leaving the seed** — `sync-corpus` is migrate-only (adds seed artifacts ABSENT from live), so it re-creates the seed copy on the next reconcile and the proposal reappears; `check:corpus-sync` only WARNs. Remove it from `knowledge.json` in the same change.
- **Removing from the seed but not live** — the live store and the studio still show the proposal; seed and DB diverge until someone runs the retire.
- **Retiring an artifact that still has dependents** — the CLI hard-refuses and lists them; hand-deleting the row to work around this leaves dangling `asset:<id>` refs. Re-point or retire the dependents first.
- **Retiring a proposal whose ask is NOT actually landed** — destroys live signal. Confirm the realization against the decision log / code first.
verification: The write-path guards are machine-checked: `retire` requires `--reason` and `--pg`, and hard-refuses while any `asset:<id>` dependent remains (`packages/cli/src/retire.ts`). Nothing, however, checks that the seed copy was removed — `check:corpus-sync` only WARNs on a seed-only artifact — so the seed removal rests on the session honouring this ceremony.
provenance: Graduated 2026-07-18 from agent-memory `retire-realized-proposal-mechanics` (ADR-0095), discovered during the ADR-0210 librarian pass (the assets.json retirement). Derived from the `retire` CLI (owner call 2026-06-20, `packages/cli/src/retire.ts` + `commands.ts`), the universal lifecycle projection (ADR-0196, `packages/library/src/lifecycle.ts`), and the migrate-only seed↔live reconcile (ADR-0103 / ADR-0120); on any disagreement the cited ADRs and code win.

title: library
description: The shared knowledge tier — schema-validated artifact docs in the live Cloud SQL store, read just-in-time by sessions via the CLI, by humans via the studio.
oneLine: The shared **knowledge tier**: schema-validated artifact docs — reference (definitions, techstack), behavioural rules (principles, guardrails, patterns), ways-of-working (processes), roles (agents), initiative overlays (arcs, and their ephemeral plans), and transient signal units (open questions, proposals, friction) — living in the shared Cloud SQL Postgres store, read just-in-time by sessions through the CLI and by humans through the studio.
whatItIs: One of the project's three working surfaces — the story tree is the **work**, the noticeboard is the **sessions**, the library is the **knowledge** (ADR-0034). It is a corpus tier parallel to the work hierarchy: structured documents discriminated by `kind` — twelve kinds as of ADR-0183: definition, principle, pattern, guardrail, techstack, process, open-question, agent, proposal, friction (the employees' upward friction channel, ADR-0168 — a transient-lifecycle kind like open-question and proposal), arc (the initiative overlay upstream of stories and ADRs, ADR-0183), and plan (the first **ephemeral** kind — Postgres-only, excluded from `knowledge.json` and every seed ceremony, ADR-0183). The authoritative per-kind field tables are `KIND_SPECS` in `packages/library/src/knowledge.ts` — on any future mismatch, trust that table over a hand-list. Stored as **JSONB docs, zod-validated at the write boundary**, with relationships as ID references inside the docs (ADR-0017). History = events, current state = projection. The **live shared Cloud SQL Postgres store is the source of truth for artifact state** (ADR-0023 §11); git holds the code plus the *generated* `assets.json` view, and `apps/studio/data/knowledge.json` is the migration seed/export of the durable kinds — ephemeral kinds like `plan` never seed — not the edit-here surface. Sessions reach it just-in-time through the exploratory `storytree library` CLI — dashboard → kind → artifact → local DAG, choose-your-own-adventure, never a corpus dump (ADR-0023) — and humans through the studio. Artifacts are **downstream and derived**: they cite their source ADRs via `references` and reference-don't-restate; on disagreement the cited ADR wins.
whatItIsNot: Not the **studio** — the UI window onto the library (and the rest of the system), not the tier itself. Not **`docs/decisions/` ADRs** — those are the source/history layer where decisions are made; library artifacts are derived from them and cite them. Not the **`stories/` tree** — that is the work to be built; the library is the knowledge consumed while building it.
provenance: Tier returned by ADR-0017 (resolving open-q §9); named "library" by ADR-0019; live-store-as-source-of-truth and the CLI interface by ADR-0023; the three-surfaces framing and the `process` kind by ADR-0034; the tenth kind (`friction`) by ADR-0168; the `arc` initiative overlay and the first ephemeral kind (`plan`) by ADR-0183.

steps:
1. **Sync** (only when resuming an existing branch): `pnpm sync` rebases onto `origin/main`; after a rebase, push with `--force-with-lease` (fine for single-author branches — ADR-0022).
2. **Gate locally**: `pnpm gate` (repo manifest + typecheck + offline tests). It mirrors CI's `verify` job, which additionally runs the build. Red means the unit is not done — do not proceed to a non-draft PR. **Invoke it BACKGROUNDED on the first attempt.** The gate walks every workspace project, and several of its steps open a live DB connection whose handshake is not time-bounded, so its wall-clock is a property of the corpus's breadth and the shared instance's power state rather than of this unit's size — it can exceed the harness's fixed foreground tool-call ceiling, and a foreground invocation is then killed mid-run and reports no verdict at all, losing the whole run at the worst moment (this step sits immediately before landing). Backgrounding costs nothing on the runs that finish fast, so it is the correct first attempt, not a fallback after a kill. A killed run is UNVERIFIED, not red (`asset:unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted`): re-run it, and never read the termination code as a gate verdict or chase it as a regression. **A green covers the tree it ran over, and nothing more.** This step is discharged only by a gate over the tree you are about to commit — never by an earlier green, including the one that satisfied the Trigger. Any edit landing after that green stales it, and the standing pre-merge librarian pass is the routine case rather than the exception, since correcting ADR bodies is its job; retro residue, a memory file, and a post-gate doc fix stale it identically. Left un-re-gated, step 3 commits files the local green never typechecked or tested and CI becomes their first check. So it is the LAST edit, not the first green, that step 3 waits on: re-gate over the final tree, then commit.
3. **Commit** the unit on the session branch, never directly on `main` — over a tree step 2's green actually covers.
4. **Push** the branch to `origin`.
5. **Open a non-draft PR** into `main` with `gh pr create`. A `claude/real/*` promotion branch's tip is the verdict's exact attested commit — never rebase, squash, or amend it (ADR-0031).
6. **Stop.** Never run `gh pr merge` in any flavor (including `--auto`): the repo has no required checks or branch protection, so a manual merge lands *instantly, pre-CI*. The workflow's `automerge` job (`needs: verify`) merges with `--merge --delete-branch` — a true merge commit, which is what keeps a promoted verdict's commit an ancestor of `main`.
7. **To hold a PR** — the only opt-out — mark it a draft or add the `hold` label. A hold is **temporary**: when the held unit is green and ready, flip the draft to ready (`gh pr ready`) or drop the `hold` label so it merges — a finished, green unit must never stay parked in draft. Every other green non-draft PR merges. Merge to `main` quickly and frequently; the cadence is trunk-based.
8. **After the merge, the branch is dead (ADR-0142).** CI's merge job machine-clears the merged branch's board state (claim release keyed on the head branch — any branch shape since PR #1025), and the merged-branch guard refuses any future PR from the same head branch. **Never resume coding in the worktree whose branch just merged** — its checkout is a stale snapshot of a `main` that has already moved (ADR-0275 D1 Axis 1, mechanical, never judged). Run the closing leg (step 9); its fork decides what, if anything, comes next.
9. **The closing leg (ADR-0271, forked by ADR-0275)** — after automerge confirms, in order: **(a) residue** — append the arc's increment-log entry (`storytree arc increment add <arc-id> --outcome "<what landed>" --pr <n> --pg`, ADR-0183 D1), flip a consumed plan's `status` to `consumed` (a drifted one to `superseded`; the arc is never otherwise edited when children land, ADR-0183 D3), and write any memory worth keeping; **(b) release claims** — `storytree noticeboard done --pg` (belt-and-braces over the machine-clear: a claim taken on a *different* branch than the PR's head is the measured dead-holder class this guarantees against); **(c) leave the worktree committed-clean** — never `git worktree remove` your own tree mid-session; **(d) debrief the owner** — what landed (PR number + a plain-language outcome paragraph), what continues (and why), and for EVERY follow-up you identified either the chip you created, named by its chip title, or **the one-line reason you judged it not worth a session** — *‘not worth a session’ is a first-class, FREE outcome* (ADR-0288: no marker, no penalty, no durable record, the same move ADR-0168 D1 made for friction capture). The bar: would this be worth a fresh session if it were the only thing on the list? Name what it costs to leave undone; if you cannot, it is below the bar — and a follow-up the closing leg ENUMERATED, rather than the work surfacing it, starts below the bar. Only SILENCE is forbidden: decline out loud, or chip it. Then what remains open + where it lives (arc / ADR / chip); **(e) the continue-or-inert fork (ADR-0275 D1)**:
   - **Non-code continuation is always available, no fresh worktree needed.** Discussion, analysis, and Library/decision-log `--pg` edits may keep going in this session, in this same worktree — none of it touches repo code, so the dead branch has nothing to make stale.
   - **The moment repo code needs to change again**, stand up a fresh worktree on a fresh branch cut from freshly-fetched `origin/main` (`pnpm storytree worktree create`, ADR-0200 D3, or the harness's own worktree-switch mechanism) — mandatory, not a judgment call. Run `pnpm install` there before trusting the next gate (the mid-session-merge staleness trap) and re-declare claims at ADR-0270 grain.
   - **Then judge whether to drive that fresh worktree in THIS session, or hand off to a fresh one** (`asset:session-cutting`) — the session's own call on its remaining context headroom, gated by ADR-0275 D2's hard ends (workstream fork, ~3 continuations, degraded context, or an owner-LOOK/decision/attestation leg — any of these end THIS session’s run at that work, never a wait; whether the work is then chipped at all is step (d)’s worth-a-session call, ADR-0288). Context thin or stale → land the decision-log residue first (this step's (a)), *then* cut the fresh session — never carry a half-oriented context into more coding.
   - **Otherwise, go inert (e)** — no further monitors, polling loops, scheduled wakeups, or new work in this session; new work re-enters through a fresh session. Inert is not mute (ADR-0271 D3): keep answering questions, analysis, and read-only exploration freely — never refuse, never fight; when the owner asks for new *work* and this session has gone inert, chip it into a fresh session, visibly and by name, rather than doing it here. Optionally at the debrief: surface qualifying merged-idle sibling sessions as an archive offer (`prState` MERGED, not running, idle past the generous ~12–24 h threshold, each named by title; every archive is owner-confirmed — ADR-0271 D4).
title: Merge ceremony
trigger: A unit of work is complete and the local gate is green — `pnpm gate` passes on the session's branch — with nothing red or WIP in the diff. Run the ceremony **without waiting to be asked**: sitting on green work is the failure this artifact exists to stop (ADR-0034). It also begins when picking a branch back up on another machine — start at the sync step.
surfaces:
**Repo/CI only.** Runs `pnpm gate` locally as the pre-merge check (mirrored by CI's `verify` job), then reads the working tree and branch state; writes a commit, a pushed branch, and a PR; CI's `verify` job re-runs the gate on the merge result and the `automerge` job writes the merge to git `main` and deletes the branch.

**Two trunks — do not conflate them.** This ceremony governs the **dev repo's git `main`**, the meta-layer that builds storytree. The **product story-trunk** is a different surface: it is approval-gated (ADR-0008; `trunk`, `approval-gated-trunk`) and is **never auto-merged** — a green agent result there is a request for human diff-review, not a landing. The invariant shared by both is *never merge un-green*; what differs is whether green is sufficient (here, yes — solo author) or necessary-but-not-sufficient (the product).
statement: When a unit of work is green, commit, push, and open a **non-draft PR** — then stop: the CI `automerge` job lands it on the dev repo's git `main` once `verify` passes, and a session never merges manually.
provenance:
Synthesized downstream of ADR-0022/0031 per ADR-0034 (the kind's first instance); on any disagreement the cited ADR wins. Step 8's branch-dies-on-merge half derives from ADR-0142; ADR-0271 (2026-07-30, amending ADR-0142) then retired that step's continuation half — cut a fresh branch and keep working — and added step 9, the closing leg (residue, release claims, owner debrief, inert). The typed reference to ADR-0271 was added by the librarian pass 2026-07-30, closing an ADR-0154 projection gap: the body cited that ADR four times while the ADR itself was absent from Sources, so the process carrying the session-ends-at-merge floor did not cite the decision behind it. This artifact is that floor's SOLE home by guidance-curator's 2026-07-30 ruling — a ceremony step with no deterministic enforcer is process content, not a principle or guardrail (ADR-0034 §2), and a restating rule would breach `asset:reference-dont-restate`; `asset:session-cutting` records the same call from the delegation side.
Step 2's backgrounded-invocation guidance was added by the librarian pass 2026-08-01, discharging the adjudicated friction `pnpm-gate-exceeds-the-foreground-tool-ceiling` (ADR-0168 D4 bounded drain, routed `edit-existing` to this artifact because a ceremony step's invocation guidance is process content, not behavioural-floor content — ADR-0034 §2). It makes NO new policy: gating locally was already mandated by this step and by ADR-0022; what was missing was how to invoke it without losing the run. Deliberately stateless per `asset:stateless-vs-stateful-graduation` — the rule is written, never a duration, because the gate's wall-clock on a given host is host-state while the ceiling and the repo's breadth are fixed. The adjudication's second half was NOT restated here: `asset:unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted` already covers a killed or timed-out job more completely, so it is CITED (`asset:reference-dont-restate`, `asset:edit-first-curation`).
Step 8/9 revised 2026-08-01 per ADR-0275 (the owner's live-conversation acceptance of the continue-or-inert fork, amending ADR-0271 D1): "cut a fresh branch and keep working" stays retired, but "the session's working life ends with the merge" is no longer unconditional — a session MAY continue, on two independent axes (ADR-0275 D1): non-code continuation (discussion, `--pg` Library/decision-log edits) needs no fresh worktree and was never actually blocked by ADR-0271; the moment repo code is touched again, a fresh worktree is mandatory (mechanical, never judged), and whether that work happens in this session or a freshly cut one is the session's own judgment call on its remaining context headroom. The failure-modes bullet on continuing on a merged branch was edited in place rather than restated, per `asset:edit-first-curation` — it now names the legal exception instead of a blanket prohibition. A new failure mode records ADR-0275 D5's honest gap: the worktree a continuation abandons is not reliably reaped on any bounded clock today (`worktree-reaper-integrity-arc`).
Step 2's gate-coverage clause, step 3's pointer to it, and the paired "Committing a tree the gate never saw" failure mode were added by the librarian pass 2026-08-03, discharging the adjudicated friction `the-pre-merge-librarian-pass-stales-the-gate-that-certified-the-unit` (ADR-0168 D4 bounded drain, routed `edit-existing` here on this artifact's OWN recorded precedent — a ceremony step's invocation guidance is process content, not behavioural-floor content, ADR-0034 §2 — the same call that placed step 2's backgrounded-invocation guidance in the paragraph above). It makes NO new policy: gating before the commit is already this step and ADR-0022, and the pre-merge pass's placement is already fixed by the failure mode this one pairs with; what was missing is only that the green must COVER what is committed. Stated deliberately on the GATE'S COVERAGE rather than on the librarian pass, so the same wording catches retro residue and post-gate doc fixes — the pass is named as the routine case, never as the scope. Deliberately stateless per `asset:stateless-vs-stateful-graduation`: the filing session's gate wall-clock and the two decision-log files its pass had edited stay OUT, on the same grounds that kept a duration out of step 2's backgrounded-invocation guidance. Two independent sessions have now filed at the boundary between the pre-merge pass and the commit — the sibling `automerge-lands-the-pr-before-the-pre-merge-librarian-pass-can-finish` (discharged into the failure mode this one pairs with) is the too-late-to-land direction, this one the too-early-to-be-true direction — so the two bullets cross-reference and the seam reads as one. Two alternatives were considered and rejected. A mechanical fence (stamping the gate's verdict with a tree hash and refusing a commit whose tree does not match) is a substantially larger unit than the defect warrants and would need care not to collide with `asset:never-bypass-the-gate`, while the sibling failure at this same seam was fixed with prose here and has not re-appeared. Editing the `session-orchestrator` agent artifact instead was rejected because the agent tier is seed-canonical under ADR-0055 with its own reconciliation ceremony, and that agent already CITES this process — so the rule reaches it through the citation and stays in one place (`asset:reference-dont-restate`).
description: The dev-repo landing ceremony: when a unit of work is green, commit, push, open a non-draft PR, and stop — CI auto-merges on green; sessions never merge manually. Read before landing anything on git `main`.
failureModes:
- **Manual `gh pr merge`** merges instantly, pre-CI — no required checks exist, so the gate is bypassed entirely. This is the recorded incident: sessions reached for `gh pr merge` (including `--auto`, which on this unprotected repo also merges immediately) and landed unverified work (ADR-0034). Let the workflow merge.
- **Squash-merging a `claude/real/*` promotion PR** mints a new sha and orphans the persisted verdict's anchor; the attested commit must remain an ancestor of `main` (ADR-0031).
- **Sitting on green work**: the owner repeatedly had to tell sessions to commit and open a PR (ADR-0034's observable symptom), and unlanded work drifts across the owner's machines.
- **Red/WIP work in a non-draft PR**: the moment it happens to go green it auto-merges, and half-finished work lands on `main`. Finish the unit or mark the PR draft.
- **Leaving a finished unit in a draft hold**: marking a PR draft to pause mid-build is correct; forgetting to flip it back to ready once the unit is green re-creates 'sitting on green work' by another name — the held PR never auto-merges and the owner has to ask why it is still a draft (the recorded 2026-06-14 slip). A hold is temporary.
- **Conflating the two trunks**: waiting for a human to merge a dev PR (a stall — none is coming), or carrying auto-merge-on-green thinking onto the product story-trunk (exactly the v1 scar `approval-gated-trunk` exists to prevent).
- **Leaving slow pre-merge work running once the PR is open**: the last moment a session controls is *before* `gh pr create`, NOT 'before the merge' — under ADR-0022 the merge is a CI event the session neither performs nor can delay, and a green PR automerges fast (measured median 4.4 min open-to-merge, p90 4.9 min, n=124 over 2026-07-23→07-28). The standing pre-merge librarian pass is the usual casualty: spawned in the same turn the PR opens, it returns to a branch automerge has already merged and killed, its edits uncommitted on it (the recorded 2026-07-28 incident — PR #984 merged inside two 30 s polls while the pass ran 29 min, stranding two ADR-0246 corrections; landing the resulting 24-line docs diff cost a re-cut branch, `pnpm install`, a full re-gate, a re-claim after the merge machine-cleared it, and a second PR #986). Sharper still, *pushing* a follow-up after the merge RE-CREATES the deleted branch, so the commit lands somewhere that is no longer an ancestor of `main` — stranded off main entirely. Finish the pass first, then commit, then open the PR. Do not 'fix' this by parking the PR in draft while the pass runs: a finished green unit sitting in draft is its own failure mode above. Its companion is the next bullet: finishing the pass too LATE strands it off a dead branch, finishing the gate too EARLY lets its edits land unverified — one seam, two directions.
- **Committing a tree the gate never saw**: the companion of the bullet above, and the routine case rather than the exception. The steps run gate → commit → push → PR with no re-gate between them, while the standing pre-merge librarian pass exists to edit ADR bodies — so on any pass that finds something to correct, the tree moves after the green: the diff grows, the commit carries files the local green never typechecked or tested, and CI becomes the first check they get. Nothing surfaces the gap — the ceremony reads as already satisfied at step 2, and the Trigger's 'nothing red or WIP in the diff' is then asserted about a tree that no longer exists — so it is silent in the ordinary case and fires precisely when the pass is WORKING. It is not specific to that pass either: retro residue, a memory file, or a post-gate doc fix stale the green identically. Re-gate over the final tree before the commit (step 2).
- **Resuming code edits in the merged worktree**: the merge just machine-cleared that branch's claims, so a session that keeps editing there works *invisibly* — no wisp, no board row (the recorded 2026-07-02 incident: an active session vanished from the map after its PR merged) — and its next PR is refused by the merged-branch guard anyway. ADR-0275 D1 Axis 1 makes the remedy mechanical: stand up a fresh worktree the moment repo code is touched again, in this session or a fresh one — never in the merged tree. Non-code continuation (discussion, `--pg` Library edits) is the one thing that legitimately keeps going in place.
- **Skipping the closing leg, or continuing past a D2 hard end**: landing and walking away parked-open re-creates the audit's biggest measured cost (~48% of lost wall-clock, 2026-07-30) — the tab sits with monitors running, the owner re-tasks it stale, and follow-ups worth doing never become findable chips. Continuing in-session past a hard end (a workstream fork, ~3 continuations, degraded context, or an owner-gated leg, ADR-0275 D2) re-creates the same parked shape by another route — a session waiting on the owner instead of deciding the follow-up out loud and going inert. The debrief (ADR-0271 D2 / ADR-0275 D1 / ADR-0288) is the checklist: residue appended, claims released, every follow-up either chipped-and-named or declined in one line (or the continuation reason recorded), then either the fresh-worktree work or inert.
- **Declining a follow-up in SILENCE**: ADR-0288 made ‘not worth a session’ a free outcome — it did not make it a silent one. The *judgment* became sayable; the *omission* did not. A debrief naming neither a chip nor a decline for work the session identified is precisely the failure ADR-0288 must not introduce, and its D7(c) measures it: a refutation there restores ADR-0271 D2(b) verbatim. Say the one line — what you considered, and why it is not worth a session.
- **Assuming the abandoned worktree cleans itself up on a bounded clock**: it does not (ADR-0275 D5) — the standing reaper only fires opportunistically at another session's `SessionStart`, throttled to once per 30 minutes, past a 48 h idle floor, and never overrides a `git worktree lock` whose liveness against the actual process is unchecked (`worktree-reaper-integrity-arc`). Don't report a continuation's old worktree as "cleaned up" without checking `git worktree list`.
verification: The green-before-merge half is deterministic: `automerge` is an Actions job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with `needs: verify`, gated to non-draft PRs without the `hold` label, and the `pull_request` checkout tests the merge result — nothing merges *through the workflow* un-green. The branch-dies-on-merge half is also deterministic: the merged-branch guard (`scripts/merged-branch-guard.sh`, a `verify` step) refuses a PR whose head branch already has a merged PR (ADR-0142). **Nothing checks the rest**: there is no branch protection, so no machine stops a manual `gh pr merge` — merge-only-via-the-workflow is enforced by convention (ADR-0022 says so explicitly); and non-squash for `claude/real/*` is a recorded operating rule whose enforcement automation is later work (ADR-0031).

title: Attempt privileged actions, approve inline
description: When an action needs the owner's authorization, attempt it yourself and let approval happen inline (issue the tool call so the harness surfaces its permission prompt, or ask a quick inline yes/no) — don't decline in prose and hand the command back for the owner to run in a terminal. The human still owns the sign-off; this changes the MECHANISM, not who decides.
statement: For an action that needs owner authorization — `terraform apply`, a deploy, an infra or `gh` mutation, any outward-facing or hard-to-reverse op — ATTEMPT it yourself and let approval happen INLINE (issue the tool call so the harness surfaces its permission prompt, or ask one short inline yes/no), rather than declining in prose and handing the command back for the owner to run manually; the human still owns the sign-off, so this is an approval-MECHANISM way-of-working, NOT a request to auto-allow.
trigger: A unit reaches a step that needs the owner's go-ahead before it can proceed — an irreversible, outward-facing, or otherwise privileged action (terraform/deploy/infra/`gh`/anything that touches a live external surface). The decision to do it is still the owner's (`owner-fork-bar`, `human-owns-the-outer-loop`); what this process governs is HOW you put that decision to them.
steps:
1. **Don't punt it to a terminal.** Refusing in prose — 'you should now run `terraform apply`' — and handing the command back is the failure this exists to stop: the owner is a solo operator, and context-switching to a terminal to run a command you could run is friction they asked to be gone (stated 2026-06-22, after an idle-stop `terraform apply` was punted to them).
2. **For irreversible infra, plan first.** Default to a read-only preview — `terraform plan`, a dry-run, a diff — and show its output, so the owner approves against a concrete change, not a blind apply.
3. **Issue the action and let the prompt surface.** Run the tool call; the harness's inline permission prompt IS the approval surface. Where a permission prompt doesn't apply, ask one short inline yes/no (a quick AskUserQuestion) — approving stays a single inline step, never a task handed off.
4. **Keep the decision with the owner.** Surface the decision every time — the human owns the outer-loop sign-off (`asset:human-owns-the-outer-loop`); you are making the approval one click, not removing it.
surfaces: **The session's own action surface** — the privileged tool call (terraform/deploy/`gh`/infra REST) and the harness permission prompt it raises, or an inline AskUserQuestion. No Library or repo state is written by this process itself; it shapes how an already-owner-owned action is put to the owner.
failureModes:
- **Declining in prose and handing the command back** — the recorded slip (the idle-stop `terraform apply` punted 2026-06-22): adds the exact terminal context-switch the owner wanted removed.
- **Reading it as auto-allow** — graduating 'attempt it inline' into blanket `allow`-rules in `settings.json` on the strength of this alone. This is an approval-MECHANISM preference; the owner still approves each one. Don't widen permissions off it.
- **Skipping the plan on irreversible infra** — issuing a blind `apply`/deploy without a `plan`/dry-run/diff first, so the owner approves a change they can't see.
- **Removing the human from the call** — treating 'make approval one step' as license to decide an owner-owned, irreversible, or outward-facing action yourself (the `human-owns-the-outer-loop` boundary).
verification: Not machine-checked — this is a way-of-working, not a gated path. The boundary it must not cross IS enforced elsewhere: `settings.json` permissions decide what runs without a prompt, and the inline permission prompt itself is the proof the owner approved a given action. Honouring 'attempt + inline approve' over 'decline in prose', and 'plan before irreversible apply', rests on the session following this process.
provenance: Graduated 2026-06-27 from agent-memory (ADR-0095 — feedback `attempt-privileged-actions-ask-inline`, owner preference stated 2026-06-22). A way-of-working (an approval MECHANISM), so a `process` per ADR-0034 — no existing artifact covered the mechanism (the corpus had WHO approves, not HOW the action is put to them). Cites `human-owns-the-outer-loop` (the sign-off stays the owner's; this is not auto-allow) and `owner-fork-bar` (what rises to the owner is unchanged). Consumers: session-orchestrator.

title: Stage the attestation experience
description: At an operator-attested gate (ADR-0070 stage 2 — the appearance / feel / live-SDK / spend legs a human must witness), the orchestrator STANDS UP the experience itself, VERIFIES it is actually serving, and hands the owner a confirmed-working URL/entry point plus the minimal what-to-walk — never a raw command for the owner to run and debug. Making the human's attestation frictionless is part of the orchestrator's job at that gate; the human still renders the verdict.
statement: When a unit reaches an operator-attested leg — the appearance / feel / live-SDK / spend judgment a human must witness (ADR-0070 stage 2) — the orchestrator STARTS the experience itself, VERIFIES it is genuinely serving/reachable (an HTTP probe, a marker check, or a re-run witness — never an assumption), and hands the owner a CONFIRMED-working URL plus the minimal what-to-walk / what-to-judge; a raw command is a fallback only, never the handoff. The human still renders the verdict — this makes the attestation frictionless, it does not move the sign-off.
trigger: A unit reaches a gate the leaf and the spine structurally cannot close — an `operator-attested` leg (ADR-0070 stage 2 / ADR-0007): the appearance of a visual surface, the feel of an interaction, a live-SDK or spend witness — where a human owner must observe a running experience and sign the verdict. This is the moment the orchestrator would otherwise chip the attestation item and hand the owner a command; it governs HOW that gate is put to the owner.
steps:
1. **Stand it up yourself — don't punt a command.** Start the preview / experience the owner must witness (`pnpm --filter studio dev` or `studio:up`; a hosted deep-link; the built site served the way the owner will actually view it), from the right directory with the right runner. Handing the owner a bare shell line to run is the failure this exists to stop — an environment-specific break (wrong cwd, a local dep like `astro` not on PATH so it needs `npx`, a missing `pnpm install`) stalls the attestation and pushes avoidable debugging onto the owner before they can even begin (the recorded slip: the increment-H UAT preview, 2026-07-04).
2. **Verify it is actually serving — probe, don't assume.** Confirm reachability with a real signal before you hand it over: an HTTP probe (`curl -sSf <url>` / a fetch to the health or entry route returning 2xx), a marker/content check that the expected surface rendered, or a re-run witness — never 'I started it, so it's up' (the same probe-don't-assume discipline as `asset:verify-edit-write-persisted-or-escalate` and the DB probe rule). If it will not serve, that is the orchestrator's to resolve or escalate — not the owner's to discover.
3. **Hand over a confirmed URL + the minimal walk.** Give the owner the working URL/entry point you just confirmed, plus a short 'what to walk / what to judge' (the deep-link to open, the interaction to try, the specific look/feel to rule on). Keep any raw command only as a fallback beneath the confirmed link, not as the primary handoff.
4. **Keep the verdict with the owner — do not cross into signing it.** Standing up and confirming the experience is the whole of the orchestrator's job here; the `operator-attested` verdict is the owner's and only the owner's (`asset:agent-never-self-exempts`, `asset:human-owns-the-outer-loop`). You remove the friction, not the judgment — never self-sign the look/feel because you made it easy to witness.
surfaces: **The session's own action surface** — the preview/experience the orchestrator starts (studio dev/`studio:up`, a served build, a hosted deep-link) and the probe that confirms it serves; the handoff message carrying the confirmed URL + the what-to-walk. **Repo/CI** — none written by this process; it composes with the merge/prove-and-promote ceremonies, it does not replace them. No Library or story-tree state is written — the `operator-attested` verdict is recorded through the existing promotion/attestation path once the owner signs, not by this process.
failureModes:
- **Punting a command instead of a running experience** — the recorded slip (the increment-H UAT gate, 2026-07-04): the orchestrator chipped the attestation and handed over a shell command to serve the preview; it failed in the owner's environment (wrong directory; `astro` is a local `web/` dependency not on PATH, needing `npx`), so the owner had to debug it before testing. The owner's direction: 'if you want uat human testing then you should do what you need to to have this up and running so i can easily do the testing.' A gate presented as 'here's a command, go run it' is a defect.
- **Assuming it serves without probing** — declaring the experience ready off 'I ran the start command' when the server never bound, the build 404s, or the tab is occluded (`preview_screenshot` hangs on a hidden tab). Confirm with a real probe/marker/witness, the way only the spine's observation counts for red/green, not the leaf's say-so.
- **Crossing from staging into signing** — treating 'I made the attestation frictionless' as license to record the `operator-attested` verdict yourself. The whole point of stage 2 (ADR-0070) is the one judgment the agent structurally cannot make; making it easy to witness never makes it yours to sign (`agent-never-self-exempts`).
- **Over-reading it as auto-serve for everything** — this is the operator-attested handoff, not a mandate to spin up servers for every message; it fires at the gate where a human must witness a running experience.
verification: Not machine-checked — this is a way-of-working (an attestation-handoff MECHANISM), not a gated path, so a `process` per ADR-0034. The boundary it must not cross IS enforced elsewhere: `operator-attested` can never be self-granted by an agent (ADR-0007 / the proof model / `asset:agent-never-self-exempts`), so nothing this process does can mint the verdict — it only removes the friction before the owner's sign-off. Honouring 'stand it up + probe + hand over a confirmed URL' over 'punt a command' rests on the session following this process; the probe in step 2 is the session's own honesty check that the experience is genuinely reachable.
provenance: Graduated 2026-07-04 from agent-memory at the owner's direction — after the increment-H website UAT gate, where the orchestrator chipped the operator-attested item and handed the owner a raw shell command to serve the preview; the command failed in the owner's environment (wrong cwd; `astro` a local `web/` dep needing `npx`), so the owner had to debug it before they could test, and directed the guidance be updated ('if you want uat human testing then you should do what you need to to have this up and running so i can easily do the testing'). A way-of-working (an approval/attestation MECHANISM), so a `process` per ADR-0034 — the sibling of `attempt-privileged-actions-approve-inline` (that one: don't punt a privileged COMMAND to the owner's terminal; this one: don't punt an operator-attested EXPERIENCE), and the outer-loop counterpart of `frontend-builder`'s inner-loop 'surface a hosted deep-link and STOP' (ADR-0070 §3) — the orchestrator RUNNING the gate must stand the experience up and confirm it serves, not relay a leaf's deep-link untested. Grounded in ADR-0070 (the two-stage proof; operator-attested is stage 2) and ADR-0007 (operator-attested is never self-granted). Consumers: session-orchestrator (composes with `frontend-builder`).

title: noticeboard
oneLine: The claim ledger — one of the three working surfaces (tree = the work, **noticeboard** = the sessions, library = the knowledge): sessions are forced to claim their unit at start (the capability being written, ADR-0270 D1; the story for cross-capability work), and coordination + observability are two views over ONE deterministic ledger (grades: exploring / waiting / work). The old advisory, staleness-aged session-presence rows are retired (ADR-0200).
whatItIs:
The **coordination organ** among the three working surfaces: the tree shows the work, the library holds the knowledge, the noticeboard shows the **sessions** — and since **ADR-0200** it is ONE deterministic **claim ledger** (`events.node_claim` + its `claim_event` audit log, with `events.work_event` for proof activity) that both coordinates agents AND drives every observability surface (forest map, studio dock, CLI board, statusline). Rows are keyed `(unit_id, session_id)` and carry a **grade**:

- **exploring** — shared (any number of sessions per unit), taken at session start, carries the intent prose; renders as a **hovering** wisp (someone is reading / planning here). *[The “stationary at the story” half of the original render is REVERSED on purpose by ADR-0212: an exploring wisp now carries a small-radius orbit BESIDE the island, so the hover family MOVES; the exploring GRADE itself is unchanged.]*
- **waiting** — shared, ordered by `claimed_at`: the **queue** behind a work claim; on release of the work claim the store atomically promotes the oldest live waiter (audited `promoted`). When NO work claim is held on the unit, there is no line and none is rendered (ADR-0270 D3.1).
- **work** — the exclusive mutex (one session per **unit** — the partial-unique index `WHERE grade='work'` is keyed on the unit id, and since ADR-0270 D1 the session ceremony claims the CAPABILITY being written, the story only for cross-capability work, so same-story siblings on disjoint capabilities never contend): a conflict is a **hard refusal** naming the holder and printing the unit's full claim board (ADR-0270 D3.2), and it renders as the **orbiting** wisp with the proving colour / verdict bloom layered on top from work-events.

**Identity is the worktree name** — derived, never typed — and there is **no signer chain**: a claim coordinates, it never attests (ADR-0138 §5: no claim state is ever a proof). Claims are **forced at start** via claim-gated `storytree worktree create --node <unit> --intent "<what>"`, which takes the exploring claim FIRST (no claim, no workspace — ADR-0121's claim-before-worktree ordering, generalised) and mints a self-describing `<arc>-<story>-<suffix>` worktree name. **Liveness is one trace-driven ~2 h heartbeat clock**; machine clears stand (build completion releases the `(unit, session)` row; the CI merge releases by branch), and `worktree prune`'s keep-signal is now "the session holds live claims." The automation is **never-blocking** — a claim write failure never fails the enclosing action, and nothing rides a blocking-capable hook (ADR-0033's V1 scar). **Retired by ADR-0200:** the advisory `events.session` presence rows, self-reported `workingOn` prose as a row, the derived fresh/stale/possibly-dead staleness bands, the ADR-0079 reaper, and `/api/presence` — all deleted in the arc's retirement sweep (#760–#766, 2026-07-17, after the owner's inc-5 render UAT). Defined by ADR-0033 and re-founded by ADR-0200; built through the prove-it-gate as `stories/notice-board` + `wisp-as-story-claim` via the `noticeboard-claim-ledger-arc` — per-capability status lives in the story, not here.
provenance: Decided by ADR-0033 (the board's origin, restoring V1 Agentic ADR-0022's forum≠noticeboard organ split) and re-founded by ADR-0200 as the deterministic claim ledger — advisory session-presence retired. Built as stories/notice-board + wisp-as-story-claim through the noticeboard-claim-ledger-arc.
description: The claim ledger: the single deterministic coordination surface — sessions are forced to claim their unit at start — the capability being written (ADR-0270 D1), the story only for cross-capability work — under grades exploring / waiting / work. Advisory, staleness-aged session-presence is retired (ADR-0200).
whatItIsNot: Not **advisory self-reported presence** — that world (a session upserting "I exist, working on X," aged by `lastSeenAt` into fresh / stale / possibly-dead bands and reaped by a sweep) is **retired** (ADR-0200): there is one deterministic ledger, not a prose roster nobody trusted. Not the **feedback organ** — cites, archival and synthesis belong to `stories/feedback-graduation` (ADR-0032); the noticeboard carries claims only.
