- **The just-in-time BODY-pull surface (read, no state written)** — `storytree library artifact <id>` fetches one ceremony/principle/pattern BODY at the step that needs it (a floor rule's rationale, or a door's ceremony); repo files (ADRs, stories, source) are pulled by direct `Read` of the brief-named path, not through a CLI entrypoint.
- **The enforcement surface (gate, no state written)** — `pnpm check:agents` gates the render's SHAPE: token budget, no full-body inline, step→refs integrity, no unattached `context` ref.
- **Writes NOTHING to the story-tree or the live store.** This is purely a read/render/pull path over the Library and repo; it takes no work-hierarchy claim, signs no verdict, and mutates no artifact state. It composes WITH [[library-edit-ceremony]] (which owns live artifact WRITES) and runs INSIDE a spawn the orchestrator's [[merge-ceremony]] wraps, but overlaps neither.
statement: A spawned delegatable subagent runs on an ESSENTIALS-ONLY prompt — its own prose (role, authority, workflow shape) plus a one-line FLOOR of rule assertions, the inline ESCALATE-UP escape hatch, and a per-step DOORS map — and PULLS ceremony/principle BODIES just-in-time from the CLI at the step that needs them, never carrying a full ref body at spawn (ADR-0156, unified into the node-keyed context DAG by ADR-0161).
provenance: Derived (per ADR-0034 §2, reference-don't-restate) from ADR-0156 (subagent prompts are essentials-only; the CLI serves ceremony bodies just-in-time) and ADR-0161 (the Library is a node-keyed context DAG; agent step-nodes and process nodes share one `next:` emitter); on any disagreement the cited ADRs win. Authored under ADR-0154 (librarian-curator owns the `process` tier as a standing projection of the decision log) as ADR-0161 decision 4's charter obligation.
description: Read before spawning a delegatable subagent or when a subagent needs a ceremony/principle body: the essentials-only prompt + just-in-time CLI pull model (ADR-0156/0161).
failureModes:
- **Pushing full ref bodies at spawn (the pre-ADR-0156 bloat).** The measured baseline: each delegatable `.claude/agents/*.md` was ~3–7k tokens, 60–83% of it injected ref BODIES (story-author ~7.2k / 90%, librarian-curator ~7.1k), so the machine did the restating `reference-dont-restate` forbids — and inlined a STALE spawn-time snapshot of guidance the agent barely re-touched (a guidance body pulled in ~3 of 119 librarian runs). `pnpm check:agents` now FAILS a rendered file that inlines any body.
- **A thin prompt that IMPROVISES instead of escalating.** The risk a thin prompt invites — inventing a process, force-fitting a hollow proof, or silently skipping work that is out of scope — is exactly what the INLINE escape hatch (step 3) exists to prevent. Skipping "stop and hand up to the manager" turns a thin brief into a wrong result rather than a clean escalation.
- **Pulling everything up front.** A cold `storytree` pull is ~5s; front-loading every ceremony body just moves the bloat into onboarding latency instead of removing it. Pulls are STEP-triggered — because each situational ceremony fires in a fraction of runs, expected pulls per run stay low. The floor and escape hatch are inline precisely so zero pulls are needed to be SAFE.
- **A dangling step→ref or an unattached `context` ref.** A step→refs entry that names no real workflow step, a ref key that resolves to nothing, or a `context` ceremony ref not attached to any step reddens `pnpm check:agents` (step→refs integrity + no just-in-case riders) — the fence the agent-file surface never had before ADR-0156.
verification:
`pnpm check:agents` deterministically gates the prompt's SHAPE: the token budget (≤6000), no full ref BODY inline (assertions + pointers only), step→refs integrity (every entry names a real workflow step; no dangling ref key), and no unattached `context` ref for an agent that carries a step-map. `pnpm build:agents` regenerates every harness-native agent directory, so the on-disk prompt cannot drift from the Library source.

What is NOT machine-checked — and rests entirely on the subagent honouring this process at runtime — is the PULL BEHAVIOUR itself: nothing forces a running subagent to actually follow its door and pull the right body at the right step, or to reach for the inline escape hatch instead of improvising. The gate guarantees the prompt is THIN and correctly-shaped (floor present, doors present, no inlined bodies); it does not — and cannot — guarantee the agent pulls when it should. That half is a convention the agent's own discipline upholds, not a gate.

title: Friction earns durable guidance by supporting evidence, not by being reported
description: A friction item's essence graduates only when its evidence SUPPORTS the claimed lesson (not merely exists) and the lesson is irreducible — worth is judged against the anti-slop floor, never counted.
statement: Before any friction item's essence graduates into durable guidance, an adjudicator must clear a justification floor whose load-bearing, non-redundant demand is that the cited evidence actually SUPPORTS the stated lesson — a real command, log, or PR is necessary but never sufficient; it must substantiate the claim, not merely coexist with it. The remaining floor is the existing anti-slop corpus applied unchanged — reconstructible-from-today's-corpus graduates nothing (`asset:` blind-reconstruction / ADR-0024), editing the closest existing artifact is preferred to a new one (`asset:edit-first-curation`), only stateless rules graduate and uncertainty withholds (`asset:stateless-vs-stateful-graduation`), the rule must be discriminatory — naming a concrete future situation where an agent acts differently (`asset:signal-and-noise`), it must have recurred or be structurally certain to recur, and the cheapest durable fix (a tool or code fence over prose an agent must remember) is preferred. Worth is EARNED by supporting evidence plus irreducibility and JUDGED, never decided by any count or threshold.
why: A session retro is structurally self-report: there is no typed event stream to cite, and an eager frontier model manufactures plausible-sounding lessons on demand. The specific failure this floor answers is confabulation atop real evidence — a genuine artifact (a true cold-start log, a real PR) is attached to a lesson it does not actually support (the log 'always db:up first' contradicts ADR-0162's need-gated posture), and a gate that checks only that evidence EXISTS waves the junk through. Left unchecked this rots the durable tier the way judgment-only admission did at production scale (a Mem0 audit found 97.8% of 10,134 LLM-gated entries were junk), and a rotted durable tier erodes trust in every piece of Library guidance a future session reads.
howToApply: The adjudicator reads the friction item's prose and evidence and asks first the discriminating question this floor adds: does the evidence SUPPORT the stated lesson, or does it merely exist alongside it? Trace the citation to the claim — a command output, error, or PR that does not substantiate the lesson (or that a live source contradicts) fails here regardless of being real; for any route that renders into agent guidance, verification is spawned to a read-only checker proportional to blast radius. The rest of the floor is applied by citation, not re-derivation: reconstructible-from-today's-corpus routes to nothing (ADR-0024); an edit to the closest existing artifact is preferred over a new unit (`asset:edit-first-curation`); only stateless rules pass and uncertainty withholds (`asset:stateless-vs-stateful-graduation`); the rule must name a concrete future situation where an agent chooses differently (`asset:signal-and-noise`); a one-off waits for reinforcement; and the cheapest durable fix — a tool or code fence over prose an agent must remember — wins. The verdict is a JUDGMENT recorded as prose, never an arithmetic score: worth is earned by supporting evidence and irreducibility, weighed, not counted. The bar deliberately trades occasional delay of real signal — a genuine but singly-observed trap waits for reinforcement rather than graduating on first sight — for the durable tier's trustworthiness; when uncertain, withhold.
provenance: Authored 2026-07-07 for ADR-0168 inc 5 (the friction feedback loop); the behavioural floor the friction-adjudication process's 7-question gate applies as its RULE (the ordered procedure ships separately as the `friction-adjudication` process, ADR-0034/ADR-0154 — this states the durable truth, not the steps). Its one new assertion is evidence-must-support-not-merely-exist; every other criterion is cited from the existing anti-slop corpus per `asset:reference-dont-restate` rather than re-derived. Consumers: graduation-synthesist and librarian-curator (the adjudicators). Grounded in ADR-0168 D5, ADR-0032 §3/§5 (no numeric threshold ever decides what graduates), and ADR-0024 (the blind-reconstruction test).

steps:
1. **Run the ordered 7-question gate, answering each into `routeReason`** (ADR-0168 D5 — the RULE and the evidence floor are `asset:friction-justification-bar`, not restated here): (1) **Does the evidence SUPPORT the claim — not merely exist?** the anchor question: a real cold-start log does not support 'always `db:up` first' (it contradicts ADR-0162); for any route that renders into agent guidance, spawn `asset:corpus-investigator` to verify (the blast-radius rule in step 3). (2) **Reconstructible?** would a fresh agent re-derive this from today's corpus just-in-time (ADR-0024, `asset:signal-and-noise`) → `nothing`. (3) **Closest existing artifact — why is an edit not enough?** (`asset:edit-first-curation`; the search and its result go in `routeReason`). (4) **Stateless?** (`asset:stateless-vs-stateful-graduation`) — UNCERTAIN stays open. (5) **Discriminatory?** name the concrete future situation where an agent acts differently. (6) **Recurred — or structurally certain to recur?** one-offs wait for reinforcement (the `reinforcedBy` testimony, never a threshold). (7) **Cheapest fix?** a code fence or tool beats guidance an agent must remember — prefer the `tool` route over prose.
2. **Route by the table (executor → reviewer):** `nothing` → the adjudicator archives (tombstone + `routeReason` — the logged reason is the audit; the item is RETAINED, recurrence re-opens it). `edit-existing` → librarian edits (guidance-curator if it touches the behavioural floor) + **corpus-investigator verify**. `principle` / `guardrail` → **guidance-curator** authors the floor artifact + **mandatory corpus-investigator verify** (renders into EVERY future session — the highest blast radius). `process` → librarian derives it, and it must cite its deciding ADR (ADR-0154, makes no new policy). `definition` → librarian, reference tier. `adr` → the adjudicator drafts a **born-`proposed`** ADR with the alignment check (step 4) — this IS the owner escalation, the owner ratifies. `tool` → the adjudicator WRITES the remedy as a `proposal` (`storytree proposal new --title "…" --summary … --motivation … --change … --scope … --migration … --readiness … --pg`) and routes CITING it (`storytree friction route <id> --route tool --reason @<file> --proposal <proposal-id> --pg`). The routing is REFUSED until the item cites a live proposal, machine-checked (ADR-0287 D1) — so `tool` is symmetric with the routes above rather than the one route that names a destination and stops. Your question-3/7 SCOPE prose IS the proposal body; nothing new is written, it just lands somewhere listable, countable and seed-scope instead of inside an archived `routeReason`. `asset:story-author` then CONSUMES that proposal when it authors the capability (agent-side, ADR-0158 discipline) — it CANNOT write one, being fail-closed fenced to `stories/**` with no Library artifact write and no `--pg`, which is what forces the adjudicator to hold the pen (ADR-0287 D2; no fence is widened). A `proposal` is SEED-SCOPE, so the ADR-0120/0263 export belongs in the same PR. A `spawn_task` chip only when the adjudicator judges owner visibility warranted.
3. **Match verification to blast radius.** Guidance-rendering routes — `principle`, `guardrail`, `edit-existing` — flow through the render pipeline into every future session's guidance, so they carry the MANDATORY `asset:corpus-investigator` verification of the friction's factual claims before anything renders. The `adr` route is contained (born `proposed`, owner-held), so it needs the alignment check, not a render-time gate. Batch adjudication is never 'owner-directed in this conversation', so a friction-born ADR can NEVER be born `accepted` (ADR-0110); it is always `proposed`.
4. **On the `adr` route, run the friction→ADR alignment check** (ADR-0168 D5) before the draft leaves the adjudicator: (a) survey `storytree adr list --load-bearing` and NAME every touched decision in the new ADR's Context; (b) `asset:corpus-investigator` verifies the friction's factual claims against live sources; (c) declare `amends` / `supersedes` edges up front — the two binary edge types (`adr-health` enforces them mechanically, and FAILS the gate on the ADR-0139-retired `supersedes_in_part`, so naming it would author an ADR the merge refuses); (d) a contradiction with an accepted load-bearing ADR HALTS as an owner escalation — never drafted around.
5. **Keep the drain aged, bounded, and fail-closed (ADR-0168 D4).** Only routable items are eligible (aged ≥1 session, filed by another branch). The pre-merge pass drains the K≈3 oldest routable items — NEVER the whole worklist per merge (it doesn't scale with landing rate; parallel sessions would clobber same-artifact adjudications). The fail-closed ceiling (open-count > N≈12 or oldest-open > M≈21 days) is delegated to `check:friction-drain`, which flips WARN → red and requires a board-drain session — agent-side, it never pulls the owner in. This is QUEUE-HYGIENE only: no count or age ever decides what graduates (`asset:meter-fail-closed-caps-in-real-cost`, the ADR-0130 turn-cap precedent).
6. **Honour the anti-self-sealing clause (ADR-0168 D6).** A graduated friction-born artifact is not sacred: contradicting one with NEW evidence is itself first-class friction (re-filed, re-opening the originating item with the counter-evidence), NEVER non-adherence. Without this line the corpus's own owner-fork-bar discipline would make a wrong graduated rule self-sealing.
7. **Stop at routing / escalation.** Setting `route`/`routeReason`, drafting the born-`proposed` ADR, and — on the `tool` route — writing the `proposal` that route emits is the adjudication's whole job; the per-route authors EXECUTE (guidance-curator authors the floor, librarian the process/definition/edit, story-author the capability behind a `tool` route's proposal), and ratifying a friction-born ADR is owner-held (`asset:human-owns-the-outer-loop`).
title: Friction adjudication
trigger: The pre-merge librarian pass (or a spawned board-drain session at the `check:friction-drain` ceiling) reaches routable friction — an open item at least one session old, filed by a branch OTHER than the current one (the filer never adjudicates its own item — no marking your own homework). The dedicated adjudicator is the `graduation-synthesist` (ADR-0168 D5); the pre-merge librarian pass runs the bounded routine drain and hands the deeper judgment (whole-system view, the ADR route, owner-escalation) to it. This governs HOW each routable item is drained; capture is a different moment (the orchestrator's retro step, `asset:session-orchestrator`), and worth is never arithmetic.
surfaces: **Library (live store, events schema)** — reads the friction tier + comments + agent-memory candidates + the decision log; the adjudicator's write verbs are `storytree proposal new … --pg` — the `tool` route's emission (ADR-0287 D1); a `proposal` is SEED-SCOPE, so it lands in the committed `knowledge.json` and the ADR-0120/0263 export belongs in the same PR — and `storytree friction route --pg`, which sets `route`/`routeReason` and, via `--discharged-by <ref>`, optionally stamps `dischargedBy` — the DELIVERY signal recorded once the routed remedy has LANDED (a PR number, an ADR id, or an `asset:` pointer), so a shipped remedy stops looking like a never-built one. **The stamp has no stamp-only path, and that is its fence:** `--reason` is required on EVERY invocation and `routeReason` is overwritten wholesale, so stamping an item adjudicated earlier means re-supplying its entire existing `routeReason` — read the current value out first and pass it back verbatim via `--reason @<file>` (the `@path` form is resolved for `--reason`, so multi-line prose survives the shell), never a fresh summary; the per-route authors write their artifacts through the standard Library boundary (`artifact new|edit --pg`), never this process directly. **Repo/CI** — the `adr` route scaffolds a born-`proposed` ADR via `storytree adr new --pg` (`adr-health` validates its edges); `check:friction-drain` reads the live store where reachable (local gates) and SKIPs in DB-free CI, like `check:agents-sync` — so the standing adjudicator duty, not CI, is the primary drain. **Story tree** — `asset:story-author` READS the `tool` route's proposal and authors the capability from it; no status is written here, and it writes no Library artifact (ADR-0287 D2). No verdict is signed by this process — the owner ratifies friction-born ADRs through the existing OQ→ADR flow.
statement: Drain a friction item by answering the ordered 7-question gate into its `routeReason` (question 1 — the evidence SUPPORTS the claim, not merely exists — is the anchor), then route it: `nothing` archives with a tombstone, `edit-existing`/`principle`/`guardrail` render into future guidance so they carry MANDATORY corpus-investigator verification, `process`/`definition` land on the reference tier, `adr` is a born-`proposed` ADR that IS the owner escalation (with the friction→ADR alignment check), `tool` EMITS a `proposal` — the adjudicator writes the remedy, the item cites it, and story-author CONSUMES it when authoring the capability (ADR-0287 D1/D2) — the drain is aged, bounded (K≈3 oldest routable per pre-merge pass), and fail-closed at a ceiling delegated to `check:friction-drain`, and no count or age ever decides what graduates.
provenance:
Authored 2026-07-07 as ADR-0168 increment 5 (the friction feedback loop's PROCEDURE). Derived from ADR-0168 D5 (the 7-question gate + the route→executor table + verification-proportional-to-blast-radius + the friction→ADR alignment check) and D4 (aged/bounded/fail-closed drain) per ADR-0034 §2 / ADR-0154 — a `process` makes NO new policy, so the RULE lives in `asset:friction-justification-bar` (the evidence floor) + ADR-0168, and on any disagreement the cited ADR wins. The sibling of the ADR-0095 memory-graduation pass (same judgment, a different signal source, read by the same adjudicator). Consumers: graduation-synthesist (chairs it), librarian-curator (the bounded pre-merge drain). Grounded also in the anti-slop corpus — `signal-and-noise`, `edit-first-curation`, `reference-dont-restate`, `stateless-vs-stateful-graduation`, the ADR-0024 blind-reconstruction test. The `--discharged-by` delivery stamp and its fence were added by the librarian pass 2026-07-30, pairing the affordance with its fence (`asset:pair-the-fence-with-the-affordance`): the flag shipped in the CLI (PR #1027) without the corpus ever learning it exists, so the process describing the adjudicator's one write verb described a verb that had grown a second effect. Both halves were measured in source this pass rather than taken from the PR prose — `--reason` is mandatory and `routeReason` is assigned wholesale (`packages/cli/src/friction.ts` `routeFriction`), and `--reason` IS run through the `@path` resolver (`resolveAtPathValue`, `packages/cli/src/commands.ts`), so the stated remedy is verified rather than plausible. No new policy (ADR-0034 §2): the deciding ADR is ADR-0168 D5, already cited, and the stamp is an extension of that same adjudication write.

A ninth failure mode — sweeping only the behavioural floor at question 3 — was added by the librarian pass 2026-08-01, from a defect measured in that same pass's own drain and NOT from a filed friction item. No new policy (ADR-0034 §2): the RULE is `asset:edit-first-curation`'s and is already unqualified (*the closest existing artifact*, no tier named), so what is recorded here is an observed way this PROCEDURE narrows it, plus the `routeReason` content that makes the narrowing visible — which step 1 question 3 already asks for. Evidence, verified at this seat rather than taken from the drain's report: `asset:verification-decay-detection`'s failure modes do state the convenience-wrapper rule (the load-and-compare wrapper that hands back the comparison and discards the load), so the `principle` route's "no existing artifact states this" was false when written. The load-bearing half is the second finding: the corpus-investigator verification this process already mandates on guidance-rendering routes did NOT catch it, because a verifier given the same tier scope reproduces the scope defect rather than refuting it — so the existing *skipping corpus-investigator verification* failure mode above must not be read as covering this one. The complementary floor-side move, naming the five guidance-bearing tiers in `asset:edit-first-curation`'s own Approach, was deliberately NOT made here: a `pattern` is behavioural-floor content and authoring it is the `guidance-curator`'s seat (this process's own route table: *edit-existing → librarian edits, guidance-curator if it touches the behavioural floor*). Escalated to the orchestrator instead of enacted.

Corrected 2026-08-03 (ADR-0139 in-place correction) for ADR-0287, which amends ADR-0168 D5's `tool` route row: `tool` now EMITS a `proposal` and the friction item cites it, so every route names the artifact kind its executor writes. The route→executor table, the ceremony lead, step 7's scope-of-the-job clause, the Surfaces write-verb list, and Verification are corrected in place rather than superseded — the DECISION did not change, the one route that could not honour ADR-0168 D2's routed lifecycle ("route set, output cited in `references`") now can. No new policy (ADR-0034 §2): the deciding ADR is ADR-0287, cited above. Two points are recorded as FORCED rather than chosen, so a later pass does not re-open them — the route ENUM is unchanged (no ninth route; 125 live rows carry `route: "tool"`), and the ADJUDICATOR holds the pen because `asset:story-author` is fail-closed fenced to `stories/**` and literally cannot write a Library artifact. This correction was DELIBERATELY deferred by the ADR-0287 session until the verb existed: instructing adjudicators to run `storytree proposal new` before it shipped is `asset:pair-the-fence-with-the-affordance` backwards. Verified in source on this pass rather than taken from the ADR's prose — the refusal, the store-resolved citation, and the `--proposal`-is-tool-only fence are in `packages/cli/src/friction.ts` (`routeFriction`), and the scaffolder in `packages/cli/src/proposal.ts`. At that pass ADR-0287 D3's `check:proposal-drain` and D4's targeted backfill were both DECIDED and NOT YET BUILT, so nothing written there claimed a delivery gate existed.

Corrected again 2026-08-03 — a SECOND pass the same day (ADR-0139 in-place correction), because ADR-0287 D3 SHIPPED between them: `check:proposal-drain` is built and wired into `pnpm gate` (`packages/cli/src/proposal-drain.ts`, the pure DB-free core; `check-proposal-drain.ts`, the live-read shell; `proposal-citation.ts`, the shared `asset:` token rule now used by BOTH the gate's bulk scan and `friction.ts`'s write-path citation fence). Verification's "decided and not yet built" was true when written that morning and false by that evening — the deferral the paragraph above records as deliberate, now discharged. The DECISION did not change, so this is a correction and NOT a supersede. No new policy (ADR-0034 §2): the deciding ADR is ADR-0287 D3 and the ceiling's shape is entirely its — recurrence-driven, with NO tunable number to raise, so the only discharge is the remedy landing and being stamped. What is ADDED here is the single thing newly actionable at this seat: parking a proposal now carries a live consequence for a later session's gate, which is exactly the obligation ADR-0287 opened and the reason the question-3/7 SCOPE prose belongs in the proposal IN FULL rather than thinned to clear the emission fence. Semantics were verified in source on this pass rather than taken from the PR prose — the strictly-`>` day comparison, the same-day WARN, the uncited-can-never-red and undated-never-red carve-outs, and `dischargedBy` as the discharge are all in `evaluateProposalDrain` (`proposal-drain.ts`), and the SKIP paths in the shell. A SECOND false claim surfaced on re-reading the artifact and was corrected in the same pass: the *Reading a `tool` routing as the delivery* failure mode asserted, in the present tense, that routing to `tool` "satisfies the loop's ONLY fail-closed gate" — true on 2026-08-02, false the moment D3 shipped, and the more dangerous of the two because a reader would have taken it for current mechanics rather than history. It is re-tensed to the measurement it describes, and the mode is NARROWED rather than retired: the delivery gate reds only on RECURRENCE, so a `tool` remedy whose trap nobody happens to re-hit still delivers nothing and nothing complains — ADR-0287's explicitly accepted risk, recorded as residue rather than treated as a defect to fix here. ADR-0287 D4's targeted backfill is STILL not built and is stated as pending above rather than quietly dropped.
description: The PROCEDURE for draining the friction worklist (ADR-0168 D5): run each routable friction item through the ordered 7-question gate, answer into `routeReason`, and route it to nothing / edit-existing / principle-or-guardrail / process / definition / adr / tool with verification proportional to blast radius. Makes NO new policy — the RULE is `asset:friction-justification-bar` + ADR-0168; on any disagreement the cited ADR wins. Read before adjudicating friction.
failureModes:
- **Taking evidence that merely EXISTS as evidence that SUPPORTS** — the anchor failure (D5 question 1): a real log cited for a claim it actually contradicts (a cold-start log for 'always `db:up` first', which contradicts ADR-0162). Spot-verify; spawn corpus-investigator on any guidance-rendering route.
- **Skipping corpus-investigator verification on a guidance-rendering route** — `principle`/`guardrail`/`edit-existing` render into every future session; a confabulated lesson atop real evidence (the STALE-benchmark hazard, ADR-0168 Calibration) self-reinforces once written. The verification is mandatory, not optional, precisely because the blast radius is total.
- **Minting a friction-born ADR born `accepted`** — batch adjudication is never 'owner-directed in this conversation' (ADR-0110), so a friction-born ADR is ALWAYS `proposed` and the owner ratifies. Born-accepted here would forge the ratification the whole loop routes to the owner.
- **Drafting around a contradiction with a load-bearing ADR** — the alignment check (d) HALTS on a contradiction with an accepted load-bearing ADR as an owner escalation; reconciling it silently in the draft hides an owner fork.
- **Draining the whole worklist per merge** — the bounded K≈3 rule exists so the drain scales with landing rate and parallel passes don't clobber the same artifact; a full-worklist drain per merge re-creates the same-artifact race and the archive-mill risk.
- **Adjudicating your own homework** — routability requires the item be filed by ANOTHER branch and aged ≥1 session; the filer adjudicating its own item defeats the aging fence.
- **Rubber-stamping `nothing` to clear the ceiling (the archive mill)** — the biggest residual risk (ADR-0168 Consequences): if a board session archives to clear `check:friction-drain` rather than to learn, the loop performs instead of learning. The Success-measures tripwires (route-nothing share near 0% or 100%, recurrence not extinguishing) exist to catch exactly this — the adjudicator watches them.
- **Treating a friction-born artifact as un-questionable** — contradicting it with new evidence is first-class friction (D6), not defection; reading it as non-adherence makes a wrong graduated rule self-sealing.
- **Stamping a landed remedy with a freshly-written `--reason`** — `friction route` demands `--reason` on every call and replaces `routeReason` wholesale; there is no stamp-only path, so adding `--discharged-by` to an already-adjudicated item OVERWRITES the adjudication that justified its route. On a board-drained item that is the entire multi-layer justification, and `friction` is not a seed-scope kind — the live row is the ONLY copy, so git cannot recover it. Read the existing `routeReason` out first and pass it back byte-for-byte with `--reason @<file>` in the same call.
- **Sweeping only the behavioural floor at question 3** — `asset:edit-first-curation` says *the closest existing artifact*, unqualified, but the tiers an adjudicator reaches for are the floor ones (`principle`/`guardrail`/`pattern`), and a rule can be stated just as completely — or more completely — in a `process` or a `definition`. Measured 2026-08-01: `convenience-wrapper-hides-the-substrate-health-its-caller-must-guard-on` was routed `principle` on "no existing artifact states this", while the rule was already stated, and more fully, in `asset:verification-decay-detection`'s failure modes. The corpus-investigator commissioned to verify it is NOT a net for this: given the same tier scope it independently repeated the sweep and also returned UNAUTHORED, reproducing the defect rather than catching it — only the authoring sweep across all five guidance-bearing tiers found it. The narrowing is invisible after the fact, because a sweep of three tiers and a sweep of five read identically in `routeReason` as "searched, nothing found"; naming the tiers actually swept is what makes it visible, and is already what question 3's *the search and its result go in `routeReason`* asks for.

- **Reading a `tool` routing as the delivery** — the whole reason ADR-0287 exists. `check:friction-drain` counts OPEN items, so routing to `tool` ARCHIVED the item and satisfied what was THEN the loop's only fail-closed gate while nothing was built; measured 2026-08-02, `tool` delivered 6 of 125 while carrying 56% of all routed signal, and `grep -rn '"tool"' packages/cli/src/check-*.ts` returned ZERO matches — nothing downstream read the route at all. The worked example is the export/corpus-gate surface: five `tool` items across four board passes (2026-07-28 → 07-30), three of them independently instructing "build the three as ONE capability unit", zero stories authored, then three MORE filings from three different branches on 2026-08-01, all tombstoned as duplicates of a remedy nobody owned. Adjudication worked flawlessly for five days and produced nothing. The proposal is what carries the obligation past the routing; writing a thin one to clear the fence recreates the failure in a new costume, so the SCOPE paragraph belongs in it in full. As of 2026-08-03 BOTH mechanical ends are closed — the emission fence (ADR-0287 D1) and the delivery gate (D3, `check:proposal-drain`) — so `check:friction-drain` is no longer the only fail-closed gate this route answers to. The failure mode is NARROWED, not retired, and the residue is worth naming precisely: the delivery gate reds only on RECURRENCE, so a `tool` remedy whose trap nobody happens to re-hit still delivers nothing and nothing complains — ADR-0287's explicitly accepted risk, failing in the quiet direction rather than the noisy one. Two gates now watch this route; neither of them is the judgement that the remedy was worth owning, and that judgement is still this seat's.
verification: Machine-checked only at the edges (ADR-0168 D7): the `friction new` capture validator (evidence present + concrete, cap-3, refs resolve) and schema `.strict()` fence what enters; `check:friction-drain` fail-closed at the ceiling gates QUEUE HYGIENE where the store is reachable (SKIPs in DB-free CI); `adr-health` enforces the `adr` route's declared edges; and the `tool` route is fail-closed on its EMISSION — `friction route --route tool` refuses until the item cites a live `proposal` (ADR-0287 D1), the ref being RESOLVED against the store rather than pattern-matched, so a dangling citation cannot satisfy it. That fence checks that a remedy was PARKED, never that it was built: the delivery signal itself is ADR-0287 D3's recurrence-driven `check:proposal-drain`, BUILT 2026-08-03 and wired into `pnpm gate` — local only, SKIPping offline / no creds / DB-unreachable exactly like its `check:friction-drain` sibling, so CI never enforces it and the standing obligation does. **What that changes at this seat: a proposal you park is no longer inert.** It goes RED on a LATER session's gate the moment a friction item citing it gains a `reinforcedBy` entry dated after the proposal's `createdAt` — the trap demonstrably bit someone again. The comparison is day-granular and strictly `>`, so same-day is a WARN (a day stamp cannot order the two) and the session that parked a proposal can never red itself on it. There is NO tunable ceiling number to raise, so the only discharge is the real one: the remedy LANDS and the source friction is stamped `storytree friction route <id> --route tool --reason @<file> --discharged-by "<PR / ADR / asset ref>" --pg` — the same single write fenced in Surfaces and the failure modes above (`--reason` mandatory, `routeReason` overwritten wholesale), so read the existing `routeReason` out and pass it back verbatim rather than re-summarising it. Two shapes stay deliberately quiet and are reported rather than hidden: an open proposal NO friction cites can never red (it has no source to be reinforced), and an undated row is a substrate gap, never a breach. ADR-0287 D4's targeted backfill of proposals for still-live `tool` items remains decided and not yet built. The GATE ITSELF — the seven questions, routing, reinforce-vs-new, tombstoning, owner-escalation judgment — is adjudicator judgment, never arithmetic (worth is never a threshold). The corpus-investigator verification on guidance-rendering routes is the adjudicator's own honesty check that the evidence supports the claim before it renders. Recurrence extinction (the routed trap stops re-appearing) is the standing success signal the adjudicator watches; a routed item that keeps recurring means the loop produced bloat, not learning.

title: Affected-only PR test scope
description: How a pull request's CI test scope narrows to the changed workspace projects plus their dependents, what forces the full suite instead, where the decision is readable, and the post-merge full run that backstops an under-selection.
statement: On a pull request, `pnpm ci:affected` classifies the merge commit's own diff and narrows CI's typecheck and test to the changed workspace projects plus their pnpm dependents — falling open to the full suite on anything the dependency graph cannot see — while every merged tree still gets exactly one full-suite proof.
trigger: CI runs the classifier itself, unconditionally, on every pull-request event into main — no session invokes it. A session runs this process by hand at three observable moments: reading WHY a PR's verify tested only some projects (ADR-0195's sanity-watch); landing a change that introduces a source or test read crossing a package boundary with no dependency edge behind it; and triaging a main that went red within minutes of an affected-only merge.
steps:
1. **CI classifies, PRs only.** In the `verify` job, after dependencies are installed, the `Affected scope (PRs only)` step runs `pnpm ci:affected` (the thin shell `packages/cli/src/ci-affected-main.ts`; the rules live in `ci-affected.ts`). It diffs the merge commit against its first parent — `git diff --name-only --no-renames HEAD^1 HEAD` on the `refs/pull/N/merge` checkout that `fetch-depth: 2` keeps the base tip available for — so the change set is exactly what the PR changes versus the base the merge was cut against, race-free against a moving main. pnpm's own `--filter "...[ref]"` git selection is deliberately NOT used: ONE diff source of truth, so the classifier and the selection can never disagree about what changed. Push and dispatch runs skip the step entirely and stay full.
2. **Read the decision off the run page, never infer it.** The step writes the scope to the job summary (`**Affected scope (ADR-0195):** …`) and logs `[ci:affected] mode=…` with the selected projects. The `verify` job then runs its typecheck and test steps with the emitted `pnpm_args` — `-r` for full, or a dependents-inclusive `--filter "...<name>"` chain that pnpm expands from the real workspace graph. `pnpm -r build` stays full at every scope, and every `check:` gate step stays unconditional.
3. **Know the four FULL triggers — the classifier is conservative by design.** Any changed file that is (a) outside `packages/*` / `apps/*` (`stories/**`, `docs/decisions/**`, `scripts/**`, `.github/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, the root manifest and tsconfig, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, the `web` gitlink); (b) under `apps/studio/data/**`, the corpus seed read across package boundaries; (c) any `package.json`, a workspace manifest being an input of the selection graph itself; or (d) inside `packages/` or `apps/` but mapping to no known workspace project — forces the full run. These are not caution for its own sake: several suites read files outside any declared dependency edge — cli's corpus guard over `stories/**`, the adr-health gates over `docs/decisions/**`, drive's node-build tests over `stories/**`, and library's and cli's tests over the corpus seed.
4. **Trust the fail-open, and read a MISSING step as red.** Not a pull-request event, a HEAD that is not a merge commit, a git failure, or any classifier error emits the full scope and exits 0 — narrowing is an optimisation, never a gate to fail. Only a crash early enough that the step's output was never written fails the step, and that fails CI visibly rather than passing a silently narrowed green.
5. **After an affected-only merge the backstop is the DISPATCHED full run, not a push run.** Every merged tree still gets one full-suite proof, but for an auto-merged PR that proof does not come from the push trigger: a `GITHUB_TOKEN` merge never starts a workflow (GitHub anti-recursion), so the automerge job dispatches a full run on main instead, skipped when the PR side already ran full. An under-selection therefore surfaces minutes after the merge that landed it and is fixed forward — ADR-0195's accepted trade, stated rather than hidden.
6. **A new cross-boundary read arrives with an edge or with an amendment — never alone.** If a change makes a package read a file that no dependency edge declares, either declare the edge, or amend ADR-0195 to add the path to the FULL triggers and pin the new trigger red→green in `ci-affected.test.ts`. Refining a classification rule is an amendment (`pnpm storytree adr new --pg`), never a quiet edit to the classifier — that is the single shape under which a narrowed PR can land red on main.
7. **Do not narrow the local gate to match.** `pnpm gate` stays full by decision; the full local mirror is exactly what makes the narrowed PR-side scope safe to trust, so only CI narrows.
surfaces:
- **Repo / CI** — `pnpm ci:affected` is the one entrypoint this process enacts, and it is CI-invoked rather than session-invoked: the `verify` job's pull-request-only `Affected scope` step runs it and reads its two outputs (`pnpm_args`, `mode`) to scope the typecheck and test steps that follow. It writes nothing to the repo or to any store; its entire output is two GitHub Actions channels — the step outputs the workflow consumes, and the job-summary line an operator reads. Running it outside a pull-request checkout is harmless and answers full.
- **Local gate** — `pnpm gate` is deliberately UNTOUCHED by this process: the local mirror runs the full suite at every scope, so a session never has to reason about selection before pushing.
- **Decision log** — ADR-0195 is the deciding policy and ADR-0022 the auto-merge invariant it amends; refining a classification rule is an amendment allocated through `pnpm storytree adr new --pg`, never an edit here or in the classifier.
- **Not this process:** the post-merge full-suite dispatch lives inside the automerge job, behind no operator command — there is no entrypoint to run it by hand, which is why it is described in the steps but named as no surface here.
failureModes:
- **Reading a green PR verify as a full-suite proof.** An affected-only run proves the changed projects plus their dependents, not the workspace. The full proof for that tree is the dispatched run that follows the merge; a scope line reading affected means the PR itself never carried one.
- **Expecting the push-to-main run to be the backstop.** It is not — and this was wrong in ADR-0195's own first wording, corrected the same day, before the mechanism ever gated a merge. `GITHUB_TOKEN`-caused events never trigger workflows, so auto-merged PRs, which is all of them, produce no push run at all. Verified against run history at the time: push runs fired for hand-merged PRs and for no bot-merged PR.
- **Introducing a cross-boundary read with neither an edge nor an amendment.** This is the one shape that makes an under-selection possible: a change that adds a file read crossing a package boundary while touching none of the FULL-trigger paths. It lands, main goes red, and the failure surfaces on a run nobody was watching.
- **Quietly refining a classification rule.** Every FULL trigger is pinned red→green in `ci-affected.test.ts` precisely so a narrowing edit cannot pass as a cleanup. Loosening one without amending ADR-0195 trades a stated invariant for an unstated one, and buys minutes of CI against a class of escape nothing else catches.
- **Narrowing the local gate to match CI.** The full local mirror is the redundancy that makes a narrowed PR-side scope safe; matching them removes exactly what the design is paying for and leaves the dispatched post-merge run as the only full proof.
- **Shipping an operator-facing entrypoint with no process behind it.** This artifact exists because ADR-0195 did that: `pnpm ci:affected` landed on 2026-07-14 with no `process` naming it, `check:surface-coverage` printed a WARN and exited 0, and the process↔entrypoint bijection ADR-0154 built that gate to assert stayed broken on main for a fortnight without failing anything, local or CI.
verification: `ci-affected.test.ts` pins every FULL trigger and every fail-open path red→green, so a classification rule cannot be loosened silently. `pnpm check:surface-coverage` (ADR-0154) asserts the bijection in both directions — that this process names a real entrypoint, and that `pnpm ci:affected` is named by some process rather than sitting on the orphan worklist — and reds the gate above the drain ceiling in `packages/cli/src/surface-coverage-drain.ts`, whose orphan axis is tightened to zero in the same increment that authors this artifact, so a regression here is a red gate rather than a warning. The dispatched post-merge full run is the machine backstop for an under-selection that got through. What nothing checks: that a session actually performed the sanity-watch on a run page, and that a new cross-boundary read arrived with a dependency edge or an amendment rather than alone. Both stay judgement, and step 6 is where they are exercised.
provenance: Derived from ADR-0195 (which amends ADR-0022) as the process-tier projection ADR-0154 requires of a load-bearing way-of-working ADR. Authored 2026-07-28 to drain the single orphan `check:surface-coverage` had carried since 2026-07-14, when ADR-0195 added the `ci:affected` entrypoint and authored no process for it; the same increment lowered that check's orphan ceiling from 1 to 0. Consumers: any session reading a PR's CI scope, and any change that adds a cross-package file read.

title: Arc
oneLine: The initiative overlay: a named multi-story owner intent tracked through an increment log to a closed end-state — upstream of stories and ADRs by provenance, containing plans, rendered as "Epic" in the studio.
whatItIs:
The fourth grouping tier ADR-0002 parked, returned as an **overlay, not a tier** (ADR-0183 D1): an `arc` names one owner initiative that spans multiple stories, ADRs, and plans, and tracks it to a closed end-state. Nothing proof-related rolls up to it — the story remains the top proof grain (no verdict, no UAT, no rollup on an arc).

An arc is live-canonical like every non-agent kind (ADR-0023) and ceremony-light by construction. It is BORN through `storytree arc new --title "…" --intent <text|@file> --end-state <text|@file> --pg`, which takes those three substantive fields and stamps the mechanical ones (id, description, timestamps, `lifecycle: active`) — an arc is never hand-authored as doc JSON. Thereafter its only authored mutations are slow — intent changes (`storytree arc edit`), and entries appended to its structured `increments` landing log at each merge ceremony (`storytree arc increment add`; date, PR#, outcome — what landed, halted, or was re-planned) — until `storytree arc close` records the end-state as reached (ADR-0239). That log is the durable residue that survives plan pruning.

Every containment edge lives on the CHILD (D3): a plan is born citing its arc (`arcRef`), and an ADR or story gains an optional, immutable `arc:` provenance stamp at creation (`storytree adr new --arc <id>`; story frontmatter). The arc reveals its plans, stories, and ADRs by derived query (`storytree arc show <id> --pg`), never by editing the arc when a child is born. Upstream means provenance and intent, not authority: the arc never overrides story-author on WHAT or the decision log on WHY.

The studio displays the kind as **"Epic"** (a display alias only — the kind key, CLI, and refs use `arc` exclusively).
provenance: The clause distinguishing the ADR-0183 D4 surface ban from the residency of an owner-approved artifact was added 2026-08-01 discharging `friction-visual-contract-lived-outside-arc-context` (the ADR-0168 guidance-routed friction drain). The rule itself is stated once, as `asset:an-owner-approved-reference-is-repo-resident`, and cited here rather than restated (`asset:reference-dont-restate`); it landed as a principle rather than as arc-only guidance because its subject is the owner's approval, not the arc — the routeReason's execution fence handed that tier call to guidance-curator. This pointer sits on the arc because the arc body is where the wrong inference was measurably made: the ban told the session what must NOT go in the arc, said nothing about where the approved renderable must therefore live, and the arc consequently kept the gauge semantics as prose while the approved playable composition evaporated with the machine-local path it was passed on.
description: The initiative overlay (ADR-0183): a named multi-story owner intent tracked through an increment log to a closed end-state — upstream of stories and ADRs by provenance, rendered as "Epic" in the studio.
whatItIsNot: Not a proof unit — nothing rolls up to it; health is judged at the story (ADR-0010). Not durable guidance — lessons still graduate out through ADR-0095/ADR-0168; an arc holds state and pointers only, and implementation surface is banned on it (ADR-0183 D4 — surface lives in anchored, disposable plans). That ban is on the PROSE, not on the artifact: a design reference the owner has APPROVED is committed to a repo path and the arc carries the pointer to it, never a machine-local one — an approved renderable passed as a visualization path does not survive the repull, and the next session rebuilds a different surface from the prose alone (`asset:an-owner-approved-reference-is-repo-resident`). Not a `plan` — the plan is the disposable choreography for ONE increment of an arc. Not mandatory — one-session, one-unit work stays arc-less (D6): the trigger is work that spans sessions or parallel lanes.

title: Plan
oneLine: The disposable, git-anchored choreography for one increment of an arc: unit decomposition with proof routes, dependency order, parallel lanes, budgets, and traps — freshness-checked at consumption, consumed once, then retired.
whatItIs:
A `plan` (ADR-0183 D2) hands one arc increment from planning intelligence to executing sessions as an inspectable artifact: the unit decomposition (story/capability ids, each with its proof route — `--real` red→green, glue per ADR-0158, or operator-attested), dependency order, parallel lanes (which units are independent, expected file surface per lane as fence hints, contention warnings), budgets in turn-cap vocabulary (ADR-0130), known traps, and escalation points.

It is the first EPHEMERAL kind (`EPHEMERAL_KINDS` in `packages/library`): live-store-only, never in `knowledge.json`, ignored by `export-corpus`, `sync-corpus`, and the `check:corpus-sync` gate. Born citing its arc (`arcRef`, D3) and pinned to the git commit it was planned against (`anchor.sha`). Consumption begins with a mechanical freshness check — `storytree plan check <id> --pg` git-logs the paths the plan names since its anchor; drift past threshold means re-plan, not repair. Once consumption starts a plan is never edited — re-planning is cheap by construction, so supersede (`status`: draft → ready → consumed / superseded / retired). Consumed plans are prunable; the owning arc's increment log is what endures.

**Naming the paths.** The freshness check has no notion of granularity: the extractor behind `plan check` (`extractPlanPaths`, `@storytree/cli`) harvests EVERY backtick path-token from five body fields — `objective`, `decomposition`, `lanes`, `budgets`, `traps` — so a path mentioned in passing in a trap note is watched exactly like a lane's fence hint, and the verdict SUMS commits across every named path against a default threshold of 0. The path set is therefore authored deliberately, and it can be wrong in two OPPOSITE directions — which matters because each is the tempting fix for the other. Too BROAD: a directory matches its whole subtree, so a single orthogonal commit under it reads as drift and forces the mandated re-plan (D2), and naming a leaf *plus* its enclosing directory counts that one commit twice. Name the narrow material file whose change would genuinely invalidate the decomposition, never the directory that contains it. Too NARROW: trimming is not the remedy — a plan naming no paths gets a VACUOUS verdict, explicitly not a green, and a real coupling left unnamed breaks a lane instead of tripping a check. Completeness is judged across every coupling graph, not just the import graph: much of the gate is disk SCANNERS keyed on paths — the coverage checks walk `stories/` and read each capability's registered `proof.real.testFile`, `check:boundaries` gathers `proof.real.sourceFile` and literal source globs the same way, `check:manifest` reads `git ls-files`, and the seed-sync checks read the corpus — and a path coupling leaves no import edge to find. A DELETION plan is the sharp case: inventory those disk-scanning registrations alongside the import graph, or the miss surfaces late, as a red gate on the deletion branch after the lane is already committed. Per path, ask both questions: would a commit here really invalidate the decomposition, and would a commit I did *not* name break a lane?

Authored by the `planner` agent (D5); consumed by the session-orchestrator, which validates freshness, takes lanes via the existing claim machinery (ADR-0121/0142), executes, and records the outcome on the arc.
provenance: The "Naming the paths" discipline was added 2026-08-01 discharging two guidance-routed friction items in one edit (the ADR-0168 drain), landed together because they are the two opposite errors on a single axis and each reads as the fix for the other. `plan-broad-paths-trip-threshold-zero`: `library-tech-tree-overlay-plan-1` named `apps/studio/src` and `apps/studio/src/components/` among its paths, ONE orthogonal commit produced "DRIFTED — 3 commit(s) touched 3 of 7 named path(s)" at threshold 0, and the mandated re-plan reproduced the same 7-increment decomposition for ~117k tokens / ~8 min. `friction-deletion-plans-miss-disk-scanning-proof-couplings`: a deletion plan's import-graph inventory missed `stories/**` proof registrations that are read from disk, halting a lane at a red gate mid-wave (~1h wall-clock plus an unplanned re-sequence). Both routed `edit-existing` to this definition, and both stay here as authoring discipline for the kind — alongside the born-through-`arc new` and never-edited-once-consumed rules already in this body — rather than becoming a principle or a guardrail. The enforcer test refuses a guardrail: `storytree plan check` REPORTS drift rather than refusing a badly-scoped path set, and the gate catches a missed coupling only late, on the deletion branch, so nothing deterministic sits between the author and either failure. Five-tier edit-first sweep (principle / guardrail / pattern / process / definition) found no existing home — 'watched path', 'path granularity', 'broad directory', 'narrow file', 'import graph' and 'disk-scan' returned zero hits across all five tiers — with these named rejections: `asset:anchor-implementation-surface`, the nearest principle, points the OPPOSITE way (it tells a DURABLE doc to name the owning surface — coarser, not narrower) and has been given a matching scope fence there instead of being transferred here; `asset:prose-names-a-set-it-never-checked` is adjacent on inventory completeness but concerns an unchecked enumeration, not a derivation method structurally blind to a coupling class; `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` is the same family one level up (a check must be able to see what it fences) but says nothing about how a plan names its paths; `asset:turn-budget-keys-on-assert-surface` is the precedent SHAPE (a plan-authoring heuristic keyed on the wrong dimension) rather than a home. Mechanism verified while authoring, against `extractPlanPaths` / `planCommand` in `@storytree/cli` and the disk gatherers behind `check:coverage` and `check:boundaries` — including that the verdict sums commits across named paths, so a leaf nested under a named parent is double-counted, and that a pathless plan returns VACUOUS rather than FRESH.
description: The disposable, git-anchored execution choreography for one increment of an arc (ADR-0183): the first ephemeral, Postgres-only kind — freshness-checked at consumption, consumed once, then retired.
whatItIsNot: Not durable — no git history, no seed, prunable once consumed; anything worth keeping graduates to the arc's increment log or the Library. Not a decision or a work definition — a design fork discovered while planning exits to an ADR, and hierarchy changes route through story-author; a plan only choreographs work that is already defined. Not mandatory — a one-session, one-unit piece of work stays planless (D6); mandatory plans would be plan-theater. Not reachable from remote (web/VM) sessions — plans are live-store data, and such a session cannot run the Cloud SQL connector (client-mTLS cannot cross its TLS-terminating proxy; ADR-0250 D1, narrowed by ADR-0258 D2). The fence is the connector, not a blocked port and not database access in general: an HTTP front door would reach them (ADR-0259), and none is deployed.

why: Surface data is the fastest-rotting prose in the corpus: files move, packages dissolve, and a stale file list misleads silently — the reader cannot tell truth from rot (the exact failure ADR-0139 evicts execution prose from ADR bodies for). In an anchored artifact the same list is honest: `anchor.sha` makes staleness DETECTABLE — git-log the named paths since the anchor, the proof tier's source-drift move applied to intentions — and disposability makes the response cheap: re-plan, don't repair.
title: Implementation surface is written only into anchored, disposable artifacts
statement: Implementation surface — file lists, package paths, expected edit footprints, ordering over concrete code — may only be written into artifacts that are both git-ANCHORED (pinned to the commit they were authored against, freshness-checked mechanically at consumption) and DISPOSABLE (superseded on drift, never repaired); a durable artifact — an ADR body, story, principle, definition, or arc — never carries it (ADR-0183 D4).
howToApply: About to write a file path, package list, or edit footprint into a durable doc? Move it into the anchored disposable tier — today a `plan` (ADR-0183), checked by `storytree plan check <id> --pg` — and leave the durable doc with intent, outcomes, and pointers. The test: would this list still be true in a month, and would the reader notice if it weren't? When a durable doc must name code (a guardrail's enforcement point, a techstack constraint), name the owning SURFACE — a command, a package, a gate — never an enumerated file list. That coarsening rule is the DURABLE side only, and it INVERTS inside the anchored tier: a plan's named paths are the very thing its freshness check git-logs, so naming the owning directory there makes any orthogonal commit in the subtree read as drift — see `asset:plan` for the path-set discipline that applies once surface has been moved. Moving surface out of a durable doc is likewise a rule about the PROSE, not about the artifact: a renderable or binary the owner approved is still committed and pointed at (`asset:an-owner-approved-reference-is-repo-resident`).
provenance: The two closing scope fences on "How to apply" were added 2026-08-01 during the ADR-0168 guidance-routed friction drain; the principle itself is unchanged and remains correct for durable docs. The first discharges part of `plan-broad-paths-trip-threshold-zero`, whose adjudication flagged this principle as BOTH the nearest existing guidance and a wrong-way pointer for the anchored tier: read without a scope, "name the owning SURFACE — never an enumerated file list" licenses exactly the broad directory that makes a plan's freshness check trip on orthogonal commits, and a naive transfer of the durable-side rule was explicitly warned against. The second was added while authoring `asset:an-owner-approved-reference-is-repo-resident` (discharging `friction-visual-contract-lived-outside-arc-context`), where the observed failure was completing a correct "surface does not go in the arc body" into an incorrect "so the approved renderable lives nowhere". Both fences name where the rule stops and cite the artifact that owns the other side rather than restating it here (`asset:reference-dont-restate`, `asset:pair-the-fence-with-the-affordance`).
description: File lists, package paths, and edit footprints rot fast: they may only live in artifacts that pin the git SHA they were true at and are superseded (never repaired) on drift — a durable doc carries intent and pointers only.

title: planner
description: The plan author (ADR-0183 D5): expensive-tier planning intelligence that reads an arc and the current tree and writes ONE git-anchored, disposable plan for the next increment — it choreographs, and never decides or defines work: design forks exit to an ADR, hierarchy changes route to story-author.
oneLine: The plan author (ADR-0183 D5): expensive-tier planning intelligence that reads an arc and the current tree and writes ONE git-anchored, disposable plan for the next increment — it choreographs, and never decides or defines work: design forks exit to an ADR, hierarchy changes route to story-author.
role: The separable planning half of the model-tier economics (ADR-0183): planning intelligence and execution intelligence are different spends, so an expensive planner authors the choreography as an inspectable artifact that cheaper orchestrating sessions consume. Given an arc (the owner's initiative), it studies the arc's increment log, the work hierarchy, the decision log, and recent movement on the surfaces involved, then authors ONE `plan` for the next increment: unit decomposition with proof routes, dependency order, parallel lanes with fence-hint file surface, budgets in turn-cap vocabulary (ADR-0130), traps, and escalation points. The plan is the handoff contract — reviewable before any `--real` build burns turns, reusable across N parallel sessions each taking a different lane. It authors plans and NOTHING else: it never decides (a design fork discovered while planning is surfaced, not settled), never defines work (story/capability changes route through story-author), and never executes.
outcome: One valid `plan` document upserted to the live store per invocation — born citing its arc (`arcRef`), anchored to the commit it was planned against (`anchor.sha` + date), body complete (objective, decomposition with a proof route per unit, lanes when parallel, budgets and traps when known), `status` left `draft` for review or flipped `ready` when the spawning session asked for a consumable plan. Zero writes anywhere else: no code, no stories, no ADRs, no arc edits (the increment log is appended by the landing session, not the planner).
tools: Read-only repo access (Read/Grep/Glob; `git log` / `git rev-parse` to anchor the plan and to check recent movement on the surfaces it names); Library CLI reads (`storytree library …`, `storytree tree`, `storytree adr list`, `storytree arc show <id> --pg`); exactly one write surface: `storytree library artifact new --file <plan.json> --pg` (plans are live-only — no DB, no plan). Least-authority: nothing else.
workflow:
**Session start.** Confirm the target arc and that the live DB is reachable (plans are live-only; no DB → stop and report). Pull the arc and its derived children (`storytree arc show <id> --pg`) and read the increment log — what landed, what halted, what was re-planned.

1. **Scope one increment** — the minimum coherent next step toward the arc's end state (slow growth), sized to hand off.
2. **Decompose into provable units** — by the routing filter ("does this piece have an isolatable red→green test?"): `--real` red→green, glue (ADR-0158), or operator-attested; name each unit's story/capability id and order by dependency.
3. **Declare the lanes** — which units are independent, the expected file surface per lane as fence hints for the takers, and where lanes contend.
4. **Budget and traps** — budget each unit in turn-cap vocabulary (ADR-0130), sizing by the ASSERT SURFACE (files the leaf authors × contracts it covers) rather than file size; known traps on this surface, and the points where the executor halts for the owner.
5. **Anchor** — pin `anchor.sha` to the commit planned against (current `origin/main` HEAD) with today's date.
6. **Write the plan** — `storytree library artifact new --file <plan.json> --pg`, then stop. One plan per invocation; the orchestrator consumes it (freshness check → claim lanes → execute → append the arc increment at landing).

**Stop condition:** the plan is written, or a blocker is surfaced. A design fork or hierarchy gap discovered mid-plan is recorded as an escalation point (or halts the plan when load-bearing) — never settled inline.
escalation: A design fork worth an ADR: name it in the plan's escalation points and surface it to the spawning session — the planner never runs `adr new` or settles it. A gap in the work hierarchy (a unit with no story/capability home): route to story-author. An arc whose intent no longer matches the tree, or an increment that cannot be decomposed into provable units: surface to the owner via the session. DB unreachable: stop — a plan that cannot persist is never parked on disk as a workaround (plans are ephemeral live-store data, ADR-0183 D2).

steps:
1. **Recognise the refusal as fail-closed correctness, not a flake.** tsx STRIPS types with no typecheck, so a runtime test of a type-only change runs GREEN at HEAD; a bare re-run fails identically (the spec steers the leaf back to the same type flip). Note the proof's `typecheck` wall runs at GREEN, not at CONFIRM_RED, so it cannot supply the red.
2. **Route to `story-author` as a proof-approach refinement** of the cap spec (Guidance / Integration test / contract wording). Keep the outcome, deps, proof config, and contract count frozen — this is a proof-shape fix, not a re-scope. Do NOT hand-hack the leaf's red→green (that self-exempts from the inner loop).
3. **Refine toward a RUNTIME WITNESS:** a runtime value ABSENT at HEAD whose introduction the RED test can assert — a write-boundary normalizer/validator (e.g. `normalizeCommentAnchor(raw): CommentAnchor` — accepts the new shape, strips dead fields, downgrades legacy/unknown to a safe default), a runtime valid-kinds list, or a guard. Often the cap's own outcome already implies the witness ("validates at the store's write boundary" ⇒ a normalizer; the studio `apiRouter.ts` `readAnchor` was the mirror precedent).
4. **Re-drive the build** (`storytree node build <cap> --real`): the witness's absence at HEAD is the observed RED; adding it is the GREEN.
title: A type-only RED needs a runtime witness
trigger: A `--real`/`--live` build fails at CONFIRM_RED with "requires an observed red (got 'green')" and the cap's intended change is TYPE-level — a union member swap (e.g. `kind: 'text'` → `'block'`), an interface field add/remove — proved by `node --import tsx --test` or vitest, i.e. a runtime run that never sees types.
surfaces:
- **The spine's CONFIRM_RED** — `packages/orchestrator/src/prove-it-gate.ts` / `phase-machine.ts` (the halted-is-never-a-pass / observed-red discipline).
- **Cap specs** — `stories/<story>/<cap>.md` proof frontmatter + Guidance (the surface story-author refines).
- **Runtime proof commands** — `node --import tsx --test` (packages) and vitest (apps/studio): both execute with types stripped, no typecheck at RED time.
statement: When a capability's intended RED is a pure type/shape change and its real proof runs under a runtime test command, the spine's CONFIRM_RED refusal ("requires an observed red (got 'green')") is fail-closed correctness, not a flake: the cap's proof approach must introduce a RUNTIME WITNESS — a runtime value absent at HEAD whose behaviour flips with the change (a write-boundary normalizer / validator / guard) — and that refinement is story-author's proof-approach edit, never a leaf hand-hack or an unchanged re-run.
provenance: Graduated from agent-memory 'type-only-red-needs-runtime-witness' on 2026-07-02 (ADR-0095): recorded when block-position-comment-anchor's first --real run failed closed at CONFIRM_RED (real-mr2124t5) and the fix — a write-boundary normalizer witness routed through story-author — proved the general rule for any type-only RED under a runtime proof.
description: A cap whose RED is a pure TypeScript type/shape change is invisible to a runtime test proof (tsx strips types), so CONFIRM_RED fails closed 'got green'; the fix is a runtime witness in the cap's proof approach, routed to story-author — never a bare retry or a leaf hand-hack.
failureModes:
- **Retrying the build unchanged** — it fails the same way every time; the spec steers the leaf to the same type flip.
- **Hand-hacking the leaf's red→green** — self-exempts from the inner loop; the fix belongs in the spec's proof approach.
- **Treating the CONFIRM_RED refusal as a spurious gate failure** and looking for a spine bug — the gate is doing exactly its job.
- **Expecting the `typecheck` wall to supply the red** — it runs at GREEN, not at CONFIRM_RED.
verification: The refined cap drives `--real` end-to-end: an OBSERVED red at HEAD (the witness's call throws / fails) and a signed PASS after GREEN. First confirmed on `block-position-comment-anchor` (library-review / ADR-0140): the first `--real` attempt (run real-mr2124t5, 2026-07-01) failed closed at CONFIRM_RED because the intended red was a pure anchor-type flip; the normalizer-witness refinement then earned the signed PASS.

why: A second route to the same place is rarely free and almost never neutral. It splits muscle memory — there are now two ways to learn, teach, and document, and the canonical one is no longer obvious. It doubles the surface that must be built, proven, and kept in sync, so the two paths drift and one silently rots. And it hides the intended route behind a choice that buys nothing: every reader and every future change pays for the duplication whether or not anyone uses the second way. What looks like added convenience is added cost, carried forever.
title: One way to do things
statement: A surface — UI, CLI, corpus, or workflow — should offer exactly ONE pathway to a given capability; a second pathway to the same destination is a defect until a very strong, explicitly stated justification earns it.
howToApply: Before adding a route to a capability that is already reachable, ask: does a pathway to this destination already exist? If so, the default is to REMOVE the new one and point at the canonical route — not to ship both. A second pathway clears the bar only on a structurally different context of use: a hard accessibility need, a genuinely different entry surface, an offline-versus-live split. 'It was easy to add here too', 'some users might prefer it', or plain convenience do NOT clear it. When a second pathway is justified, state the justification where it is introduced, so a later reader knows the duplication is deliberate and not an accident to be pruned. When in doubt, one way wins.
provenance: Owner-directed 2026-07-17 during the studio HUD-chrome walk (studio-hud-chrome-arc, ADR-0204): the HUD avatar menu's Library/Documents entries duplicated the forest map's library-drawer pathway to the same destination and were removed rather than kept as a second route. The owner stated it as a general principle — 'there should be one way to do things, and a second pathway needs very strong justification' — not a studio-specific note. Kin to `asset:reference-dont-restate` (the same one-canonical-thing discipline for guidance content) and `asset:deep-modules` (pay the interface cost only when the hidden work justifies it).
description: A surface should offer ONE pathway to a given capability; a second pathway to the same destination requires very strong, stated justification — duplicated affordances split muscle memory, double the maintenance and proof surface, and hide the canonical route.

title: probe
oneLine: A **probe** is the owner's working term (alias) for an **explorer subagent**: a read-only, disposable subagent sent out to answer one scoped question — find, verify, survey — and return a DIGEST (conclusions plus file:line pointers), never raw file dumps.
whatItIs: An alias, not a new mechanism. 'Send out probes' means: spawn read-only explorer/digest subagents — the WHERE-exploration-runs rule is `asset:delegate-exploration-to-digest-subagents` (multi-step exploration runs in a disposable subagent context, not the long-lived orchestrating session), and the probe itself behaves per `asset:exploration-principles` (pattern-over-enumeration, context-minimal, read-only). Concrete probe shapes: the generic `Explore` agent, a `corpus-investigator` (a single-claim verification probe returning a structured verdict), or any general read-only subagent explicitly asked for a digest. A probe's context is disposable: it absorbs the exploration volume and dies at digest-return; only the digest enters the expensive orchestrating context.
description: The owner's working term for an explorer subagent: a read-only, disposable subagent sent out to answer one scoped question and return a digest.
whatItIsNot: Not a builder: a probe never edits, writes, signs, or lands anything — mutating work routes through the inner loop or a write-scoped subagent, never a probe. Not the inner-loop leaf (which authors code under the prove-it-gate). And not a single targeted lookup — when the file or symbol is already known, one inline Read/Grep is cheaper than a probe.

title: in-session subagent
oneLine: A subagent spawned in-process by a running session's own Agent tool — starts immediately with no owner approval, is a CHILD of the spawning session, and dies if the parent's process exits.
whatItIs: A subagent a running session spawns itself, in-process, via its Agent (Task) tool — e.g. an `Agent({...})` call, or the desktop chat's scoped `spawn_glue_worker` / `spawn_story_author` MCP verbs. It STARTS IMMEDIATELY: no owner approval gate sits in front of it, the spawning session's own permission grants cover it. It is a CHILD of the spawning session — it shares its process lifetime, so it DIES if the parent session's process exits (an app restart, a closed terminal) — and its completion notification is delivered back to the spawning session, not directly to the owner: a top-level session that nests several has to act as a message bus/watchdog for stray notifications bubbling up from grandchildren. Right for: work that finishes WITHIN the current session and benefits from direct supervision — parallel design lanes (the art-asset designer-swarm, `asset:art-asset-designer-swarm`), read-only exploration/digest probes (`asset:delegate-exploration-to-digest-subagents`), curation passes (the librarian-curator spawn) — anything the spawning session will itself watch through to completion.
provenance: Named 2026-07-17 at the owner's direction to disambiguate the two delegation mechanisms sessions were blurring under the slang "chip off" (agent-coined, not owner-sacred) — ground truth observed on the forest-parcels arc, where an in-session subagent was used for work the owner expected as a session-cutting. Companion definition: `asset:session-cutting`.
description: A subagent spawned in-process by a running session's own Agent tool: it starts immediately with no owner approval, is a CHILD of the spawning session (it dies if the parent's process exits), and its completion notifications can leak to the top level — the mechanism for work that finishes within the session and benefits from direct supervision.
whatItIsNot: Not a **session-cutting** (`asset:session-cutting`) — the owner-approved, fresh top-level session with its own context, lifecycle, and `SessionStart` hooks, which survives the spawning session entirely. Reach for a cutting instead when the work must OUTLIVE the current session (a long-running arc-increment drive) or the owner wants an explicit approval click before it starts. Observed trap (2026-07-17, the forest-parcels arc): spawning an in-session subagent for a long-running drive the owner expected as an approval-gated cutting worked mechanically but skipped the owner's expected approval step, and a mid-flight app restart killed it outright.

title: session cutting
oneLine: The owner-approved delegation mechanism — a fresh top-level Claude Code session (own context, lifecycle, SessionStart hooks) launched via the desktop's `spawn_task` chip, surviving the proposing session entirely.
whatItIs:
A NEW, independent top-level Claude Code session — its own context window, its own process lifecycle, its own `SessionStart` hooks (worktree auto-provision, the claim-ledger anchor nudge) — created via the desktop app's `spawn_task` action: a clickable chip the OWNER approves before it launches. Named for the botanical **cutting**: a piece taken from a parent plant that roots and grows as its own independent plant, sharing lineage with the parent but none of its lifecycle — the proposing session can exit, restart, or die, and a session-cutting keeps running regardless. Right for: work that must OUTLIVE the proposing session (a long-running arc-increment drive, `asset:arc`); anything where the owner wants an explicit approval click as the launch/spend gate (`asset:human-owns-the-outer-loop`) before work starts running unattended; and **the driving that follows a decision when the deciding session's context is spent** — a session that has spent its context DECIDING (reserving and landing the ADRs and arc increments) hands the building to a cutting rather than continuing in-thread. The owner's words, 2026-07-27: *"you really should just be landing the adrs and arcs and then cutting a fresh session to drive"* — said after one thread landed four decision-log PRs (#964, #967, #971, #972) and kept offering to build next. The reason is orientation, not tidiness: a session that has spent its context arguing a design is the worst-oriented session to build it, and the long in-thread chain compounds — it landed four PRs with no librarian pass and paid the branch-dies-on-merge re-declare (ADR-0142) once per landing, which a fresh cutting gets for free at `SessionStart`. Naming the next increment is the hand-off; starting it is not. A cutting's prompt can itself carry a self-regenerating 'perpetual chain protocol' so a multi-increment arc advances chip to chip, HALTing at every owner-fork or operator-attested leg for a fresh owner click — the owner's click stays the spend/attest gate, never self-attested.

**Since ADR-0275 (2026-08-01), a cutting is one of two legal ways a session hands off the next unit, not the only one.** A session that lands a unit may itself continue onto a fresh worktree in the same thread when its own context still has useful room — the continue-or-inert fork on `asset:merge-ceremony` step 9. A cutting is the right call when context does NOT have room (land the residue — the ADRs and arc increments — THEN cut, the situation above, now the ordinary judgment call rather than the exception), when the next unit forks to a different workstream or surface, or whenever the owner wants the explicit approval click as the launch gate regardless of context. This definition does not restate that fork's mechanics or hard ends — read `asset:merge-ceremony`.
provenance:
Named 2026-07-17 at the owner's direction ("maybe we define in the library proper terms for this, i honestly didn't come up with the word chip") to give the owner-approved, outlives-the-session delegation mechanism a durable Library term, disambiguating it from the in-session subagent (`asset:in-session-subagent`) it was being blurred with on the forest-parcels arc. Extended 2026-07-27 by the ADR-0095 graduation pass, from agent-memory `land-decisions-then-cut-a-fresh-session`: the owner's directive that a decision/orienting session lands its ADRs and arcs and then cuts a fresh session to drive, recorded here as a third situation this mechanism is right for — edit-first (`asset:edit-first-curation`) onto the definition that already enumerates when a cutting is the right delegation, rather than a new artifact. Flagged here 2026-07-27 for the graduation-synthesist: the BEHAVIOURAL-FLOOR form of the same directive — making stop-and-hand-off a default every session is held to — was withheld for want of a deciding ADR. ADR-0271 (2026-07-30, amending ADR-0142) supplied one and CLOSED that flag rather than opening a mint: the floor now lives in `asset:merge-ceremony` step 8 and its step 9 closing leg, projected into the `session-orchestrator` landing step and escalation paragraph, and guidance-curator ruled 2026-07-30 that no principle or guardrail is owed — a ceremony step with no deterministic enforcer is process content (ADR-0034 §2), and a fourth statement would breach `asset:reference-dont-restate`.
