Edited 2026-08-01 per ADR-0275 (the owner's live-conversation acceptance of the continue-or-inert fork, amending ADR-0271 D1): the "driving that follows a decision" situation above is no longer the ONLY way a session hands off past its own context limit — a session may now continue in-thread onto a fresh worktree when its context has room. Edit-first onto `whatItIs` (`asset:edit-first-curation`) rather than a new definition: this artifact still names the right mechanism when context does NOT have room, or the owner wants the explicit spend/attest click regardless; the fork itself is NOT restated here (`asset:reference-dont-restate`) — it lives on `asset:merge-ceremony` step 9.
description: The owner-approved delegation mechanism: a fresh, top-level Claude Code session launched via the desktop's `spawn_task` chip the owner clicks — its own context, lifecycle, and SessionStart hooks, surviving the proposing session entirely; the mechanism for long-running drives (arc increments) and anything needing the owner's explicit launch approval.
whatItIsNot: Not an **in-session subagent** (`asset:in-session-subagent`) — the child a running session spawns in-process via its own Agent tool, which starts without owner approval and dies with its parent. Formerly called a "chip" or "chip off" by convention (an agent coined the term; it was never owner-sacred) — that slang still resolves to this concept in older session memories and docs, and the UI action that creates one remains `spawn_task`. "session-cutting" (or plain "cutting") is the durable Library term going forward; this does not rename the `spawn_task` verb itself.

title: Geometry libraries for the grounded-art pipeline
whyThis:
Each rejection is a decision, not an oversight — surveyed 2026-07-18, re-verdicted 2026-07-19 after ADR-0217 and the increment-4 landing.

**A boolean kernel as a present-day dependency — REJECTED (ADR-0217 decision 5).** Zero of the 19 catalogued house defects has a fault a CSG subtraction would have prevented, and the shipped aperture path settles it empirically: an opening is a hole cut by an even-odd compound path, and a wall's thickness reads as a *real* reveal — an outer rim, a pane set back along the facet normal, and two jamb/head quads bridging them (`apertures.ts`; `DEFAULT_REVEAL` is 0.34). Two quads per opening, no kernel, no dependency — and because the reveal is real geometry rather than a painted trapezoid, it takes the same N·L shading as every other surface and cannot drift out of register with the hole it lines.

**PixiJS / Three.js as a scene graph — REJECTED.** ADR-0069 D3 names PixiJS as deferred-behind-the-seam (and Konva, not a game engine, as the lowest-risk target if a swap ever fires); none of its three swap triggers have fired. WebGL forfeits free DOM text and no-GPU rendering, both load-bearing for the hosted IAP members app (ADR-0042). It also would not buy the physics: an affine scene graph gives you transforms, but the part-tree's value is that `on` DERIVES base-z from the parent's top. That is a structural invariant, not a matrix multiply, and would still be hand-written on top.

**Wave Function Collapse — REJECTED, but not for the reason first recorded.** The conclusion stands: we have no ambiguity to resolve. The author declared a windmill, and the job is to VERIFY a specification, not GENERATE a valid one; handing authorial control to an entropy solver fights ADR-0214's hard non-goal (match the reference, never reinterpret). **The original reasoning was wrong and is corrected here** (increment 1, PR #819): it treated constraint propagation and verification as different kinds of thing when they are the same declarative artifact, and it dismissed typed socket compatibility as "a lookup and an equality test" when that is precisely Merrell's model synthesis (2007). Reject WFC on authorial control, not on a technical distinction that does not hold. Its voxel half is moot — ADR-0214 rejected voxel occupancy as the authoring substrate.

**`seedrandom` — REJECTED, already solved and actively harmful to add.** `packages/forest-world/src/rng.ts` (~21 lines) exports `hash`/`rand01`; it is what ADR-0069 D4 mandates and it already drives the lantern marks, vegetation drifts, and stone scatter. A second PRNG risks determinism DIVERGENCE between the new art layer and the existing world — the precise failure that must not happen.
whatItIs:
A survey of the open-source libraries that map onto the pipeline's stations, with a current verdict on each. **Nothing here is adopted today** — `packages/procedural-architecture` is pure and zero-dependency, and stations 1 through 3 shipped that way.

**RETIRED PLAN — vendoring `evanw/csg.js`.** This artifact previously recorded csg.js as ADOPTED: vendor it, own it, and build "aperture-as-subtraction" on it. **ADR-0217 decision 5 retired that plan**, and increment 4 then shipped station 3 and the aperture decision without it — *zero* of the shipped machinery needed a boolean kernel. Both claims that motivated the adoption were wrong: apertures do not need subtraction (CGA does them as facade subdivision and asset instancing; Müller et al. deliberately avoided booleans citing their unreliability), and subtraction was never what killed the silent-occlusion class — a part-tree derives *positions*, not *draw order* (ADR-0217 Context, assumption 1).

**The one prediction that held.** The old entry noted that csg.js's BSP tree was "independently valuable: it is the exact-occlusion solution even if only used for depth-correct polygon splitting." That is exactly what shipped — but written ourselves rather than vendored. `packages/procedural-architecture/src/draw-order.ts` is a BSP that splits interpenetrating polygons on a GL2PS `BEST_ROOT` plane choice and walks back-to-front, with `findDepthConflicts` as its oracle and `viewOf` exposing the (u,v,depth) basis. Read csg.js's BSP for technique if that code ever needs hardening; do not vendor it.

**QUALIFIED BUILD-TIME FALLBACK — Manifold / `manifold-3d`** (the recommended choice for robust CSG numerics; the kernel behind modern OpenSCAD). ADR-0217 decision 5 records it as the fallback *should a future defect actually demand booleans*: Apache-2.0, cross-platform bit-exact determinism proven in CI under `MANIFOLD_PAR=OFF` (the shipped npm default); open defect #1706 emits silent slivers on near-coincident input, so cut through rather than flush. It is **not** a dependency, and no defect has yet demanded it. Its earlier REFERENCE-ONLY filing rested on a browser-safety objection that no longer applies — see Constraints.

**REFERENCE ONLY — `three-bvh-csg`** (actively maintained, >100x faster than BSP-based CSG in complex cases; requires two-manifold watertight input). Read it for algorithmic technique. It sits on `three-mesh-bvh`/three.js — a heavy dependency for a package family that has needed no boolean at all.

**MAYBE LATER, NARROWLY — `paper.js`** (2D vector object model: bezier math, path intersection, compound-path flattening). Does NOT do 3D solid booleans. Its real fit is the ground-shadow pass (a cast shadow is the union of projected silhouettes, exactly a 2D boolean path op) and the vector bake/flatten step. ~250KB with its own scene-graph assumptions, so it earns its place only when the shadow pass is real.
statement: The grounded-art pipeline (ADR-0217) adopts **no boolean-geometry kernel**: apertures are facade subdivision plus even-odd compound paths with real reveal quads, and correct draw order is our own BSP splitter. The libraries below are surveyed so agents reach for the right precedent instead of re-deriving one or reflexively adding a dependency — this is a reading list, not a shopping list.
constraints:
**The four hard constraints this artifact used to impose on kernel adoption were re-scoped by the owner (2026-07-19, increment 1) and no longer apply as written.** ADR-0069 D4's determinism / browser-safety / text-output / dependency-light constraints govern the **live runtime world-geometry layer**; ADR-0214 decision 6 over-inherited them onto "the kernel choice", which is authoring-time tooling. Under ADR-0217 decision 4 parts bake at build time and the runtime composes them — **the runtime performs no geometry** — so a build-time library is not bound by browser-safety or pixel-stability at all. That re-scoping is what voided Manifold's REFERENCE-ONLY filing, which rested entirely on the browser-safety objection.

What actually still binds:

- **Runtime output** must be 2.5D, browser-compatible, and look right. Unchanged, and it is the constraint that matters.
- **Model-level determinism** is retained — for the prove-it-gate only. Pixel-determinism across machines is dropped.
- **Dependency-light** stays a preference with teeth rather than a hard gate: the package family is pure and zero-dependency today, nothing in stations 1 through 3 needed to change that, and adding the first real dependency remains a decision rather than a convenience.

This artifact is a SURVEY, not a permission slip. Adopting anything listed here is a fresh decision; ADR-0217 decision 5 is the standing verdict and it adopts nothing.
description: Which geometry/vector libraries the grounded-art pipeline surveyed, why it adopted NONE of them, and what it built instead (ADR-0217, superseding the ADR-0214 CSG plan).

why: The whole value of a verifier is that a negative verdict MEANS something was checked and found wanting. When the checker's own failure is scored as that negative verdict, an infrastructure artifact is laundered into a finding, and the two become indistinguishable downstream: a consumer that trusts the negative bucket then silently drops true, well-sourced claims or chases phantom regressions — the most dangerous failure for any process whose purpose is to avoid asserting unverified things. The corpus already draws exactly this line inside the spine — `right-kind-red` advances CONFIRM_RED only on the red the test pins and fails the phase CLOSED on a syntax error or unrelated breakage, because an unattributable red is not the unit's red. This principle is that same unverified-vs-negative distinction, lifted out of the spine to every checker an agent reads.
title: A check that could not run is unverified, not refuted
statement: Before you cite or dismiss a verifier's output, establish that the checker actually ran. A verdict produced by a check that could not run — a dead verifier panel, a rate-limited or crashed agent, a hung or errored job, a harness that failed to launch — is UNVERIFIED, not a negative result about the thing under test. Surface it as unknown/unverified and quarantine it; never silently fold it into the refuted / failed / red bucket, where an infrastructure failure becomes indistinguishable from a genuine adverse verdict. The same holds for an instrument that ACTS rather than reports: a batch mutation that matched nothing did not do the work, and its exit code is evidence that the script ran, never that the edit landed — so establish that the instrument DID what you are about to read it as having done, before you read the result in either direction.
howToApply:
Treat the checker's liveness as a precondition you verify BEFORE you read its buckets. Look for the tells that a check did not run: session-limit / rate-limit / crash errors, empty or missing reason fields on a negative, a job that timed out or was killed, a summary whose counts show every panel dead (e.g. verified=N with confirmed=0 killed=0 unverified=N), or the same subject appearing simultaneously confirmed and refuted. Any of these makes the verdict UNVERIFIED — route it to unknown and, if it matters, re-run it; do not cite it in either direction. Prefer harnesses that make the distinction impossible to miss: capture and surface the checker's own error / visible state on any failure — the e2e sibling, where a launch-failing harness threw away the app window's on-screen boot reason, is the same trap wearing a different hat. This lives on the agent's READING: no single storytree mechanism enforces it across external harnesses, and `right-kind-red`'s classifier enforces it only inside the spine's CONFIRM_RED phase — which is exactly why it must be stated and checked by hand at every other verifier boundary. State the principle when you quarantine a bucket, rather than the detection mechanic (`state-the-principle-not-the-mechanics`).

**The hardest case is an instrument YOU authored, because not one of the tells above fires.** A checker can launch cleanly, execute, exit 0 and answer confidently while being structurally incapable of ever returning a positive — no rate-limit error, no crash, no empty reason field, no dead panel. And there the laundering runs in the OPPOSITE direction to the cases above: the instrument's uniform silence is not read as unverified, it is read as a substantive FINDING, because "nothing matched" is precisely what a real adverse result looks like for a scan. A scan whose every answer is "no match" is indistinguishable from a scan that searched hard and found nothing. Measured 2026-08-01 (PR #1060): a coverage probe's regex was authored into a script through a Bash heredoc, which collapsed a doubled backslash in a word-boundary escape down to a single one — so the pattern compiled to a backspace-delimited expression that can never match anything. Every symbol therefore came back uncovered, the probe reported 28 of 28 symbols uncovered, and that number reached an ACCEPTED ADR before a separate mechanical instrument contradicted it; two of its findings were provably wrong. Two further scripts in the same session were corrupted the same way — one silently degraded a word-character class into the literal two-character class `[w$]`, one died loudly on an unterminated regular expression, and only the loud one announced itself. The remedy is not more care with escapes: it is to **pair every scan with a POSITIVE CONTROL — a case that MUST come back with the opposite answer.** A symbol you already know is covered, a plain `blob.includes(knownPresentSymbol)` sitting beside the regex, a fixture planted to be found. Read the control BEFORE you read a single finding: a control that fails to fire condemns the instrument outright, and on a self-authored dead instrument it is the ONLY tell available — it is what caught this one, and without it the probe merely looked thorough. Two corpus neighbours state this same discipline in narrower settings and are worth reading as a family: `asset:capture-the-oracle-for-a-convention-you-dont-own` requires a captured reference set to be DISCRIMINATING ("at least one value must come out differently under the wrong rule, or the capture is decoration"), and `asset:an-assert-oracle-proof-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-proof` enforces exactly this fail-closed for the spine's assert oracle, where a fresh non-zero assertion count IS the control. This principle is their general parent, covering any scan, probe, sweep or inventory an agent writes and then believes. State it as the rule: a uniformly-negative sweep carrying no control is UNVERIFIED, not a finding.

**The same instrument fails open when it APPLIES rather than scans — and there the silence is not even mistaken for a finding, it is mistaken for SUCCESS.** A self-authored batch MUTATION — a scripted `s.replace(old, new)` sweep, a `sed` pass, a rename driven across many sites — has exactly one honest outcome for a pattern that is not present: it changes nothing and says nothing, because a no-op substitution is not an error in any of the languages a session reaches for in the moment. The script exits 0 and prints whatever success line you wrote it to print, and that line is evidence the SCRIPT ran, never evidence the EDIT landed. This is worse than the scanning case in one specific way: a partially-applied refactor reports TOTAL success, so the surviving old code is not quarantined as unknown — it is believed to be gone, and it surfaces one defect at a time, later, under names that do not point back at the script. Measured 2026-08-02, on the wide mechanical removal of the ADR-0257 hook in the PR for ADR-0284: about 8 sites across 6 files driven by `python - <<'PYEOF'` blocks doing `s.replace(old, new)`; three never matched while the script still printed `ok`, and they surfaced separately across later typecheck and test cycles — first as `error TS2304: Cannot find name 'wallHookCommand'`, then a failing assertion in `packages/drive/src/write-authority-rules.test.ts`, then two more at the next run, one of them in `packages/cli/src/write-authority-install.test.ts`. All were then fixed on the FIRST attempt with the exact-match Edit tool, and that is the discriminator rather than a coincidence: that instrument REFUSES on a non-match, so the three sites that vanished silently under the script were impossible to miss under the tool. Take one of two moves, and take it before you read the result. Either use the instrument that FAILS CLOSED on a non-match, or make the script count — capture the applied count at the point of transformation and refuse on any shortfall against the number of sites you intended: `assert applied == expected`, not `print("ok")`. The asserted applied count is the mutation-side analogue of the positive control above, and the completeness information is available in-process the whole time; the failure is never that it could not be known, only that nothing was written down to demand it. Note the discriminator from the scanning case directly above, because the two look alike and their causes are not: there the pattern was CORRUPTED by the path it was authored through and could never match anything, where here the pattern was fine and simply was not present at three sites. The instrument's defect is identical in both — it cannot distinguish "did nothing because there was nothing to do" from "did nothing because it was broken" — which is exactly why the remedy is a count you assert rather than care you take.
