Under ADR-0139 and asset:reference-dont-restate it should cite this artifact instead — an ADR-body edit, which is librarian-curator's seat, not guidance-curator's.  Same pass, one addendum: a cross-reference to the sibling authored beside this edit, `trace-the-defect-to-its-producing-stage-before-building` — deliberately NOT folded in (its remedy is a fourth, ORDER THE WORK, and the corpus consolidation test is whether the remedy is one), but cited here because that artifact discriminates itself from this one and the reverse pointer was missing, which would have left an agent holding a correctly-measured figure and a stubborn defect with no route from this page to the right rule.
description: A check must gate on something that can see the property it fences, and a measurement is evidence only for what it actually measured, over the interval it actually spanned — a correlated observable is never a stand-in for the property itself, and a reading at one end of a run is never evidence about the whole of it.

why: A test earns its keep by putting the code in front of something the code did not decide. When the value comes from a convention nobody in the repo owns - a host's directory naming, a third-party file layout, a wire format, another tool's output shape - the cheapest way to write the test is to derive that value the same way the code does, and the result is an assertion that compares the code to itself: green exactly when both copies are wrong together. Nothing flags it, because the guards the corpus already carries all pass. The deletion check in test-creation-principles is satisfied - delete the derivation and the test does go red - so the sharpest instrument in the corpus certifies a test that cannot fail for the one reason it exists. Measured at commit e947b6d6, linked-session-context-arc increment 8: import-occupancy.ts derived the host transcript directory by replacing only the two path separators and the colon, and import-occupancy.uat.test.ts planted every fixture through a byte-identical private copy of that helper, so neither could see that the host also replaces the dot - C:/code/storytree/.claude/worktrees/<slot> maps to C--code-storytree--claude-worktrees-<slot>, not C--code-storytree-.claude-worktrees-<slot>. Two capabilities reached a signed --real PASS at 00b5f24 with coverage 4/4 and 10/10 package tests green over an import that was a silent no-op for every worktree session - which is every session that arc observes - and it surfaced only when someone ran the real verb and got an empty occupancy section against a transcript holding 183 occupancy-bearing records. The same commit carries a second, independent instance with a different mechanism: exact cwd equality discarded all 183 of those observations because 6 records carried a subdirectory cwd that the real host stamps per request, and the test had composed its cwd fixture straight from production's own assumption. The author generalised both in one contemporaneous line - neither was reachable from either suite, because both tests composed the value they then asserted against.
title: Capture the oracle for a convention you don't own
statement: When code binds to a convention the repo does not own, the test's reference - the fixture it plants, the input it locates by, the value it compares against - must be CAPTURED from the external authority and never composed from the same assumption the code holds, because two copies of one belief agree with each other whatever the world does.
howToApply: Before writing the test, ask who decides the value it will key on: the code, or something outside the repo. If the answer is outside, the reference has to come from a CAPTURE and not a computation. Go to the real thing once, read what it actually produces, and freeze the literal pairs into the test as data - the fix carries REAL_HOST_SLUGS, four hand-copied cwd-to-directory-name pairs taken from a real listing - then assert that the production code reaches a fixture planted at the LITERAL name. The tell that you are about to make this mistake is small and easy to miss: the test file imports, or privately copies, the very function it is meant to pin. Make the captured set DISCRIMINATING - at least one value must come out differently under the wrong rule, or the capture is decoration. That same file's header cited C:/code/storytree mapping to C--code-storytree as verification against a live host, and that example contains no dot, underscore or space, so it holds under the broken rule too and made the defect look checked (asset:example-carries-the-discriminator). Prove the pin the way any red is proved: revert only the production derivation, and watch that exact assertion go red naming itself in the message. Discriminate it from the neighbours, because several look closer than they are. asset:test-creation-principles forbids ASSERTING a value the test composed, and this extends the same discipline one step upstream to the test's REFERENCE - the fixture it plants and the input it locates by - which is exactly why its deletion check passes over this defect. asset:a-mocked-seam-leaves-its-default-implementation-unproven is the nearest sibling, and the pair is worth reading together: both clear that same deletion check, and by different routes - this one sits one step UPSTREAM of what the check governs, the test's REFERENCE rather than its assertion, while that one sits one level ABOVE it, a property of the SUITE rather than of any test in it. The axes are mirror images across the assert: there the reference is sound and the SUBJECT is a fake, the seam's default implementation reached by no test, so the remedy is to ADD a test driving the default against a real substrate; here the subject is already the production code and it is the REFERENCE that is contaminated, so the remedy is to CAPTURE it from the outside authority. why:
The seam pattern earns its keep: splitting a pure decision from its IO makes the decision provable with fixtures and no real substrate. What it hides is that the default implementation — the code the binary actually calls — is then reachable by no test at all, and the suite gets GREENER the more thoroughly the seam is mocked, so nothing ever flags the hole. `packages/cli/src/worktree.ts` splits `classifyWorktree` (pure) from a `WorktreeIo` seam; every one of the 26 pre-existing tests injected a fake, and `defaultStatMtimeMs` — the real implementation — had no test of its own. The defect lived precisely there: it read the per-worktree admin reflog as an activity signal, and `git reflog expire --all` (auto-gc, `gc.auto` default 6700) rewrites every worktree's reflog in one pass, so no worktree could ever age past the 48 h threshold. Measured 2026-07-27, three unrelated worktrees carried an identical reflog stamp while their genuine activity spanned two days; `storytree worktree prune` reported `reap 5, keep 77` with all five targets already lost to git — a run reclaiming zero bytes — while `.claude/worktrees/` grew from 21 GB to roughly 93 GB. The suite stayed green throughout. The cost was never the roughly twenty-line fix; it was that a green gate was read as evidence of a working reaper for weeks while about 72 GB accumulated.

**A CORRECTION, established 2026-08-01 by the mechanical instrument this rule motivated (ADR-0278).** This artifact previously said the blind spot survived its own repair — that the fix re-keyed the signal and left `defaultStatMtimeMs` exercised by nothing today. That is FALSE, and the correction matters because the claim was carried into an owner escalation as live evidence. The fix commit `f4ef42d8` added a NEW sibling file, `packages/cli/src/worktree-idle-signal.test.ts`, which builds real worktree admin layouts in a temp directory, stamps real mtimes, and drives the real `defaultWorktreeIo.statMtimeMs` — that being `defaultStatMtimeMs` — including a named regression test for the reflog-rewrite condition. The claim came from searching ONE file (`worktree.test.ts`) where this rule's own remedy says to search the PACKAGE's test files, and the coverage had landed next door. **The error sharpens the rule rather than weakening it**: it was made by a careful reader applying this very rule, by hand, one file too narrowly — and the mechanical sweep got it right on its first run, which is precisely the argument for an instrument over prose. The shape remains systemic: that sweep located 24 genuinely uncovered seam defaults across the repository. It is simply no longer this instance, and `worktree.ts` now reads as the worked example of the REMEDY rather than of the hole.

The rest of the floor genuinely does not catch it, and it is worth knowing why. `test-creation-principles`' deletion check is applied per test to the behaviour that test pins, and every one of these tests passes it honestly — delete the classifier and they all go red. `test-fixtures-mirror-production-failure-modes` asks whether a fake stages a world more forgiving than production, and `statMtimeMs: () => 0` stages nothing more forgiving; its two-step inversion returns "fine" on every fake in the file and still misses the defect. Both rules govern a test that exists; this governs production code that no test reaches, which is a property of the SUITE rather than of any test in it — so it is invisible to every check applied one test at a time, and invisible by construction to the reader, because the symptom of the hole is a cleaner test file.
title: A mocked seam leaves its default implementation unproven
statement: Injecting an IO seam makes the policy beautifully testable and, in the same move, exempts the seam's DEFAULT implementation from every test that injects a fake — so a green suite over a fully-mocked seam is evidence about the fakes and says nothing about the code that runs in production; introduce or extend a seam only alongside at least one test that exercises the default against a real substrate.
howToApply:
The trigger is the moment you introduce or extend an injected seam — not the moment you write a fixture, which for a default may never come. Ask one question and answer it mechanically: which tests exercise the default? Search the default's SYMBOL name across the package's test files; zero hits is the finding, and a green test file sitting beside the seam is not an answer to it. The remedy is to ADD, never to replace — the mocked tests are sound and stay: add at least one test that drives the default against a real substrate (a temp directory, a throwaway repo, a real spawn) and asserts the behaviour the default alone decides. Where the default carries a platform-conditional or an error-fallback arm, that arm needs its own case or the hole simply nests one level down. When a default genuinely cannot be exercised offline, that is a capability gap to raise, not a hole to leave unnamed.

Four worked instances make the shape concrete, each open for a different reason. All four are now CLOSED (2026-08-01), so read them as the canonical worked examples rather than as a live worklist — and note that closing them is what established the search discipline above, because the first pass got one of them wrong. `builtinRunGit` in `packages/cli/src/branch.ts` had no direct test and sat in the very file `worktree.ts` names as its precedent — so "I followed the house pattern" was never a defence, because the house pattern was copied without its test discipline; `branch-default-io.test.ts` now drives it by OMITTING `deps.runGit` exactly as production does, against a real repository with a real merge commit, so `--abbrev-ref HEAD`, `--fixed-strings --grep`, `--is-ancestor`'s exit code and `status --porcelain` are answered by git rather than by a fixture author's belief about git. `defaultWorktreeCreateIo` and `defaultInstall` in `packages/cli/src/worktree-create.ts` had no coverage at all while a green test file sat next to them covering only the pure `mintWorktreeName` — the most convincing false reassurance available, because the tempting read ("worktree-create is tested") and the true one ("worktree-create's naming policy is tested") are indistinguishable from the test summary; `worktree-create-io-default.test.ts` now runs real git and a real `pnpm install` against them, and the case it pins is the one no fake could state — `primaryRoot()` called from INSIDE a worktree must still answer with the primary, or the ceremony nests `.claude/worktrees/` one level deeper on every hop. `defaultRemoveDir`'s `win32` branch in `worktree.ts` was the thinnest instance and shows the nesting: even a default that acquired a test would leave that arm unexercised wherever CI does not run that platform. It is now exercised by holding the target directory open as a live child process's working directory — a genuine Windows sharing lock, under which every rung of the ladder fails — and the assertion is that `removeDir` THROWS, because `removeOne` turns a throw into `ok:false` and a swallowed error would print "reaped" for a directory still on disk. Off-Windows that arm is unreachable, and it is skipped VISIBLY (the reason in the test name, an empty body) rather than silently.

The fourth instance is the one that corrects the method, and it is worth more than the three that confirmed it. `defaultStatMtimeMs` in `worktree.ts` is where this principle's most expensive defect actually lived: it read the admin `logs/HEAD` reflog as an activity signal, `git gc` rewrites every worktree's reflog in one pass, and so no worktree could ever age past the idle threshold — the reaper silently no-op'd for weeks while `.claude/worktrees/` grew to ~93 GB, under a fully green suite that mocked `statMtimeMs` away in every test. It was ALREADY CLOSED before this pass, by `worktree-idle-signal.test.ts`, and a fresh audit nonetheless reported it as still open — because the audit read the import list of the seam's OWN test file (`worktree.test.ts`, which imports no default) and stopped there, while the coverage lived in a sibling file named for the SIGNAL rather than for the module. That is why the check above is a package-wide search for the default's SYMBOL and not a glance at the neighbouring test file: the same read that under-reports coverage on a sibling-file layout is the read that would have declared this seam uncovered on the day it was fixed. A wrong answer in the safe direction still costs a session, and on a defaults audit the safe direction is not the cheap one.

Discriminate it from the near neighbours, which sit on genuinely different axes. `an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` governs a check keyed to a merely correlated property, and its remedy is to REPLACE the observable; here the tests measure exactly the right property on the wrong SUBJECT — a fake instead of the real implementation — so the remedy is to add, which by that rule's own stated discriminator puts this on the same side as `a-green-positional-oracle-is-necessary-not-sufficient` (that artifact being this shape already solved narrowly for positional oracles and visual defects). `a-live-only-guarantee-is-an-honesty-gap` is the closest in structure — it too says the test fired the helper rather than the enforcement — but it fires only when a guarantee's ONLY proof is expensive, fragile, or billed, and half its remedy is pinning an external dependency contract; nothing here was billed or deferred on cost, and the substrate is the local filesystem. `audit-the-signed-verdict` audits an authored test against a spec's DECLARED contract list, which `storytree coverage` can read; a seam default is not a declared contract, so that check is structurally blind to it. `capture-the-oracle-for-a-convention-you-dont-own` is not a neighbour but the nearest SIBLING, and the pair is worth reading together: both clear `test-creation-principles`' deletion check, and by different routes — that one sits one step UPSTREAM of what the check governs, the test's REFERENCE rather than its assertion, while this one sits one level ABOVE it, a property of the SUITE rather than of any test in it. The axes are mirror images across the assert: there the subject is already the production code and the reference is contaminated, having been derived from the same belief the code holds, so the remedy is to CAPTURE that reference from the external authority; here the reference is sound and the subject is a fake, so the remedy is to ADD. Neither absorbs the other, and a reader who has diagnosed one should check the same file for the other.

why:
ADR-0252 D1 chartered a warn-escalation backstop with two deferral-keyed lines, and the note "Lines keyed to a signal's AGE or to a count of declined arc-closes are NOT built" went into `packages/cli/src/check-verification-decay.ts`. It then survived BYTE-IDENTICAL across the four commits that landed the four chartered instruments — PRs #955, #956, #963 and #965 — a `git show <commit>:<file> | grep -c` across all four printing `1 1 1 1`. Four sessions each read the note, left it verbatim, and landed other work. The fork was settled only once it was promoted out of the source header into a record with a status and an owner (ADR-0256, 2026-07-27), where the answer turned out to be "decided against" rather than "not yet done" — and ADR-0256's own Status prose names the reason in its own words, which is the tell that this belongs stated once for every medium rather than re-learned per file.

The asymmetry is what makes it durable. A "NOT built" comment cannot distinguish unbuilt-but-wanted from decided-against, so the cheap and safe-looking move is always to carry it forward: leaving the note costs nothing visible, while settling it first requires a reader to notice they are holding a fork rather than a chore. Nothing degrades in the meantime — the machinery around the note stays green and passing — so a decision can sit unmade indefinitely with no surface anywhere showing that it is waiting, which is the difference between this and ordinary backlog: a backlog item is at least counted somewhere. It bites hardest when the deferred thing is a backstop, because the gap it leaves is invisible by construction. Here the very mechanism chartered to catch a signal sitting unexamined was itself the signal sitting unexamined, for four increments.
title: A deferral recorded without a status reads as pending work
statement: A deferral — a decision NOT to build, or a fork left open — is settled only when it lives in a container that carries a STATUS and an OWNER; recorded as a note in source, which has neither, it cannot be told apart from unfinished work, so every later reader re-inherits it instead of settling it. Promote it into a status-bearing record rather than carrying it forward.
howToApply:
The trigger fires in both directions: when you are about to WRITE a note in source saying something is not built, deferred, or left for later, and when you READ one. Ask what the medium is able to record — could a reader six months out tell, from this note alone, whether the thing is wanted-but-unbuilt or decided-against, and whose name is on that answer? A source comment has no status field and no owner field, so the honest answer is always no; which means the note is not a record of a decision at all, it is a description with a decision hidden inside it.

The remedy is PROMOTION, not verification, and the direction is worth naming because it inverts most verification work: the note was TRUE, and there is nothing to check it against in the code — its defect is the medium, so re-reading the source settles nothing and a fresh sweep of the surrounding machinery will keep coming back green. Route the promotion by the rules that already exist rather than inventing a home for it. `survival-test-for-adrs` sends a decision that would outlive the unit that prompted it to an ADR (`storytree adr new --pg`, born accepted when the owner directed it in conversation) and everything else to the unit's own guidance, which also carries a status. `owner-fork-bar` decides whether it is an owner's `open-question` at all — the decision being the owner's is the trigger, never your own uncertainty. Then leave a POINTER where the note was rather than a copy of the answer, so the two cannot drift apart (`reference-dont-restate`).

Distinguish it from three neighbours it is easily folded into. `owner-fork-bar` governs WHO decides and what earns an owner's attention; this governs what makes a record legible as SETTLED once someone has decided — both can apply to the same note, and they are not the same call. `accepted-adrs-carry-no-stale-prose` governs a record whose CONTENT went stale and must be made true again; here the content stayed true across four increments and only its container was wrong. `price-the-deferral` is the closest sibling and inverts the remedy: it governs a deferral resting on a quantity nobody measured, where the fix is to spend the probe; this governs a deferral whose statement is already complete and correct, where measuring changes nothing and the fix is to rehouse it. `anchor-implementation-surface` is the same family read the other way — it moves fast-rotting surface data OUT of durable docs into anchored disposable ones, where this moves a settled decision OUT of an un-owned medium into a status-bearing one.
provenance:
Authored 2026-08-01 by guidance-curator from the adjudicated friction `not-built-in-a-source-header-reads-as-pending-work`. KIND — the adjudicator routed GUARDRAIL; OVERRIDDEN to principle on the guidance-curator enforcer test. A guardrail must name a deterministic mechanism that REFUSES (the corpus bar: `an-advisory-list-stays-readable-or-stops-being-advisory` names `evaluateDecayCeiling`; `an-assert-oracle-proof-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-proof` names `verifyOracleExercised`), and none exists here — no gate or lint scans source comments for deferral notes, and none could decide the question mechanically anyway, because the same words are an ordinary factual description in one file and an un-owned fork in another. Telling those apart is precisely the judgement a reader must supply, which is the definition of a principle rather than a guardrail. Same call, same reason, as `unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted` and `an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes`, both routed guardrail and authored principle on this test.

EVIDENCE re-verified this pass: `docs/decisions/0256-deferral-keyed-escalation-lines-are-not-built-a-backstop-s-t.md` is `accepted`, carries `amends: [252]`, and its Status prose states this rule in its own words — that a "not built" living only in a source comment reads as pending work to the next session, which is exactly what happened four times. The note itself is now GONE from `check-verification-decay.ts`, so the evidence is a closed loop (defect, promotion, resolution) rather than an open complaint, and the remedy is demonstrated rather than merely proposed.

EDIT-FIRST applied across all 60 principles, 17 guardrails and 25 patterns live. `owner-fork-bar` was read in full and rejected as an edit target: it is a routing bar for owner ATTENTION whose whole structure is a three-clause test for what earns an `open-question`, and grafting a medium-legibility rule onto it would blur the single axis it exists to hold; an independent corpus-investigator read reached the same adjacent-but-distinct verdict. `survival-test-for-adrs` was the next strongest candidate and was rejected because it fires only once a reader KNOWS they are holding a decision and is choosing where to file it, whereas the entire failure here is four readers who took a fork for a chore — this rule sits upstream of that choice, and folding it in would also blunt a deliberately lean artifact. `accepted-adrs-carry-no-stale-prose` (stale content, not wrong container), `price-the-deferral` (an unmeasured quantity, remedy measure) and `anchor-implementation-surface` (the same family read the other way) are cited with their discriminators in How to apply rather than edited. Nothing in the corpus becomes redundant — this is a pure addition.

RECURRENCE is stated plainly rather than dressed up: four independent re-inheritances at ONE site — four sessions, four PRs, the note byte-identical throughout — not four sites. The generality claim therefore rests not on site count but on the MEDIUM: the absent status and owner fields are properties of source comments as such, not of that file, and the reading side of the rule makes every session that opens a file carrying such a note a current consumer. It clears `friction-justification-bar` because the evidence is mechanical (a `grep -c` across four named commits) rather than recalled, and because it names a concrete future move that changes behaviour — promote, do not re-read. description: A decision not to build, recorded in a medium with no status field and no owner, cannot be told apart from unfinished work, so each later reader re-inherits it instead of settling it; promote it into a record that can be marked decided and owned.

why:
A written enumeration carries no marker separating "not listed because it does not exist" from "not listed because the search did not reach it", so a reader cannot tell an inventory from a sample — and the cheapest move available, believing it, is the one that carries the defect forward. Both recorded saves were reader-side, one increment apart on the same arc, and in neither case was the author careless. The two directions fail differently and both are needed to recognise the shape.

UNDER-INCLUSIVE — a set that is short. ADR-0246's "What was measured" block asserts "Every repo root is derived from the module's own location, and none is a parameter" and enumerates six sites. Verified at the checkout it pins (8afabd5c): nine further runtime sites derive a root by the byte-identical path.resolve(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), '..', …) idiom and are unlisted — among them repoRoot() at packages/drive/src/node-build.ts:141, the single site the ADR's own D5 decision ("the proof leg is inside the arc") depends on, because it feeds storiesDir, createBuildWorktree and the promotion. Consumed as written, increment 1 would have parameterised everything except the site that made the decision true, and a --real build would still only ever have proven storytree's own tree — a plausibly-complete increment quietly deferring the part that mattered. It was found only because a consuming session searched by symbol name rather than by the path shape the list reflects. THE DISCRIMINATOR: the block is not sloppy — it is headed "Grounded in the checkout at 8afabd5c, not assumed", and every site it names is real. Seven of the nine omissions were in fact deliberate exclusions, storytree's own tooling rather than a foreign project's. That is exactly the information the reader could not recover, and exactly why re-deriving is not optional: a list that omits its own search idiom cannot distinguish a considered exclusion from a miss, so a correct list and a short one are indistinguishable on the page.

OVER-INCLUSIVE — a set with a member that was never real. This is a NEAR MISS, already repaired; the lesson survives the repair. The increment that landed the parameter wrote a call-site comment (packages/drive/src/node-build.ts:146-148) describing the seam as symmetric: "the per-call NodeBuildOpts.repoRoot / StoryBuildOpts.repoRoot injections already override this for tests". Only StoryBuildOpts.repoRoot existed; NodeBuildOpts had no such field. The sentence propagated verbatim into the next increment's briefing as settled ground and scoped that increment as pure threading work onto a field that did not exist. Increment 2 caught it only because it verified against main first, and repaired it in commit fefc1ecb. THE DISCRIMINATOR: a comment at the call site, written by the session that had just read the code and newer than any ADR, is the highest-trust description of a seam the next session can find — which is precisely what makes a wrong one expensive, because it is cheaper to believe than to re-derive. And the phantom member is not the costly half: naming a field that does not exist buys a compile error, which is loud and cheap. The cost is that a confident claim of symmetry stops the reader examining the side that DID land — here storyBuild honoured opts.repoRoot for the worktree cut and the promotion while resolving story and capability specs from the module-derived repoRoot(), so a caller aimed at a foreign project built storytree's own stories inside the foreign repo's worktree. The wrong tree proven in the right tree's worktree, concealed by a sentence about a different field.

The two directions are one defect: in neither case was the set ever checked. The repairing commit reached that conclusion on its own, at the moment of repair and without prompting, recording the comment defect as "the ADR-0246 measured-inventory failure mode re-firing on inc 1's own prose".
title: Prose names a set it never checked
statement: A written list or existence claim — an ADR's site inventory, a call-site comment, a briefing's settled-ground line — reads as a CHECKED set, nothing missing and everything named real, when all its author did was write down what one search or one recollection returned: re-derive the set against the code before you consume it as a worklist, and scope it to what you actually checked before you write it.
howToApply:
CONSUMING a set — an ADR's measured block, a call-site comment, a plan's site inventory, a briefing line that says a capability already exists — is where this fires first and where both recorded saves happened. Before the sentence becomes your scope, ask: what one search or one recollection produced this, and would it have reached a member spelled a different way? The text will not say, and that silence IS the answer — a checked set and an unchecked one look identical on the page, so absence of doubt is not evidence. Re-derive against the code, cheaply and in two moves: sweep the set again with at least one idiom the author plainly did not use (a different symbol name, a different path shape, the interface declaration rather than the call site), and confirm that each NAMED member actually exists — grep the field, not the sentence that mentions it. Test the set's EXTENT in every dimension it claims, not just its membership: a list can be short in a dimension it never had, as ADR-0246's block was, measuring where a root is DERIVED and never who could SET one. The re-derivation costs minutes; skipping it costs an increment that lands plausibly complete around the one member that mattered.

AUTHORING a set is the cheaper prevention, and it has now failed twice, so it is the discipline to install rather than the one to rely on. Do not write the universal. Scope the sentence to the search that produced it — "the six sites this path-shape grep found", never "every repo root is derived" — and let the reader inherit the reach along with the result. Name a neighbouring capability as already existing only after reading it in the code; the change you just made is not evidence about the code you did not touch. When you have landed one side of a symmetric pair, describe the side you landed, because the other side is a claim and you have not checked it.

FENCES. `asset:doc-vs-implementation-precedence` is downstream and composes: it is reactive, arming only once a doc-versus-code disagreement is already named, so when your re-derivation surfaces a real discrepancy this rule has done its work and that one takes over to decide correct-the-doc versus extend-the-code. This rule governs the state before any gap is visible. Distinct from `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes`, which asks whether a claim is about the right SUBJECT: in both cases here the subject is already correct — "sites where a repo root is derived" is exactly the right property — and only the set's membership is wrong, so that rule's instruction to state what was measured in the narrowest terms that are true would have made ADR-0246's block honest and would still have handed the consuming session a list that reads as the worklist. Distinct from `asset:price-the-deferral`, where an untested QUANTITY steers a DEFERRAL and the remedy is to measure; here an unchecked SET steers a SCOPE and the remedy is to re-derive. The separating test: there nothing was ever measured, while here the search WAS run and written down honestly, and the defect is only that its limits did not travel with its result. Distinct from `asset:accepted-adrs-carry-no-stale-prose`, which is truth-maintenance for prose that WAS true and BECAME false: neither case here is staleness — the enumeration was already incomplete at the checkout it pins, and the comment named a field that had never existed. Nothing was overtaken; the claim was never established. Distinct from `asset:authoritative-source-beats-derived`, which arbitrates between two KNOWN sources that disagree — here there is one sentence, no second source, and nothing yet visible to arbitrate.
provenance:
Authored 2026-08-01 by guidance-curator on the graduation-synthesist's chaired call, from two foreign-project-forest-arc friction items both routed principle and CONSOLIDATED here rather than authored separately: adr-measured-inventory-reads-as-complete-but-is-a-single-idiom-sweep (an ADR enumeration consumed as the increment worklist) and increment-doc-comment-claims-a-seam-is-symmetric-when-it-landed-on-one-side (a call-site comment naming a field that never existed). The second item's route reason handed the separate-or-single call to this seat explicitly.

WHY ONE ARTIFACT. Both route reasons rest on a past-versus-present axis — A1 "a claim about a PAST search", A2 "a claim about the PRESENT state of the code" — and that axis is not real. It is residue of the two items being described from opposite ends of one sentence's life: A1 from the author's production process, A2 from the reader's consumption. No reader of A1's list experiences it as a claim about a past search; they read it as "these are the sites in the code", which is exactly why they consume it as the worklist. What actually remains is one defect in two directions — A1's set under-inclusive (nine idiom-identical runtime sites unlisted), A2's over-inclusive (a named member that never existed) — and neither set was ever checked. The reader-side/author-side cross-cut is the reason to consolidate, not a seam: one rule, two faces, one remedy, the shape this corpus already consolidates on (price-the-deferral folded two items as "one rule, two mechanisms, one remedy"; an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes folded a design-time and an inference-time face the same way). Two artifacts would each have needed a cross-reference to the other on its only load-bearing line. Independent corroboration the chair did not have, found this pass: the repairing commit fefc1ecb, written at the moment of repair and without prompting, records A2's defect as "the ADR-0246 measured-inventory failure mode re-firing on inc 1's own prose" — the engineer closest to both instances named them as one failure mode in contemporaneous prose.

LEAD FACE. The consuming face leads the statement and the How to apply because both recorded saves were reader-side: A1's missing site was found by a consuming session searching by symbol name rather than path shape, A2's phantom field by a consuming session verifying against main before scoping. The authoring face is the cheaper prevention and has now failed twice, so it is stated as the discipline to install rather than the one to rely on.

EVIDENCE VERIFIED FIRST-HAND, not taken from the route reasons — the rule would be self-refuting authored off an unchecked enumeration. A1: at 8afabd5c the ADR block enumerates six sites, and git grep at that same commit returns nine further runtime sites on the byte-identical idiom (node-build.ts:141, build-unit-status.ts:99, doctor.ts:320, graduate.ts:131, guide.ts:161, web-engine.ts:31, check-dist-drift.ts:107, check-web-grounding.ts:109, web-experience-check.ts:289), so the enumeration was incomplete AT the checkout it pins. MATERIAL REFINEMENT to the chaired framing: the ADR's own in-place correction records that seven of those nine remain derived BY CHOICE, being storytree's own tooling — so "nine sites missing" is true as omissions but would overstate the harm if read as nine sites needing repair; only two did. This is rendered in the Why as strengthening the rule rather than weakening the item, because the reader had no way to tell a considered exclusion from a miss, which is the defect itself. A2: at 47b9d95f the comment reads exactly as quoted and NodeBuildOpts carried no repoRoot field; fefc1ecb added it ("NodeBuildOpts.repoRoot ADDED. It did not exist"). A2 therefore renders as a NEAR MISS throughout — never as pending work. A second refinement carried into the Why: A2's own route reason notes the phantom field would have cost only a compile error, so the expensive half of an over-inclusive set is not the unreal member but the confident symmetry claim that stops the reader examining the side that DID land — here storyBuild's spec resolution.

KIND — principle, not guardrail, on the enforcer test: no deterministic mechanism can refuse a prose enumeration for being short, because a checker would need to already know the true complete set, which is precisely what nobody established. Both source items reach this independently ("no check can judge whether an enumeration written in prose is exhaustive, so a fence cannot reach this one"; "no machine reads a doc comment for truth"). Not a pattern either: this is a truth about what an unchecked written set can and cannot evidence, not an approach with tradeoffs.

NAMING — "boundary" is deliberately absent from the id, title and statement. asset:boundary is a live definition (the ADR-0010 cross-story seam) and reusing the term would make this artifact unfindable by search; "extent", "membership" and "reach" carry the sense instead. WHY EACH NEIGHBOUR IS A CITATION, NOT AN EDIT TARGET. an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes is the load-bearing fence and was read in full first: it has NO reader-side face — its How to apply runs exactly two faces, AUTHORING a check and CITING a measurement, both producer-side — and it sits on the SUBJECT axis where this sits on the EXTENT axis. Its own instruction to state what was measured in the narrowest terms that are true would have made ADR-0246's block honest and would still have left the consuming session holding a list that reads as the worklist; that residue is this artifact's load-bearing content. Its provenance deliberately left both of these items standalone and handed the extent axis to this seat, so this consolidates strictly within its stated scope and does not widen it. doc-vs-implementation-precedence is downstream and reactive (it needs a named gap; this governs the state before one is visible) and composes rather than overlaps. price-the-deferral governs an untested QUANTITY steering a DEFERRAL, remedy measure, where nothing was ever measured; this governs an unchecked SET steering a SCOPE, remedy re-derive, where the search was run and recorded honestly and only its limits failed to travel. accepted-adrs-carry-no-stale-prose is truth-maintenance for prose that was true and became false; neither case here is staleness, since one was already incomplete at the checkout it pins and the other named a field that had never existed. authoritative-source-beats-derived is the closest of the three near-misses surfaced by the live sweep and is cited: it arbitrates between two KNOWN sources that disagree, where here there is one sentence and no second source. Both worked examples are carried with their discriminating rationale per asset:example-carries-the-discriminator — without both directions the rule degenerates into "verify things", which has no discriminatory power. description: An enumeration or existence claim reads as a checked set even when nobody checked it — re-derive its membership against the code before consuming it as a worklist, and scope it to what you actually searched before writing it.

why:
The two trees look like one repository and behave like two, and the tools report success in both directions. That is what makes this cost real work rather than a moment's confusion.

THE WRITE HALF. All of one increment's code — five modified files and four new ones — was written to the primary checkout while the session ran in a worktree. The worktree's own `git status` was CLEAN, and that clean status is the harm rather than the symptom: the write tool returned success, the session's own honesty check reported nothing outstanding, and the edits were meanwhile being applied against a divergent baseline that had removed code the branch's real base still carried. Recovery cost a restore in the wrong tree, a fast-forward of a worktree fifty-five commits behind, and a re-application of every edit against the right files. It is not a one-off: after the item was already routed, a subagent on a later librarian pass stat-touched decision-log files in the primary checkout while its report claimed worktree edits, and two of three edits it reported were never persisted in ANY tree.

THE READ HALF is the same shape one step earlier and cheaper to miss, because it leaves no residue at all. A session read two source files through the primary checkout's path and got a schema two decisions out of date, while the worktree it was actually building in carried the current one; the mismatch surfaced only because the line numbers from a Read and a Grep of the "same" file disagreed. Verified again independently on a later pass, with the primary checkout two merges behind the worktree: the same path returns genuinely different bytes. Nothing is dirty and nothing is inconsistent — the file simply says something else, and the session reasons from it, so the defect enters as a premise rather than as an error.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING. An absolute path is the most portable-looking string an agent can write, and the primary checkout's path is the one written down everywhere — in briefs, in memory files, in the previous session's transcript. It survives being copied across contexts precisely because it never looks environment-specific. And an agent delegating work hands the slip along with the path: a subagent inherits no knowledge of which tree is yours.

WHAT PARTIALLY FENCES IT, AND WHAT DOES NOT. There is a gate-time lobby arm that reds the landing gate on a dirty primary checkout, but it fires long after the write, keys on residue the read half never produces, and fails open on its skip arms. There WAS a fail-closed write-authority DECISION module, deliberately not the wall by its own header, waiting on a pre-tool boundary that would consult it before a byte moved. ADR-0284 retired that boundary on 2026-08-02 without ever registering it — a pre-tool hook fails open on anything but an explicit block, so it could never have been the authority it was specified as — and deleted the module with it. The same decision DE-SCOPED writing into another session's tree as a hazard the system builds against, on zero evidenced instances against thirteen for the shared primary checkout. A static deny list does refuse a write into the PRIMARY checkout, on one machine, for file tools only; it is a path list and knows nothing of trees, claims or branches, so it does not touch this rule's subject. So nothing refuses the act — and, which is the part that changed, nothing is scheduled to. This is a principle carried by the agent's own discipline because that discipline is now the ONLY thing standing here, not because a wall is on its way.
title: The same file in another tree is a different file
statement: A repository that is checked out more than once — the primary checkout plus every worktree slot — carries one path per tree and different bytes behind it, so in a worktree session EVERY path an agent addresses must be resolved against THIS session's own root, and any signal taken from another tree (its file content, its clean status, its green typecheck) is evidence about that tree's branch and never about yours.
howToApply:
ESTABLISH THE ROOT ONCE, FROM THE SESSION. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run in the session's own directory is the answer. A path from a brief, a memory file, or a previous session is a recollection, and the whole failure mode is that a recollected absolute path stays syntactically perfect while pointing at the wrong branch.

CHECK THE PREFIX, AND KNOW WHY THE OBVIOUS CHECK IS WRONG. Worktree slots live UNDER the primary root (`<primary>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`), so "the path starts with the primary checkout's root" is true of every legitimate worktree path and settles nothing. The longest matching root wins; that containment asymmetry is exactly why a textual prefix test is unsafe here.

VERIFY BOTH TREES AFTER A WRITE, NOT ONE. A clean `git status` in your worktree is fully compatible with the edit having landed in the other tree, so it is not confirmation of anything. This is `asset:verify-edit-write-persisted-or-escalate` with the read-back pointed at the right root — and where that principle asks whether the bytes landed, this one asks WHERE, which its read-back does not answer if you read back through the same wrong path you wrote through.

DELEGATE WITH THE ROOT SPELLED OUT. A spawned subagent starts with no knowledge of which tree is yours; give it the absolute worktree root explicitly, and check both trees when it returns. A subagent's report that it edited "the file" is a claim about a path it chose, not about a path you own.

BEFORE A READ INFORMS A DECISION, ASK WHAT COMMIT THAT TREE IS ON. Two checkouts of one repository are not two views of one state, and the read half produces no error to notice. If the content is going to become a premise — a schema you will conform to, an interface you will call, a status you will report — it has to come from your tree.

THE RECOVERY IS NOT THE RULE. Restoring files in the wrong tree, fast-forwarding a behind worktree, re-applying edits, triaging which tree a stray change came from: these are situational recipes that belong in session memory, and they change with the tooling. Only the rule graduates (`asset:state-the-principle-not-the-mechanics`).

DISCRIMINATE IT FROM THE NEIGHBOURS, which are closer in words than in remedy. `asset:authoritative-source-beats-derived` governs two sources KNOWN to disagree and resolves to the one the system enforces; here neither tree is derived from the other, both are enforced, and the failure is that you never noticed there were two — its precedence chain has no arm for this. `asset:work-hierarchy-is-disk-canonical` answers WHICH SURFACE an artifact is authored on, disk versus the live store, and its phrase "in the worktree" is about that boundary, not about which of several trees. `asset:an-inherited-precondition-holds-only-where-and-when-it-was-authored` is the direct sibling and the pair is worth reading together, because the remedies are mirror images: there an ambient value the runner supplied must be REPLACED by one the author chooses, while here a value the author hard-coded from memory must be REPLACED by one derived from the session's own root. Same family, opposite directions — which is why they are two artifacts and not one.
provenance:
Authored 2026-08-01 by guidance-curator. DISCHARGES two friction items, both routed guardrail and both left deliberately unauthored pending one combined brief: `friction-worktree-path-wrong-checkout` (the WRITE half, filed twice — the second occurrence a post-route recurrence during a librarian pass) and `worktree-session-stale-main-checkout-read` (the READ half, whose route reason directs "routing both onto ONE guardrail brief rather than two"). Both halves land here.

GROUPING. This artifact and `asset:an-inherited-precondition-holds-only-where-and-when-it-was-authored` consolidate a five-item family the adjudication explicitly refused to author as five siblings. They are TWO artifacts rather than one on the corpus's split-by-remedy test — the same test `asset:capture-the-oracle-for-a-convention-you-dont-own` and `asset:a-mocked-seam-leaves-its-default-implementation-unproven` used to stay separate, and the same test `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` and `asset:prose-names-a-set-it-never-checked` used to consolidate. The two remedies here point in OPPOSITE directions: the sibling replaces an ambient value the runner supplied with one the author chooses, while this one replaces a value the author carried in from memory with one derived from the session's own root. They also fire on different actors at different moments — a test author writing a precondition, versus any agent addressing any path in any tool call. Folding them would produce a rule whose remedy contradicts itself on half its instances. The two are cross-referenced with that discriminator rather than merged (`asset:example-carries-the-discriminator`).

KIND. The adjudicator routed GUARDRAIL; authored as principle on the guidance-curator enforcer test — a guardrail must name a deterministic mechanism that REFUSES, and nothing refuses this act today. Verified at this seat rather than assumed, and RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-02 with the opposite result: at authoring time `packages/drive/src/write-authority.ts` existed as the pure fail-closed DECISION layer, deliberately not the wall by its own header, exported from the drive barrel and consulted by no caller. It has since been DELETED — ADR-0284 D2 retired the pre-tool boundary that was to consume it rather than finishing it, and deleted the decision core, the hook and the claim receipt together (recoverable at `git show f34b35a7^`). The enforcer test therefore still returns the same answer, more strongly than before: nothing refuses this act. Two live mechanisms exist and neither reaches this rule. The gate-time lobby arm in `packages/cli/src/check-declared.ts` reds a LANDING on a dirty primary checkout — after the write, blind to the read half, and failing open on its skip arms by design. (Its SCOPING was corrected in place on 2026-08-02, after this text was written: the arm used to be reached only inside `if (identity === null)` and then only in the primary checkout, so a session running the gate from its own worktree never asked the lobby question at all; it now runs unconditionally, for every session, against the primary checkout's tree. That widened its reach — but not toward THIS rule's subject. It still observes the PRIMARY CHECKOUT alone, never a sibling worktree, and still only at landing time, so the enforcer test is unchanged by it.) The static `permissions.deny` block installed user-level on one developer machine refuses a file-tool write into the primary checkout before mutation — but it is a list of absolute paths that necessarily permits everything under `.claude/worktrees`, so it cannot distinguish your tree from a sibling's, which is precisely this rule's subject. Same call and same reason as `asset:a-mocked-seam-leaves-its-default-implementation-unproven`, `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` and `asset:unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted`, each routed guardrail and authored principle on this test. The promotion path recorded here has LAPSED and the reader should not wait on it: this said it PROMOTES to a guardrail the day ADR-0255 D2 / ADR-0257 D1's boundary is installed, "a build task already decided". That build task was un-decided by ADR-0284 D1/D2, so the condition can never fire and this artifact is a permanent principle unless someone decides otherwise. Whether the lapse changes the KIND call is guidance-curator's to make, not this seat's — recorded here so it is a live question rather than a silently dead clause. The enforcer test itself is unchanged and still returns principle.

EDIT-FIRST APPLIED AND EXHAUSTED ACROSS ALL FIVE GUIDANCE-BEARING TIERS — principle, guardrail, pattern, PROCESS and DEFINITION, 175 live artifacts, swept by extracting every sentence carrying "worktree", "checkout", "main tree" or "both trees" from every field of every artifact in all five tiers rather than by reading the floor tiers alone. That widened sweep is the point: a floor-tier-only search had twice returned a false "not covered" for a rule the `process` tier already stated. Everything the sweep returned is operational rather than normative — `asset:prove-and-promote-ceremony` and `asset:merge-ceremony` describe the spine's disposable build worktree, `asset:software-factory-line` says work happens in a worktree cut from origin/main, `asset:claim` and `asset:noticeboard` derive session identity from the worktree name, `asset:launch-studio` and `asset:desktop-e2e-conventions` observe a checkout that MOVED under a running process, `asset:affected-pr-test-scope` names the pull-request merge checkout. EVIDENCE. Both halves were verified first-hand by their reporters rather than taken on report — the write half by the split between a clean worktree status and the primary checkout's five modified plus four untracked files, the read half by the primary checkout sitting two merges behind while the same path returned different bytes. The per-flavour git recovery recipes are DELIBERATELY NOT imported here and stay in session memory, at the read half's route-reason direction (`asset:state-the-principle-not-the-mechanics`).

CONSUMERS: every agent that addresses a file path in a worktree session — session-orchestrator, story-author, librarian-curator, guidance-curator, glue-worker, frontend-builder, and any spawned subagent given a path by its caller. NOTE FOR THE WIRING PASS: authored guidance reaches an inner-loop leaf only when it is referenced from that agent's context, rules or antiPatterns list, so this artifact governs nothing until it is wired; the agent tier is seed-canonical and outside this seat's write fence, so the wiring is handed up rather than done here.
description: A repository checked out more than once holds one path per tree and different bytes at each, so in a worktree session an absolute path rooted at another checkout addresses a different branch's copy: a write lands there invisibly to your git status, and a read returns content your branch does not carry. Resolve every path against your own tree's root, and never read another tree's signal as evidence about your branch.

why:
Nothing flags an inherited precondition at authoring time, because the environment agrees with it. The test goes green honestly, the assertion is real, and the belief is recorded as a passing suite. It then inverts the first time the suite runs somewhere else or later — and in both measured faces the session that pays is not the session that wrote it.

THE PLACE FACE. A leaf authoring under a `--real` drive wrote its assumption into the test as a comment: that the suite never runs from a worktree slot, so the identity derivation genuinely resolves to null there. The derivation (`deriveIdentity` in `packages/drive/src/noticeboard.ts`) resolves by running `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in the CHILD's cwd and matching the slot pattern — true in the spine's disposable temp build worktree and true in CI, false in every session worktree. The capability passed `--real` with coverage 5/5 in the spine's tree; run from a session worktree the same suite was 23/24, failing on an assertion that an unresolved identity must create no trace file while a live trace file sat there. The implementation was correct throughout; only the test's precondition was environment-inherited, and spawning the child with a cwd outside any worktree took it to 24/24. The asymmetry that makes this structural rather than unlucky is permanent: every `--real` leaf authors inside the spine's disposable temp worktree while every session observes the result from a worktree slot (ADR-0031).

THE TIME FACE, hit twice independently. A test pinned heartbeat timestamps as absolute ISO literals while the endpoint under test folded them against its own non-injectable `new Date()` and a two-hour stale-reclaim window. It landed green and was red about twenty-six hours later with ZERO changes to the file, expecting the grouped sessions and getting an empty list. The second instance is the same trap reached from the other end: a verify job failed at the same suite, reproduced identically on pristine main, and the root cause was arithmetic — the last green CI run had started twenty minutes before the fixture's heartbeat plus the reclaim window expired. Both were fixed the same way, by deriving the fixtures from a `now` the test establishes itself. A wall-clock fixture is worse than a flake because it is not random: it goes red on EVERY branch simultaneously, at an instant that was computable the day it landed, in a file nobody touched.

WHY THE EXISTING FLOOR DOES NOT CATCH IT. The deletion check in `asset:test-creation-principles` passes honestly — remove the behaviour and both tests do go red. `asset:right-kind-red` sees a genuine attributable assertion failure, which is exactly what it wants. `asset:test-fixtures-mirror-production-failure-modes` asks whether a fixture PRE-INSTALLS a property production lacks, and here nothing was pre-installed at all: the defect is the ABSENCE of any staging, so its two-step inversion returns "fine" and misses it. And on the place face the inner loop cannot drive the repair even once someone knows about it — re-running `--real` re-observes GREEN in the temp worktree and fails closed at CONFIRM_RED, so the one instrument that would normally force the fix is structurally unable to see the red.
title: An inherited precondition holds only where and when it was authored
statement: When a test's outcome depends on an ambient value its RUNNER supplies rather than its AUTHOR chooses — WHERE it runs (cwd, worktree slot, any identity derived from them) or WHEN it runs (the wall clock a fold under test reads) — the test has recorded a precondition that held only at its own place and time of authoring; make that value an explicit input the test itself establishes, or the suite is a fact about the machine and the minute that ran it.
howToApply:
The trigger is the moment a test's outcome depends on a value nobody in the test chose. Ask the two questions, one per face, and answer them by supplying the value rather than by reasoning about whether the current environment happens to agree.

WHERE — does anything in this test, or in the code it drives, resolve a LOCATION? The tells are a bare `process.cwd()`, a child spawned with no `cwd` option, a repository root discovered by walking up from a module's own path, and any identity derived from either. If so, choose the location and pass it: spawn with an explicit `cwd`, hand the root in as a parameter, plant the fixture in a temp directory the test created. The test must be able to name which location it is asserting about; if the honest answer is "wherever this ran", the precondition is inherited. Note that this face bites hardest on exactly the code that reads the environment for a living — identity derivation, root resolution, workspace classification — because such code cannot be exercised without deciding where it runs.

WHEN — does any fixture value flow into a comparison against a clock the test does not control? A date or time literal in a fixture is the tell, and the fold that reads `new Date()` is usually one call away and usually not injectable, which is what makes the literal look harmless. Derive every such fixture from a `now` the test establishes itself — capture `const now = new Date()` and express fixtures as relative offsets — so the fixture and the fold read the same instant no matter when the suite runs. Injecting the clock at the seam is the better fix where a seam exists; a clock-relative fixture is the cheap one that works where it does not.

PROVE YOU FIXED IT RATHER THAN MOVED IT, by changing the ambient value and re-running. Run the suite from a different directory, and from inside a worktree slot if the code reads one. Shift the fixture offsets by a wide margin. A test that still passes is pinning behaviour; one that flips on either change was pinning its environment, and you have simply found the next place it will invert.

A COMMENT ASSERTING THE PRECONDITION IS THE STRONGEST TELL, not a mitigation. In the measured place-face instance the leaf wrote its assumption down in full and the assumption was wrong; writing it down proved only that the author knew the test depended on it. If a precondition is worth a comment it is worth an argument.

DISCRIMINATE IT FROM THE NEIGHBOURS, which are close enough that a reader who has diagnosed one should check the same file for the others. `asset:capture-the-oracle-for-a-convention-you-dont-own` is the nearest sibling and sits one step across: there the test's REFERENCE is composed from the same belief the code holds, so the remedy is to CAPTURE it from the outside authority; here the reference is fine and the PRECONDITION is whatever the runner supplied, so the remedy is to SUPPLY it. `asset:a-mocked-seam-leaves-its-default-implementation-unproven` is a property of the SUITE — production code no test reaches, remedy ADD a test; here every test runs and asserts truthfully, about an environment. `asset:test-fixtures-mirror-production-failure-modes` governs a fixture that STAGES too much and its remedy is to DROP the pre-install; this governs one that stages too little and its remedy is to ADD one — the exact inverse, which is why its inversion check returns fine here. `asset:pin-the-dual-runtime-import-form` is the same proof-here-ships-there asymmetry solved for a dependency's import mechanism, with the remedy in the SPEC rather than the test. `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` governs a check keyed to a merely correlated property; here the assertion observes exactly the right property and it is the INPUT that was never chosen. `asset:the-same-file-in-another-tree-is-a-different-file` is the direct sibling, and the pair is worth reading together because their remedies are mirror images: there a value the author hard-coded from memory must be replaced by one derived from the session's own root, while here a value the runner supplied must be replaced by one the author chooses. No mechanical check can tell an intended environment dependency from an inherited one, so this is asked by hand, at the moment the test is written.

description: A test that takes a precondition from its runtime environment — the directory it happens to run in, the clock at the moment it happens to run — has recorded a fact about that environment rather than pinned a behaviour: the assumption is true where and when it was written and false elsewhere. Establish the ambient value inside the test instead of inheriting it.

why:
A contract required that proof state painted from cache be "distinguishable from freshly-confirmed". The leaf satisfied it with a data attribute on the wrapping element and NO CSS: a grep for the marker across the app's source returned exactly one non-test hit and zero stylesheet hits. The build reported a PASS at coverage 7/7 contracts with the package suite green at 976/976. A person reloading the studio would have seen a stale crown identical to a confirmed one — which is exactly what the governing decision (ADR-0240 D3, "cached paint is never cached truth") forbids. The zero-stylesheet grep is the control that turns "this looks thin" into "no human could see it", so what shipped was a wrong OUTCOME and not merely a suspicious shape.

THE LEAF DID NOT CHEAT, AND THAT IS THE POINT. It satisfied the sentence it was given. Every instrument downstream is likewise honest: the assertion is real, the test carries the contract id verbatim so the coverage check maps it, and the spine observed a genuine red-to-green. Each of them is faithfully answering the question the contract asked. The defect is upstream of all of them, in a predicate that never said who had to be able to tell — so there is no rung of the proof ladder where it could have been caught, and the honesty of every rung is what makes the false green so convincing.

WHY THE UNDERSPECIFICATION RELIABLY RESOLVES THE WRONG WAY. Under turn pressure a leaf takes the cheapest satisfying implementation — the same force `asset:implementer-shortcut-patterns` names and `asset:audit-the-signed-verdict` measured when a signed green dropped its trickiest contract. A machine-readable marker is always cheaper than a rendered difference: it is one attribute, it needs no design decision, and it makes the assertion trivially writable. So an unnamed observer is not a coin flip; it resolves to the machine essentially every time. The predicate is where the fix costs one clause and the only place the choice is still open.

WHY THIS IS AN AUTHORING FENCE AND NOT A GATE. Whether a marker is actually rendered is not decidable in general, and the stylesheet grep that caught this instance is brittle by construction — a class applied conditionally, a styled component, an inline style, or a rule living in a sibling package each defeat it. A check built on it would fail open on the cases that matter, which is worse than no check. That is why the cheapest durable fix here really is a rule about how the contract is written; it is the exception the corpus's prefer-a-code-fence bar allows for, not a way around it.
title: A contract that says "observable" must name its observer
statement: When a contract's success condition is an observability word — observable, visible, distinguishable, apparent, surfaced — it will be satisfied by the cheapest thing capable of observing, so the contract must name WHO has to be able to tell: name a machine and the assertion is the whole contract; name a human and the contract must also say what is RENDERED, or a machine-readable marker satisfies its letter, every instrument downstream agrees, and coverage reports it proven.
howToApply:
AUTHORING A CONTRACT is where this fires, and it is one question. When you write observable, visible, distinguishable, apparent or surfaced, finish the sentence with "to WHOM". If the answer is a machine, say what is asserted and the contract is complete. If the answer is a person, the contract must name the RENDERED difference — the thing that changes on screen — and not the state that becomes true. "Marked provisional" is a state and any attribute satisfies it; "the crown renders desaturated and carries a provisional badge" is something a person can actually fail to see. The test of your own wording: could this sentence be satisfied by a value no one will ever look at? If yes, it names no observer yet.

WHEN THE OBSERVER IS A HUMAN, SPLIT THE CONTRACT RATHER THAN STRETCHING IT. The machine-checkable half — the marker exists and is applied under exactly the right condition — is a genuine contract and should stay one. The look is operator-attested, and the leaf never self-signs it (`asset:agent-never-self-exempts`). Naming the observer at authoring time is what makes that two-stage split visible while it is still cheap, instead of at the owner's walk. Do not resolve a human observer into a machine assertion because the machine one is writable; that is the substitution this rule exists to prevent, and it is also how a merely-missing harness ends up wearing a human glyph (`asset:human-witness-is-a-judgment-gap-not-cost` decides WHICH witness a leg carries once the observer is known — this rule decides who the observer is, and runs first).

READING SUCH A CONTRACT — as the leaf about to implement it, or as the orchestrator auditing a signed green — treat an observability predicate with an unnamed observer as UNDER-SPECIFIED rather than as permission. Resolving it to the cheapest reading is the failure; surfacing it is the move (`asset:escalate-up-when-blocked-or-out-of-scope`), and it costs one question asked before the implementation exists rather than a rework after a signed PASS.

THE CHEAP CONTROL, when you suspect an already-green contract of this: ask what a person would lose if every non-test line mentioning the marker were deleted, and whether any of those lines was a render or style line. Zero render hits means the observer was only ever a machine. Treat it as a control that CONFIRMS a suspicion, never as a sweep that clears one — the same brittleness that disqualifies it as a gate applies to you.

DISCRIMINATE IT FROM THE NEIGHBOURS. `asset:uat-proves-the-goal-not-the-surface` governs the BREADTH of a UAT list, and its human-witness clause covers a surface an agent CANNOT exercise; here the agent exercised the surface, passed, and was right to. `asset:render-and-witness-a-flag-guarded-surface` is the visual leaf's self-QA on a surface already specified, so it fires strictly after this one and cannot repair a predicate that was never written. `asset:a-green-positional-oracle-is-necessary-not-sufficient` is the closest in feel and differs on the remedy: there the oracle is structurally BLIND to a defect class and the fix is to render and look, whereas here the oracle saw exactly what the contract asked and the fix is to reword the contract. `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` governs the KEY a check is built on and its remedy is to REPLACE the observable; this governs the PREDICATE a contract is written in and its remedy is to NAME the observer — a different actor, a different moment, and an artifact that does not exist yet at the moment this one applies. `asset:faked-uat-theatre` is about stubbing collaborators in a walkthrough. `asset:audit-the-signed-verdict` catches a contract with NO test; this one catches a contract whose test is real and whose sentence was weak, which no coverage read can distinguish.

description: An observability predicate with no named observer is satisfied by whatever can observe most cheaply — a DOM attribute, a log line, a field on a payload — while the human-facing requirement it was written for goes unmet and the signed verdict reports it fully covered.

why: The consumable and the alarm live in different places. The payload is what a caller naturally reads and act on; the count of members that died is a sibling field nothing forces it to look at. So the default reading of a partially-failed run is that it succeeded — and it succeeded in a way that looks entirely normal, because an array is not self-describing and eight results have no shape that distinguishes them from ten. That is what makes this worse than a loud failure: the run does not stall, nothing is red, and the missing members are indistinguishable downstream from members that were never dispatched at all. The expensive consequence is not the lost work but what is decided over the narrowed set. A fan-out is usually run precisely because breadth is the point — options to compare, reviews to weigh, lanes to land — so silently dropping members converts a breadth exercise into a narrower one while preserving every appearance of breadth, and the decision taken over the survivors is made in good faith on a set nobody knows is short. The loss is also usually recoverable at the moment it happens and unrecoverable later: dispatch layers commonly let a run be resumed, but only while the caller still knows what was dispatched. Consume without reconciling and that knowledge is gone with the turn.
title: A fan-out result does not report its own completeness
statement: A result set returned by a fan-out — a workflow swarm, a batch of parallel subagents, any dispatch of N units of work — carries no assertion that it holds all N. Members lost to a mid-run failure are dropped from the payload silently, and a short result array is indistinguishable from a complete one by inspection, because nothing in it states what it was supposed to contain. The caller holds the only copy of the dispatched set, and the run's failure count usually sits in a field beside the payload rather than in it, so before consuming a fan-out result: compare returned against dispatched, and read the run's own error or failure count. A shortfall is an incomplete result to resolve, never a smaller complete one.
howToApply: Write down what you dispatched, at dispatch. On return, run two checks before the result is allowed to influence anything: count the members that came back against that number, and read the run's own error or failure count rather than inferring success from the presence of a payload. Either check failing means the result is INCOMPLETE — resolve it before consuming, and prefer resuming the run over re-dispatching from scratch, since the failures are frequently transient and a fresh dispatch pays for the survivors again. If the shortfall cannot be resolved, the honest move is to say what is missing and decide explicitly whether the narrowed set still supports the decision; what is never acceptable is to proceed on the survivors while describing them as the whole. The same reconciliation applies to any dispatch whose result set is assembled by a layer you do not control — parallel subagent batches, batch APIs, multi-lane drives — not only to a named swarm mechanism. Discriminate it from the neighbours. `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` is the closest in spirit but governs semantic SCOPE, an instrument that measures a property adjacent to the one you care about; here the instrument is exactly right about what it reports — these results returned — and the defect is that the returned set is being read as the dispatched set, a COMPLETENESS axis whose missing datum is held by the caller, not by the instrument. `asset:prose-names-a-set-it-never-checked` is the authored-prose member of the same completeness family: there a human wrote down what one search returned and the remedy is to re-derive the set against the code, where here the true set was never in doubt and the remedy is a comparison needing no new search. `asset:unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted` governs how to score a checker that could not run; this governs a run that partly ran. `asset:an-awaited-notification-is-not-a-turn-ending-state` is the sibling failure at the other end of the same seam — there the caller holds nothing and the turn never ends, here the caller holds something and proceeds.
