Nothing in the corpus becomes redundant; this is a pure addition. Consumers: any agent that dispatches work in parallel and consumes the aggregate — session-orchestrator, graduation-synthesist, planner, frontend-builder.
description: A result set returned by a fan-out carries no assertion that it holds every unit dispatched: members lost to a mid-run failure are dropped silently and the short result reads exactly like a complete one. Reconcile returned against dispatched and read the run's own failure count before consuming it.

why: Ending a turn in a wait state is the one failure an agent cannot recover from by itself, because it has no further turn in which to notice it was wrong. Every other bad move leaves the agent running and able to correct; this one converts a live lane into a silent stall that only an outside party can end — and that party has to notice it first, which is exactly what nobody is watching for. The three ways the signal fails to arrive present identically as nothing has arrived yet, so no amount of waiting discriminates them and waiting longer is never the answer to any of them. The cost is paid twice. The stalled lane costs its own wall-clock plus a manual nudge to restart it, per lane. The misrouted-report case additionally costs the RECEIVING session, which becomes an involuntary router for a conversation it is not part of: it must notice that a report is not its own, work out whose it was, and relay it down before the stall ends. That second cost compounds with spawn depth — the deeper the tree, the more reports land where nobody asked for them and the less the asker can see — which is what makes the shape structural to spawn-and-await rather than a quirk of any one role. What settles it is a controlled comparison rather than a tally: in one increment the lanes whose briefs told them to poll in-turn did not stall while the lanes without that line each did, with the brief as the only varied factor. The instruction is therefore the entire fix — nothing else in the environment prevents this, and nothing downstream detects it.
title: An awaited notification is never a turn-ending state
statement: An agent that dispatches asynchronous work — a background subagent, a background shell task, a sub-spawned helper — never ends its turn awaiting that work's completion notification. The delivery seam belongs to the harness, not to the agent: the report can be routed to a session that did not commission it, the child can already be dead, or the work can simply outlast the turn — three states that produce the same view from inside the wait and none of which patience resolves. Poll the dispatched work's own state in-turn instead; when the answer is not available within the turn, complete on your own judgment THIS turn and name in the return what was dispatched, what could not be learned, and what was decided without it. The turn is the only unit of agency the agent controls, and spawning asynchronous work does not extend it.
howToApply: Before returning, ask one question: does anything in this return depend on a result I dispatched and have not read? If it does, POLL it now — read the dispatched work's own state and its output directly rather than waiting to be told about it. Treat the three unanswered states identically, because you cannot tell them apart and the response is the same for all three: complete the work on your own judgment THIS turn, and state plainly in the return what you dispatched, what you could not learn, and what you decided without it. A caller can act on that; a caller cannot act on silence. Never let awaiting the notification be the last line of a turn, and never re-spawn a helper to replace one whose result never reached you — that doubles the tree without touching the seam. This is the fence that comes with the affordance (`asset:pair-the-fence-with-the-affordance`): dispatching asynchronous work is legitimate and often right, and this is what it costs — you may dispatch, but you may not borrow the caller's patience to cover the gap. The receiving half of the same seam is a duty, not a courtesy: when a completion report arrives for work you did not commission, it belongs to the agent that did — relay it down rather than consuming it as your own or dropping it, and when you relay, say explicitly that the recipient should act on its own judgment this turn, because handing a parked agent a result without that instruction does not reliably end the park. Discriminate it from the neighbours. `asset:escalate-up-when-blocked-or-out-of-scope` is the opposite failure on the same axis: that rule governs an ACTIVE, addressed handoff up the ladder when you cannot proceed, where this governs a PASSIVE wait addressed to nobody — an agent that follows this rule and still cannot proceed escalates, it does not park. `asset:unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted` is the sibling one step later, governing how to SCORE the output of a checker that could not run rather than whether to end a turn waiting for it. `asset:a-fan-out-result-does-not-report-its-own-completeness` is the sibling at the other end of the same seam: there the caller holds something incomplete and proceeds, here the caller holds nothing and stops. `asset:delegate-exploration-to-digest-subagents` governs where exploration runs and is silent on what the delegating agent does after dispatch. `asset:in-session-subagent` states the delivery mechanism — that notifications can leak upward past the agent that asked — but prescribes no behaviour; this is the behaviour.
provenance: Authored 2026-08-01 by guidance-curator from three friction items routed to the behavioural floor and never authored, CONSOLIDATED here as one rule. It discharges: `friction-background-subagent-reports-route-to-main` (reinforced), `friction-builder-agents-stall-awaiting-background-gate`, and `friction-subagent-parks-awaiting-dead-subspawn`. Consolidated rather than authored three times because the three differ ONLY in what is being awaited — a background subagent's report, a background shell task, a sub-spawned helper — and are identical in harm (a turn ends in a wait nothing will end), in detection (nothing arrived, and which of the three you are in is unknowable from inside) and in remedy (poll in-turn, finish on your own judgment). The corpus precedent is to consolidate when the remedy is one: `asset:price-the-deferral` folded two routed items as one rule with two mechanisms and one remedy, and `asset:an-observable-is-evidence-only-for-what-it-observes` folded two faces on the same ground. Three artifacts differing only by flavour would be the per-flavour recipe `asset:state-the-principle-not-the-mechanics` keeps out of the corpus. The fourth item the drain grouped with these, `friction-workflow-swarm-dies-on-spend-limit`, was deliberately NOT folded in and is authored separately as `asset:a-fan-out-result-does-not-report-its-own-completeness` — its harm is a result that reads as complete and its remedy is arithmetic, where this one's harm is a turn that never ends and its remedy is temporal; one artifact spanning both could only say that delegated results need care, which fails the discriminatory bar. EVIDENCE LEDGER (kept here per `asset:reference-dont-restate`, out of the rule text). Misrouted delivery: every one of six background lanes on a forest-parcels increment-1 session had its completion report land at the main session rather than the coordinator, which hand-forwarded all six; the same shape recurred 2026-08-01 in a friction-drain session where a guidance-curator's own commissioned corpus-investigator reported to the main orchestrator instead, leaving the parent waiting on the load-bearing verdict its authoring depended on and making the orchestrator an involuntary router for a conversation it was not part of. Controlled comparison: on a noticeboard-claim-ledger increment-6 sweep, the lanes briefed to run the gate in the foreground and poll in-turn did not stall, while the lanes without that line each stopped awaiting a gate notification and each needed a manual nudge — the brief was the only varied factor, which is what clears `asset:friction-justification-bar`. Dead child: a guidance-curator subagent ended its turn awaiting an investigator that its own task notification showed was not running; a one-line nudge to act on its own judgment completed the write, the persistence verification and the full return in a single resumed turn. A fourth occurrence is recorded in agent-memory on the graduation-synthesist seat, so the shape spans at least three distinct roles. KIND — principle, not the routed guardrail, on the enforcer test this seat applies: a guardrail must name a deterministic mechanism or it is not one, and every guardrail in this corpus names real code or CI (`asset:two-surfaces-required-to-agree-are-gated` names its conformance check; `asset:escalate-up-when-blocked-or-out-of-scope` names the unconditional escape-hatch render plus the agent-file gate). Nothing detects an agent ending a turn in a wait state, and the delivery seam is the harness's — all three route reasons say so in their own words and each concludes that the fence IS the fix. The one enforcer shape that could otherwise be claimed, structural PRESENCE in every rendered agent file, is not claimable today: wiring this rule into the agent tier is a separate seed-canonical change (ADR-0055) outside this authoring pass, and asserting it now would be false, which is precisely what the enforcer test prevents. The same call is stated in `asset:unrun-check-is-unverified-not-refuted`, which records that no single mechanism enforces it and that this is exactly why it must be checked by hand. Recorded for whoever wires the floor: this rule reaches a spawned agent only once it is referenced from that agent's rules or antiPatterns list.
